Conversation — client and staff (PV4-03, 2026-10-12) — `platform-nest/src/core/{portal-conversation,conversation}.controller.ts`, `conversation-core.ts`; predicates in `portal-visibility.ts` — **STATUS: BACKEND BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `conversation.controller.test.ts` runs against real Postgres + Cerbos on the Linux CI gate; portal UI BUILT by PV4-08, PROTOTYPED (vitest, a demo-mode Playwright spec and a stub-BFF Playwright spec; not run against a live platform-nest); staff UI BUILT by PV4-09 (§29f), PROTOTYPED (vitest and demo-mode Playwright specs))**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-12-pv4-conversation-tickets.md` (PV4-03). Rulings PV-D22 (a thread per project plus ONE client-wide "general" thread per client), PV-D23 (agents draft, staff send), PV-D24 (every contact who can see a project takes part, viewers included). Tables: migration `202610122330_pv4_conversation_data_model.sql`. Cerbos: `resource_conversation.yaml` (staff kind) and `resource_portal.yaml` `converse` (client).

**Rules that hold on every route below**
- **Portal isolation** (§16 "Isolation model"): `portal` `read` for GETs, `portal` `converse` for writes, then `resolvePortalScope`, then the thread predicate `conversationThreadInPortalScope` (client AND project). A message and its attachments are admitted **through their thread**. Outside scope = **404**, never 403 (no existence oracle). A revoked or invited contact is refused by the kernel (403 "not a portal client").
- **PV4-Q1 (default in force):** the client-wide thread (`project_id IS NULL`) is visible **only to client-wide contacts**. Unlike contracts and change requests, a project-scoped contact is NOT admitted to project-less rows here.
- **PV-D24:** no route calls `requireSigner`; a `viewer` contact opens threads and posts.
- **Server-derived fields:** `author_id` (the principal), `author_side` (`client` on portal routes, `staff` on staff routes), `client_id` (from the admitted project/thread, or the caller's own client) and `tenant_id` (the route) never come from the body. Body fields `authorId`, `authorSide`, `author_side`, `clientId` (except to choose among the caller's OWN clients), `status`, `tenantId` are ignored.
- **Plain text only** (design decision 7): `body` 1..10,000 characters (also a DB CHECK), PAN/national-id scrubbed like change requests, never interpreted as HTML or Markdown. **The UI must render it as text** (links may be made clickable on render).
- **Messages are permanent (PV-D34, owner ruling 2026-10-13):** no edit, no retract; a correction is a new message. A message is final from the moment it is posted. There is no `PATCH` or `DELETE` on a message on either side: those routes do not exist and answer **404** (no such route), not 403. `editableUntil`, `edited`, `editedAt` and `retracted` are gone from every message payload, and `body` is always a string. The database enforces it too: a trigger on `conversation_messages` (migration `202610132145_pv4_conversation_messages_permanent.sql`) refuses every `UPDATE` and every `DELETE` with SQLSTATE `PD034` (`conversation messages are permanent (PV-D34)`), whoever issues it; the only way through is an operator's `SET LOCAL app.conversation_purge = 'on'` on a `DELETE` (erasure or test teardown; no application code may set it). The columns `edited_at` and `retracted_at` stay, unused. A message retracted under the retired 15-minute window (PV4-Q2, now ruled) stays hidden from both sides and its files stay withdrawn. Both composers say: "Messages can't be edited or removed once sent. Post a correction instead."
- **Closed thread:** posting (either side) is **409** until staff reopen it.
- **Drafts are staff-only by table** (`conversation_drafts`): no portal route or portal helper names the table (static guard `conversation-portal-guard.test.ts`).
- **"Client sees this"** (plan trap 9): every staff thread and message row carries `clientVisible: true` computed in SQL from `staffConversationThreadClientVisible` / `staffConversationMessageClientVisible`; every draft row carries `clientVisible: false` from `staffConversationDraftClientVisible`. The UI shows the marker from this field, never from its own logic.
- **Attachments:** `attachments?: [{filename, contentType, content /* base64 */}]`, **at most 5 per message and at most 10 MB in total per message** (lead decision; the ticket's 5 x 10 MB was reduced). Text types are scrubbed like payment proofs. Stored as `files` rows with `target_entity_type = 'conversation'` and `target_entity_id` = the MESSAGE id. **Request-body limit (PV4-03b, per route, never app-wide):** the app's Fastify default stays 1 MiB, but the four routes that take attachments (portal `POST /api/:t/portal/conversation` and `.../:threadId/messages`, staff `POST /api/:t/conversation` and `.../:threadId/messages`) and the payment-proof route (§16b) each get `bodyLimit = ceil(cap × 4/3) + 64 KiB` = **14,046,550 bytes** (cap = the handler's own 10 MiB; table and derivation in `src/core/upload-body-limits.ts`, installed in `buildApp()` before the routes register, and `buildApp()` throws at boot if any table entry does not match exactly one registered route). So a message with attachments totalling up to the 10 MB cap is accepted, and one byte over is refused by the handler with `400 {error: "attachments too large (max 10 MB per message in total)"}`; only a body past ~14 MB gets the body-limit `413 {error: "payload too large", code: "payload_too_large"}` (Fastify's FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE). The draft routes (`.../drafts`) carry no files and keep the 1 MiB default. The edge proxy must also admit a ~14 MB body on these paths (nginx `client_max_body_size`) or the browser sees the proxy's 413 first.
- **Downloads:** portal `GET /api/:t/portal/files/:fileId` (§16b) admits `conversation` files through message -> thread -> `conversationThreadInPortalScope`, (a message retracted under the retired 15-minute window keeps its files withdrawn). Staff use `GET /api/:t/files/:fileId/content`, which authorizes `{kind: 'conversation'}` `read` with no change there.
- **Unread counts:** messages on the thread written by the **other side** newer than the caller's `conversation_reads.last_read_at`. Opening a thread (GET detail) marks it read; posting marks it read for the poster.
- **Events** (transactional outbox, entity type `conversation`; every payload carries `clientId`, `threadId` and ids only, never text): `conversation.thread.opened`, `conversation.message.posted`, `conversation.thread.updated`. (`conversation.message.edited` is retired by PV-D34: nothing emits it and it is no longer mapped to a portal topic.) Drafts emit `conversation.draft.created` on the `conversation_draft` stream, which is NOT mapped to any portal topic.
- **Live updates:** portal topic **`conversation`** (§16d), narrowed to the thread's client. Staff screens poll (20 s while a thread is open; design decision 6); there is no staff live channel.

### 29a. Portal — `src/core/portal-conversation.controller.ts`

| Status | Method | Path | Cerbos | Payload / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/portal/conversation[?projectId]` | `portal` · `read` | `{threads: PortalThread[], canUseGeneral: boolean, generalClientIds: string[]}`. `PortalThread` = `{id, clientId, clientName, projectId, projectName, general, subject, status:'open'\|'closed', createdSide, lastMessageAt, createdAt, unreadCount}`, newest activity first, max 200. `canUseGeneral` = the caller is client-wide on at least one client (a summary); **`generalClientIds` = the clients whose general thread they may read, post to and lazily create (those they reach client-wide), and the UI offers General per client from it (PV4-13)**. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/portal/conversation/:threadId` | `portal` · `read` | `{thread: PortalThread (no unreadCount), messages: Message[]}`, oldest first (newest 500). Marks the thread read. `Message` = `{id, threadId, authorId, authorName, authorSide:'client'\|'staff', body: string, createdAt, mine, attachments:[{id, filename, contentType, byteSize}]}` (PV-D34: no `retracted`, `edited`, `editedAt` or `editableUntil`). No `draftedBy` on the portal: the sender shown is the named person (design decision 4). |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/portal/conversation` | `portal` · `converse` | `{projectId?, clientId?, subject?, body, attachments?}` -> **201** `{threadId, messageId, created, attachmentIds}`. With `projectId` (one of the caller's projects; otherwise 404): a NEW thread on that project. Without: the client's ONE general thread, created on first post (race-safe: concurrent first posts land in one thread via the partial unique `ux_conv_threads_client_wide`); a project-scoped contact gets 404; a client-wide contact of several clients names one with `clientId` (validated against their scope, else 400). |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/portal/conversation/:threadId/messages` | `portal` · `converse` | `{body, attachments?}` -> **201** `{id, threadId, createdAt, attachmentIds}`. 404 outside scope, 409 closed. |

Each filter also accepts the literal `all` = no filter (PV4-07: mcp-hub fills every path token, so the `conversation.listThreads` tool sends `all` for a filter it was not given). `mine=true` (DW-5g) keeps only threads where the caller is a staff recipient by the SAME rule the notices use (`staffRecipientIdsSql` in `conversation-notify.ts`: an author of a live staff message in the thread, the project's owner for a project thread, or the client's account manager); `mine=false` is the complement, `all` or absent is no filter; it narrows an already-authorized list and is not an authorization rule. |

Marks read. `drafts` = the PENDING drafts (same shape as `GET .../drafts`; staff-only, `clientVisible: false`), added by PV4-07 so one call answers "what was said, and what is waiting to be sent". |

Default pending only. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/conversation` | `conversation` · `post` | `{clientId, projectId?, subject?, body, attachments?}` -> **201** `{threadId, messageId, created, attachmentIds}`. With `projectId`: a new thread (the project must belong to `clientId`, else 400). Without: the client's general thread (lazy, race-safe). The internal client is refused (400). |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/conversation/:threadId/messages` | `conversation` · `post` | `{body, attachments?}` -> **201** `{id, threadId, createdAt, attachmentIds, clientVisible: true}`. **Refused to `bot`/`automation` principals by Cerbos** (403 `{error, reason: "agents_draft_staff_send"}`; `error` names `conversation.draftReply` and ends with the Cerbos reason `cerbos denied post on conversation`; PV-D23, PV4-07). 409 closed. |

Writes a `drafted_reply` activity naming the caller (not on a replay). ONE transaction: the message is authored by the SENDER (`author_id` = the caller, `author_side = 'staff'`) with `drafted_by` = the draft's author; the draft becomes `sent` with `sent_message_id`, `decided_by`, `decided_at`. ### 29d. Notifications, both ways (PV4-06, 2026-10-13) — `src/core/conversation-notify.ts`, `src/mail/intake.ts` — **STATUS: BACKEND BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `conversation-notify.test.ts` runs against real Postgres + Cerbos on the Linux CI gate; portal UI BUILT by PV4-08, PROTOTYPED (vitest, a demo-mode Playwright spec and a stub-BFF Playwright spec; not run against a live platform-nest); staff UI is PV4-09)**

No new route. Every write route in §29a/§29b calls into `conversation-notify.ts` **after its transaction commits**. The call is best-effort and never throws: a failure in the thread lookup, the recipient queries, or any one `notify()` is logged (`[conversation-notify]`, `[client-notify]`) and swallowed, so a notification problem can never fail or roll back the message. Edit, retract, close and reopen notify nobody.

| Fires on | Recipients | Type | Title | `href` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a CLIENT posts (portal `POST /portal/conversation`, `.../:threadId/messages`) | staff recipients (below) | `conversation.message.client` | `New message from <client name>` | `/clients/<clientId>/work/conversation/<threadId>` |
| STAFF post (`POST /conversation`, `.../:threadId/messages`) or a draft is SENT (`POST .../drafts/:id/send`) | every active contact in the thread's scope | `conversation.message.staff` | `You have a new message` | `/portal/conversation/<threadId>` |
| a draft is CREATED (`POST .../:threadId/drafts`; a replay of the same `idempotencyKey` does not notify again) | staff recipients | `conversation.draft.created` | `A draft reply is waiting` | `/clients/<clientId>/work/conversation/<threadId>` |

Payload (stored in `notifications.payload`, plus `actorId`): `{title, href, entityType: 'conversation', entityId: <threadId>}`. **It never contains the message text** (asserted on the stored row); the text stays in the thread. A staff href is a page PV4-09 builds; the portal href `/portal/conversation/<threadId>` is the thread page PV4-08 built (`platform-ui/src/app/(portal)/portal/conversation/[threadId]/page.tsx`, in the Projects area's Conversation sub-tab); the deep-link ledger (`portal-links.guard.test.ts` `AWAITING_PAGE`) is empty again.

**Staff recipients** (design decision 5; there is no project-team table): the thread's staff participants (distinct `author_id` of its `author_side = 'staff'` messages) ∪ the project's owner (`projects.owner_id`, project threads only) ∪ the client's account manager (`clients.owner_user_id`); deduplicated, the **actor excluded**, users that are not `active` (or soft-deleted) dropped. An **empty set notifies nobody and is not an error**: the thread still shows as awaiting reply (§16b `needsUs`), so a missed notice never hides it.

**Contact recipients**: `resolveClientRecipients(kind: 'general')` with the thread's own `project_id`: active contacts that are client-wide or scoped to **that** project, never a contact scoped to another project. For a client-wide thread (`project_id` NULL) that is **client-wide contacts only** (PV4-Q1: a project-scoped contact cannot open that thread, so they are not told about it). Signers, admins and viewers alike (PV-D24); the actor is excluded.

**Mail to client contacts** (`conversation.message.staff` is the third type on the mail allow-list, with its own template `conversation.message.staff`): the mail has no message text, a fixed subject `You have a new message`, no reply token, and its **only link is the plain deep link** (`<MAIL_LINK_BASE_URL>/portal/conversation/<threadId>`), never a token or a session.
- **Throttle: at most one mail per contact per thread until that contact has read the thread.** A mail is skipped when `mail_log` already holds a `conversation.message.staff` row for this (contact, thread) newer than the contact's `conversation_reads.last_read_at`, or any such row at all when the contact has no read marker. Every status counts (queued, sent, suppressed, failed). The thread is recorded in the mail row's `payload.threadId`.
- **Flag, default OFF: `CONVERSATION_CLIENT_MAIL_ENABLED=1`** (`config.mail.conversationClientMailEnabled`; only the exact string `1` enables it). It is separate from the master `MAIL_ENABLED` because this is the one mail type that reaches people outside the company. Off means `mailIntake` returns before any lookup: **no `mail_log` row and no enqueue**; the in-app notification above still lands. Turn it on only once a real client-delivery sender exists (the board's "Before real clients use the portal"). The compose file does not pass the variable through yet, so it cannot be turned on by accident.

**Counts (additive)**
- `GET /api/:t/portal/overview` (§16a) gains **`conversationUnread: number`**: the number of threads in the caller's scope with at least one unread message from STAFF. It is the same predicate (`conversationThreadInPortalScope`) and the same unread rule (`unreadCountSql`) as the per-thread `unreadCount` on `GET /portal/conversation`, so it equals the number of rows in that list with `unreadCount > 0`. A project-scoped contact does not count the client-wide thread. The portal nav's Projects badge adds it to the open gates (PV4-08).
- `GET /api/:t/clients/:clientId/overview` (§16b) gains **`conversationsAwaitingReply: number`**, and `needsUs[]` gains items **`{kind: 'conversation', id: <threadId>, label: 'A client message is waiting for our reply', context: <subject | project name | 'General conversation'>, href: '/clients/<clientId>/work/conversation/<threadId>', since: <time of the last client message>, clientVisible}`**. A thread is awaiting when it is open and its last non-retracted message is the client's (`awaitingReplySql`, the same rule as the staff list's `awaitingReply`). The UI's `needsUs` item `kind` union grows by `'conversation'` (PV4-09).

**DW-5g (client conversations waiting for MY reply in Needs you).** The staff list gains the `mine` filter above; with `awaitingReply=true&status=open` it answers "client threads waiting for my reply", and the department-workspace Overview's Needs you reads exactly that per company (`getMyWorkQueue`, queue item type `conversation`, link `/clients/<clientId>/work/conversation/<threadId>`). The MCP tool `conversation.listThreads` is unchanged: an agent principal has no "mine" (the tool sends no `mine`, so it is unfiltered). A failed read marks the company's `partialSources` with `conversations`.

### 29e. MCP tools for Conversation and minutes (PV4-07, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/core-tools.ts`, `agent-refusal.ts`, `approval-executables.ts`

Agent surface for owner ruling **PV-D23: agents draft, staff send.** Each tool fronts exactly one endpoint above and carries that endpoint's Cerbos authorization. Core tools: advertised to every tenant, `minAssurance: verified`. Nothing is on the n8n `AUTOMATION_ALLOWLIST`; no workflow writes to a conversation in v1.

| Tool | Endpoint | Impact | Barred from D14? | Agent may call? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `conversation.listThreads` (`clientId`, `projectId`, `status`, `awaitingReply`, each defaulting to `all`) | GET `/api/:t/conversation?...` | read | n/a | yes |
| `conversation.getThread` (messages + pending drafts) | GET `/api/:t/conversation/:threadId` | read | n/a | yes |
| `conversation.draftReply` (`threadId`, `body`, **`idempotencyKey` required**) | POST `/api/:t/conversation/:threadId/drafts` | low | no | **yes: the agent's main write** |
| `conversation.closeThread`, `conversation.reopenThread` | PATCH `/api/:t/conversation/:threadId` (`status` fixed by the tool) | low | no | no (`manage`) |
| `conversation.post` (reply on `threadId`) | POST `/api/:t/conversation/:threadId/messages` | medium | **yes** | no |
| `conversation.open` (`clientId`, optional `projectId`/`subject`) | POST `/api/:t/conversation` | medium | **yes** | no |
| `conversation.sendDraft` (`draftId`) | POST `/api/:t/conversation/drafts/:draftId/send` | medium | **yes** | no |
| `meetings.getMinutes` | GET `/api/:t/meetings/:id/minutes` | read | n/a | yes |
| `meetings.saveMinutes` (an agent may draft minutes from the transcript) | PUT `/api/:t/meetings/:id/minutes` | low | no | **yes** |
| `meetings.shareMinutes` | POST `/api/:t/meetings/:id/minutes/share` | medium | **yes** | no |

- **"post" is two tools** because a tool def maps to exactly one path: `conversation.post` replies on a thread, `conversation.open` starts one.
- **Barred** = `registerBarredExecutable` (`CONVERSATION_BARRED_TOOLS` in `approval-executables.ts`), reason `agents_draft_staff_send`, note "PV-D23: agents draft, staff send — nothing an agent writes reaches a client until a staff member approves it". They are medium, so an unattended call suspends for approval; approving it can never execute it (the executor fails closed with `not_executable`, and `registerExecutableApproval` throws for the name). A **person** using an MCP client under their own identity calls them all as themselves: the sent message's author is that person, and `drafted_by` is the agent whose draft it was.
- **Typed refusals (criterion 5).** An agent (`users.kind` `bot` or `automation`) reaching a denied route gets `403 {error, reason}`, never a bare 403:
  - `reason: "agents_draft_staff_send"` on `conversation.post`, `.open`, `.sendDraft` and `meetings.shareMinutes`; `error` names `conversation.draftReply` (or `meetings.saveMinutes` for the minutes).
  - `reason: "agents_cannot_manage_conversation"` on `conversation.closeThread` / `.reopenThread` (`PATCH :threadId`, Cerbos `manage`).
  - Cerbos still decides; `error` keeps its reason at the end. A human who is refused for another reason gets the ordinary 403 with no `reason`.
- **Idempotency (criterion 3).** `draftReply` requires `idempotencyKey`; a retry returns the same draft (`replayed: true`). `saveMinutes` replaces the draft in place; close/reopen set state.
- **Activity rows (criterion 6), each with the actor and `metadata.via` (the agent or MCP client that drove it):** `drafted_reply` (new), `posted`, `sent_draft` (now also `draftedBy`), `closed` / `reopened` / `renamed` (new), `saved_minutes` (new: ids and size, never the text), `shared_minutes`. The staff `posted` and `sent_draft` rows now carry `channel: "staff"` where they carried `via: "staff"`, because a row's own `metadata.via` overrides the ambient agent stamp.
- **Hub transport.** `meetings.saveMinutes` is the first core tool whose endpoint is a `PUT`; `McpToolDef.method` (and mcp-hub's mirror type) gained `"PUT"`. The hub passes `def.method` to `fetch` unchanged. Because the hub fills every `:token` of a path, optional filters on `listThreads` are query tokens whose schema default is `all`.

### 29f. Staff screens (PV4-09, 2026-10-13) — `platform-ui` — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED (component tests and the demo-mode Playwright specs; the BFF itself is unchanged except `sourceMessageId`, §16f-ii)**

The staff UI adds no route. It reads and writes only the routes in §29b, §29c, §16f and the contracts list.

- **Where.** Hub Projects tab, `#conversation` section (`/clients/[clientId]/work`): this client's threads, "Awaiting our reply" first then by last activity, with unread and waiting-draft counts and "Start a conversation" (on a project, or General). Thread page `/clients/[clientId]/work/conversation/[threadId]` (the hub's Projects tab stays lit under `work/`). Project workspace: a **Conversation** tab, only for a project that has a client. Meeting page `/meetings/[id]`: a **Minutes** card. Overview: `needsUs` items of kind `conversation` (the UI union grew by `'conversation'`) and a tile from `conversationsAwaitingReply` (absent on an older server, and then no tile).
- **Markers.** Every thread row, message row, draft card and minutes row shows "Client sees this" / "Internal" from the backend's `clientVisible` only; a missing field renders nothing (plan trap 9).
- **Reads.** The page reads `GET /conversation/:id` and `GET /conversation/:id/drafts?status=all` (the sent drafts carry the agent's name for the staff-only "Drafted by" line). A refused read renders a `ReadRefusal`, never "no conversations".
- **Polling.** Every 20 s while the page is visible and once on window focus or when the tab becomes visible; nothing runs while it is hidden (design decision 6). Each poll re-reads the thread, which marks it read.
- **Writes.** Post; Close and Reopen (`PATCH :threadId`); draft Send (behind a confirm that names the client), Edit and Discard. **No edit or remove on a message (PV-D34):** a sent message is permanent, so the thread shows no Edit or Remove control, no "edited" mark and no "Message removed" row, and the composer says "Messages can't be edited or removed once sent. Post a correction instead." beside the prices-and-terms hint. Plain text only, at most 10,000 characters, 5 files and 10 MB in total (files travel as base64 in the server action and on to the §29b body).
- **"Turn into a change request"** on a client message opens a small request form (kind, title, details) prefilled from the message and sends `POST /webdev/change-requests` with `sourceMessageId` (§16f-ii). The staff app had no request-create form before this, so this is the only one.
- **Minutes.** The editor saves with `PUT .../minutes` and stays a draft; "Share with client" is offered only when the meeting has a client, there is a saved non-blank draft and no unsaved edit, and it asks first, naming the client. After a share the editor is read-only and says "Shared on <date> by <name>". There is no unshare.
- **Gating.** Controls are shown for `client.write` (the same members, managers and company admins that Cerbos lets post, draft, manage, update and `share_minutes`). That is cosmetic: the platform decides.

## 29c. Meeting minutes shared with the client (PV4-05, 2026-10-12) — `platform-nest/src/core/meetings.controller.ts` (staff), `portal-workspace.controller.ts` (portal); predicates in `portal-visibility.ts` — **STATUS: BACKEND BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `meeting-minutes.controller.test.ts` and the Cerbos matrix run against real Postgres + Cerbos on the Linux CI gate; portal UI BUILT by PV4-08, PROTOTYPED (vitest, a demo-mode Playwright spec and a stub-BFF Playwright spec; not run against a live platform-nest); staff UI BUILT by PV4-09 (§29f), PROTOTYPED (vitest and demo-mode Playwright specs))**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-12-pv4-conversation-tickets.md` (PV4-05; finding 8; design decisions 8 and 9). Cross-referenced from §16a. Rulings PV-D23 (nothing an agent writes reaches a client until a staff member approves it), PV4-Q1 (default: minutes of a meeting with NO project are visible only to client-wide contacts).

**What a client can read of a meeting: the minutes, and nothing else.** `meeting` STAYS in `NEVER_CLIENT_VISIBLE`: the recording, `transcript`, `transcript_ref`, `audio_ref`, `local_hint`, `drive_*`, the participants and the pipeline run are internal and no portal read names them. Minutes are a separate object (`meeting_minutes`, PV4-01): one row per meeting, written as a **draft**, then deliberately **shared** by a person. Once shared they are **frozen** (a save is 409) and there is **no unshare route** (once a client has read something, taking it back is a conversation, not a button).

**Visibility rule (one predicate, shared by the portal and the staff marker).** `meetingMinutesInPortalScope(minutesAlias, meetingAlias, params)` in `portal-visibility.ts`: the **meeting's** `client_id` is one of the caller's clients, `meeting_minutes.status = 'shared'`, the meeting is not soft-deleted, and for a project-scoped contact the **meeting's** `project_id` is one of theirs. **No NULL-project admission** (same shape as runs and conversation threads, `allowNullProject = false`). Minutes carry **no `client_id`/`project_id` of their own** (design decision 8): both come from the meeting, so re-linking a meeting moves its minutes with it and removing its client takes them out of every portal.

### Staff — `src/core/meetings.controller.ts` (Cerbos kind `meeting_recording`)

| Status | Method | Path | Cerbos | Payload / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/meetings/:id/minutes` | `meeting_recording` · `read` | `{meetingId, clientId, projectId, title, shareable, minutes: null \| {id, bodyMd, status:'draft'\|'shared', draftedBy, updatedBy, createdAt, updatedAt, sharedAt, sharedBy, sharedByName, clientVisible}}`. `minutes` is `null` until one was ever saved. `shareable` = a non-blank draft on a meeting that has a client (state only; the action decides who). `clientVisible` is computed in SQL from `staffMeetingMinutesClientVisible` (the meeting has a client AND the minutes are shared on a live meeting), never retyped (plan trap 9). 404 for an unknown, deleted or non-uuid meeting id. |
| PROTOTYPED | PUT | `/api/:t/meetings/:id/minutes` | `meeting_recording` · `update` | `{bodyMd: string}` (0..100,000 chars) -> the same view as GET. **Saving keeps `draft`.** `updated_by` = the caller always; `drafted_by` is set **only** when the caller's `principal.kind` is `bot` or `automation`, and is kept when a person later edits the text. **409** once shared. Authorization runs before validation (a denied caller never sees a 400). **Allowed to agents** (an agent may draft minutes). Emits `meeting.minutes.saved` (ids and size, never the text) and, after the commit, writes a `saved_minutes` activity for the caller (PV4-07). |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/meetings/:id/minutes/share` | `meeting_recording` · **`share_minutes`** (new) | no body -> **200** `{id (the minutes), meetingId, status:'shared', sharedAt, sharedBy, notified}`. **Refused to `bot`/`automation` principals by Cerbos** (403 `{error, reason: "agents_draft_staff_send"}`; `error` names `meetings.saveMinutes` and ends with `cerbos denied share_minutes on meeting_recording`; PV-D23, PV4-07). **409** when the meeting has no `client_id`, when there are no minutes or they are blank, and when they are already shared (including the loser of a concurrent double share). ONE UPDATE stamps `status='shared'`, `shared_at`, `shared_by` guarded `WHERE status = 'draft'`. See "On share". |

There is no `DELETE`, `PATCH` or `unshare` route on minutes.

### Portal — `src/core/portal-workspace.controller.ts` (`portal` · `read`, then `resolvePortalScope`)

`GET /api/:t/portal/meetings[?projectId]` and `GET /api/:t/portal/meetings/:minutesId` are listed in §16a. **Payload (pinned by a key-set test, never widened by a new column):**

```
{ id, title, meetingDate, bodyMd, sharedAt, sharedBy }
```

`title` falls back to `"Meeting"`; `meetingDate` = `started_at`, else `scheduled_at`, else `created_at`; `bodyMd` is Markdown (render it sanitised, or as text); `sharedBy` is the sharer's display name only (never an email or an id). **Not in the payload, on purpose:** `transcript`, `transcript_ref`, `audio_ref`, `local_hint`, `drive_*`, participants, the pipeline run, `clientId`, `projectId`.

### On share

- **Outbox event** `meeting.minutes.shared` (entity type `meeting_minutes`, entity id = the minutes id), payload `{clientId, projectId, meetingId, minutesId, actorId}` (ids only, never text). Mapped in `portal-live.service.ts` to the **existing portal topic `projects`**; `meeting_minutes` is added to `TAILED_ENTITY_TYPES`. `clientId` narrows the frame to that client's connections (§16d). No new topic, so `PortalTopic` in `platform-ui/src/lib/portal.ts` is unchanged.
- **Notification** (in-app, best-effort, after the commit) to the client's contacts **in scope**: `resolveClientRecipients(kind: "general")` for the meeting's client and project (client-wide contacts, plus contacts of that project; a project-less meeting reaches client-wide contacts only; viewers included), type `meeting.minutes.shared`, title `Meeting minutes shared: <title>`, **href `/portal/meetings/<minutesId>`**. This is a NEW portal path used in a notification: `platform-ui/src/lib/portal-links.guard.test.ts` lists it in its `AWAITING_PAGE` ledger until **PV4-08** builds the page and gives it a portal area (PV4-08 must delete that ledger entry; a test fails the moment the page exists). The notice carries no minutes text.
- Mail: not sent (the mail allow-list is two types; PV4-06 owns client mail).

### Authorization summary

`share_minutes` reaches exactly the roles that hold `update` on `meeting_recording` (`company_admin`, `manager`, `member`; perm mirror `perm_meeting_recording_share_minutes`), and is **denied to `kind` `bot`/`automation`** (PV-D23). See `PERMISSION-CONTRACT.md` §34.

## 30. Billing profiles, issue readiness, issue and void (PV5-04, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/modules/invoice/{issue.ts,billing-profile.controller.ts,invoice.controller.ts}`, migrations `202610130400` (data model), `202610131850` (the invoice CHECK; its guard trigger reuses 1820's `pv5_legacy_flag_guard()`) and `202610132115` (invoice numbers, PV5-04b, §30b) — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `src/modules/invoice/issue.test.ts` and DB suite `src/db/pv5-invoice-enforcement.db.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; not driven live — PV5-13)**

Ruling PV-D7: the finance ledger is the invoice of record. `invoices` stays the drafting stage (lines from logged hours,
maker/checker approve); **issuing** numbers it and posts the matching ledger AR invoice in one transaction, after which
both are immutable except `status → paid | void`. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-12-pv5-contracts-billing-tickets.md`.

| Status | Method | Path | Authz | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/billing-profile` | `finance_config` · `read` | `{ legalName, address, invoicePrefix, defaultPaymentTermsDays, currencyCode, bank: {bankName, accountName, accountNo} \| null, bankLedgerAccountCode, defaultRevenueAccountCode, signatureThreshold, updatedBy, updatedAt }`. **404** before one exists. Not module-gated (readiness must be able to say "finance module off" separately). **PV5-10:** adds `gatewayClearingAccountCode` (string or null). |
| PROTOTYPED | PUT | `/api/:t/billing-profile` | `finance_config` · `update` for any non-bank field; **`set_bank_details`** when the body has a `bank` key (owner or finance_manager GRANT on this company, or platform_admin; HIGH assurance for everyone; bots never. PV-D29's interim relaxation for an owner / finance_manager was LIFTED by PV-D40 / PV5-14 (2026-10-13); on the dev stage high is reached through the simulated second factor, §1, and a below-high refusal carries `reason: "assurance_required"` while it is on) | Upsert; omitted fields are kept. A new profile needs `legalName`, `address`, `invoicePrefix` (`^[A-Z0-9-]{1,16}$`). `defaultPaymentTermsDays` 0–365, `currencyCode` a known ISO code, account codes are free codes resolved at issue time (readiness names a missing one), `signatureThreshold` positive or null (PV-D8). `bank: {bankName, accountName, accountNo}` sets the block clients pay into (all three or `null` to clear). Both authorizations run before validation; a body touching only `bank` needs only `set_bank_details` (so an owner can change it). A bank change writes an activity row `bank_details_changed` (account masked to the last 4) and notifies EVERY owner of the company (`billing.bank_details_changed`, warning; the number is never in the notification) — PV-D26. **PV5-10:** `gatewayClearingAccountCode` (an account code or `null`; `finance_config` `update`, like the other two codes: it books money, it does not redirect it) names the account an ONLINE payment's AR receipt is booked into. Online payment is not offered while it does not resolve to a live, postable, non-control account. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/billing-profile/masked` | `finance_config` · `read` | PV5-12, the agent view (tool `billingProfile.read`): the profile as above but `bank: {bankName, accountName, accountNoMasked} \| null`, where `accountNoMasked` is `••••` plus the last 4 characters. The full number is never returned, to any caller. **PV5-F4:** adds `gatewayClearingAccountCode` (`string \| null`, the ledger account an online payment is booked to; an account code is not secret, unlike the bank number). **404** before a profile exists. Agent tools of this section: `invoices.issueReadiness` (read), `invoices.issue` and `invoices.voidIssued` (HIGH, D14; an approved call re-runs as the human the agent acted for, who must hold `invoice` `issue` / `void_issued`; a bot or automation principal is refused 403), `billingProfile.read`. No tool sets bank details, certifies a contract or creates a checkout. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/invoices/:invoiceId/issue-readiness` | `invoice` · `read` | See §4. One row per blocker; `ready: true` with `[]` when issuable. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/invoices/:invoiceId/issue` | `invoice` · `issue` | See §4 for the shapes. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/invoices/:invoiceId/void` | `invoice` · `void_issued` | See §4. |

**What one issue does, in one `withFinance` transaction** (`issue.ts`): lock the invoice row → re-check readiness on it
(refuse with every blocker, nothing written) → find or create the client's AR customer (`code CL-<client id>`, terms from
the profile; a group client's customer carries `counterparty_company_id = clients.group_company_id`, decision 20) → take
the number `{prefix}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{code}/{nnnn}`: the `{code}` from `billing_number_code()` (generated on first use for the (service line, client business type) pair, advisory-locked per company), then `next_document_no(tenant, 'invoice', year, month)` with the year and month of the ISSUE DATE (row-locked: a rollback returns the number and leaves no code behind, concurrent issues serialise; §30b) →
compute each line's tax with `finance_tax_compute(code, line amount, issue date)` rounded to the currency's minor unit,
all in `numeric` → insert the AR invoice + lines (revenue account from the profile) and `finance_ar_issue_invoice()` →
write `invoice_no`, `issue_date` (today), `due_date` (+ the customer's terms), `subtotal`, `tax_total`, `total`, the
frozen `issuer` snapshot and `ar_invoice_id`, status `sent` → emit `invoice.issued` and an `issued` revision. Other
series: receipts `{prefix}/RC/{yyyy}/{nnnn}`, credit notes `{prefix}/CN/{yyyy}/{nnnn}`.

**Rules a consumer must not get wrong**
- `sent` = **Issued**. Label it so; there is no other way into `sent`, and `paid` is never set by a person.
- The books are kept at exchange rate 1, so an invoice in a currency other than the company's functional currency is
  refused (`CURRENCY_NOT_FUNCTIONAL`) rather than booked at face value.
- A taxed invoice (`taxCode` set at create) is refused until Finance records the company as PKP (`PKP_NOT_CONFIRMED`,
  owner, PV-D7) and the code has a rate in force.
- Legacy invoices (sent/paid before PV-5, `legacyUnissued: true`) are exempt from the CHECK, take no new payment
  claims, and keep the old confirm rule.
- Agent tools for these routes are PV5-12.

**Screens — PV5-09 (PROTOTYPED; vitest on the pure rules and the components, DEMO_MODE Playwright written but not run, no live backend).** No new endpoint: every screen calls the routes above and the ones in §16b and §16e.

- **Staff invoice page `/invoices/[id]`:** for an approved invoice, the readiness blockers are listed (each with a link to where it is cleared) before the click, and Issue is disabled with that reason; once issued, the invoice of record (number, issue and due dates, the PDF or "being prepared"), the issuer as frozen at issue (the bank account masked until Show), subtotal, tax and total, a link to Receivables for the finance read tier, and **Void** behind a confirm step that asks for a reason (the 409 `reason`s `not_issued`, `not_voidable`, `pending_payment` are shown in plain words). The staff `GET /invoices/:id` carries `subtotal`, `taxTotal` and `taxCode` but no per-line tax breakdown (the portal's `taxLines[]` has one), so the staff page shows the tax as one line.
- **Billing profile `/finance/settings/billing-profile`:** the issuer fields are saved by one PUT that never carries `bank`; the bank account is a separate section, "Clients pay into this account", masked by default, saved by its own PUT with only `{ bank }`. **Step-up:** the platform answers an assurance denial with the same plain 403 as a role denial, so the UI reads the cause from `/api/me`'s `assurance`: below `high` the user is sent to `/step-up?return=/finance/settings/billing-profile` (the existing flow) and back; at `high` the 403 is the role and is said in words (a redirect there would loop). A structured `reason` on that 403 would let the UI stop inferring it.
- **Client billing page `/clients/[id]/billing`:** each contract shows its tier, its `contentSha256` in short form with a Copy button, "Mark certified" (a draft only; **rendered only while the backend's `certifiedSigning.available` is true, otherwise absent, not disabled** (PV5-F4, PV-D44); a 409 `no_certified_provider` is still put in words if it is ever called) and, once signed, the sealed copy through `GET /api/files/:id`. Invoices list their number, an "Issued" status and the PDF or "being prepared".
- **Portal invoice `/portal/invoices/[id]`:** the invoice of record laid out (number, dates, issuer legal name, address and NPWP, the PDF through `/api/:t/portal/files/:id`), tax and totals from `taxLines[]`/`subtotal`/`taxTotal`, "How to pay" from `issuer.bank` with the invoice number as the reference, and the manual claim form with bank transfer, cash and other (**no Card**, design decision 17; the server enum keeps `card`).
- **Portal contract `/portal/contracts/[id]`:** a "Your signed copy" card once `status` is `signed`: the link through `/api/:t/portal/files/:id`, or "being prepared".
- **Read fields PV5-07 added (now real), still treated as optional:** `pdfFileId` (invoice list and detail, staff and portal) and `signedCopyFileId` (contract list and detail, staff and portal). Absent and `null` read alike: an issued invoice or a signed contract says "being prepared", anything else says nothing (`lib/billingView.ts`). Every screen works whether or not PV5-07 has merged.


### 30b. Invoice numbers: service lines, number codes and the monthly counter (PV5-04b, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/modules/invoice/{billing-numbering.ts,billing-numbering.controller.ts,issue.ts,invoice.controller.ts}`, migration `202610132115_pv5_invoice_numbering.sql` — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `src/modules/invoice/invoice-numbering.test.ts` and DB suite `src/db/pv5-invoice-numbering.db.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; not driven live)**

Ruling PV-D35 (owner, 2026-10-13): an invoice number reads **`{company}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{code}/{nnnn}`**, e.g. `GDA/2026/10/7K3/0001`.
`{company}` is the billing profile's `invoicePrefix`; `{mm}` is zero-padded and, with `{yyyy}`, comes from the **issue date**;
`{nnnn}` runs **per company per month**, never per code (so numbering stays gap-free for audit), at least four digits;
`{code}` is a short alphanumeric code for the (service line, client business type) pair, **deliberately not mnemonic**: a
client cannot easily read it and staff decode it in the ERP. The AR invoice carries the same number (unique per tenant).
Receipts (`{prefix}/RC/{yyyy}/{nnnn}`) and credit notes (`{prefix}/CN/{yyyy}/{nnnn}`) keep their yearly numbers.

**Service lines are company data** (`billing_service_lines`: `key` `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$`, `name`, optional `departmentId` (an
org-node id, free text like `projects.department_id`), `active`). Switched off, never deleted. **The code lookup**
(`billing_number_codes`: unique `(tenant, service line, business type)` and unique `(tenant, code)`, code `^[A-Z0-9]{2,4}$`) is
assigned the first time a pair is needed, inside the issue transaction: 3 random characters from an alphabet without O, 0, I, 1,
L, drawn under a per-company advisory transaction lock so two concurrent first issues agree on one code. A code is **never
changed, deleted or reused** (a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE, for the owner too; the runtime role has neither grant).

| Status | Method | Path | Authz | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/billing/service-lines` | `finance_config` · `read` | `[{ key, name, departmentId, active, updatedAt, invoiceCount }]`. Staff only. |
| PROTOTYPED | PUT | `/api/:t/billing/service-lines/:key` | `finance_config` · `update` | Create or edit. `{ name?, departmentId? (null unlinks), active? }`; a new line needs `name`. The key is the identity and never changes. Authorization before validation. Answers the line. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/billing/number-codes` | `finance_config` · `read` | The decode table: `{ codes: [{ serviceLineKey, serviceLineName, businessType, businessTypeLabel, code, createdAt, invoiceCount, used }], businessTypes: [{ id, label }] }`. **Staff only: no portal route reads it.** |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/billing/number-codes` | `finance_config` · `update` | Pre-assign a pair's code before its first invoice: `{ serviceLineKey, businessType, code? }`; `businessType` is a client-centre type. No `code` generates one. **200** `{ serviceLineKey, businessType, code, alreadyAssigned }`. A pair that already has a code is never changed: the same request answers it back (`alreadyAssigned: true`), a different `code` is **409** `reason: "code_already_assigned"`; a code held by another pair is **409** `code_taken`; unknown line **404**. |
| PROTOTYPED | PATCH | `/api/:t/invoices/:invoiceId/service-line` | `invoice` · `issue` (company_admin, manager; bots and automation DENIED), before validation | `{ serviceLineKey: string \| null }` (`null` clears the choice). Only a `draft` or `approved` invoice: an issued one is **409** `reason: "issued"`. An unknown or switched-off line is **400**. No revision row (the revision action list is a closed CHECK); the choice is an `updated` activity. |

**How an invoice gets its service line.** Staff choose one (`PATCH …/service-line`). With no choice it DEFAULTS when every
line of the invoice carries a `projectId` (the generator now writes it), every such project has a department, each department
maps to **exactly one** active service line, and they are all the same line (`defaultServiceLineKey` on the detail). Anything
else (a line with no project, a project with no department, two lines linked to one department, projects that disagree) gives
**no default, never a guess**. No line at all is the readiness blocker `NO_SERVICE_LINE` (the readiness GET, the issue 409 and
the agent tool `invoices.issueReadiness` all carry it). Issue writes the effective line and the code onto the invoice; both
are **frozen** with the other invoice-of-record columns (`pv5_invoices_issued_immutable` names `service_line_key` and
`number_code`). The business type is the client's client-centre `business_type` (`other` when the client has no profile).

**Rules a consumer must not get wrong**
- **Staff only.** The code, its meaning, the decode table, the service line and `lines[].projectId` are never in a portal
  read: the portal shows the number only (`GET /portal/invoices[/:id]` select none of them and strip `projectId` from `lines`).
  A client contact is refused (403) on every route above.
- A number's `{code}` is not derived from the key or the business type; never compute or guess one in the browser.
- The monthly counter is `document_series (tenant, series, year, month)`; `month 0` is the legacy yearly counter, which every
  pre-existing row keeps. The 3-argument `next_document_no(tenant, series, year)` still counts the yearly series.
- A legacy number (`{prefix}/{yyyy}/{nnnn}`, none exist on live) has no `numberCode`: show no decode, never an error.

**Screens (PROTOTYPED; vitest on the pure rules and the page, no live backend).**
- **Billing profile `/finance/settings/billing-profile`:** a "Service lines" section (add, rename, link or unlink a department,
  switch off or on) and a "Number codes" section (the decode table: code, service line, business type, invoices; plus an
  optional pre-assign form). Each section reads on its own and refuses explicitly. There is no edit control on a code.
- **Staff invoice page `/invoices/[id]`:** a "Service line" card with a picker before Issue (it names the default when there is
  one; the `NO_SERVICE_LINE` blocker's link lands on it), the line in the Summary, and, next to an issued number, its code with
  what it stands for. The demo mode mirrors the routes.

### 30c. Online payment: the provider webhook and how a gateway payment is booked (PV5-10, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/payments/{provider,midtrans,registry,checkout,process,webhook.controller}.ts`, migration `202610140830_pv5_online_payment_checkout.sql` — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED against a SIMULATED Midtrans (owner ruling 2026-10-13: no sandbox keys yet; unit suites in `src/payments/*.test.ts`, DB suite `src/payments/online-payment.db.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; never driven against Midtrans)**

Ruling PV-D9 / PV-D25: a provider-hosted checkout (Midtrans Snap) for issued invoices; a verified provider notice confirms the
payment with no staff step. Everything is OFF unless `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY` is set (runbook `infra/runbooks/midtrans-payments.md`).

| Status | Method | Path | Authz | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/webhooks/payments/:provider` | none: the provider SIGNATURE is the authentication (no AuthGuard, no Cerbos; the GitHub receiver's shape) | Midtrans' "Payment Notification URL" = `https://erp.gaiada.com/api/webhooks/payments/midtrans`. Unknown or switched-off provider **404**, nothing written. Signature (`signature_key` = hex SHA-512 of `order_id + status_code + gross_amount + server key`, `gross_amount` as the exact string sent, constant-time) fails **401**, nothing written. Otherwise claims the dedupe key in `provider_events` (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (provider, event_id) DO NOTHING`) and, in the same transaction, emits `payment.notice.received` on the `provider_event` stream; answers **200** `{ok: true}` (a replay: `{ok: true, duplicate: true}`) without waiting for anything else (Midtrans wants 200 within 5 s). |

**Processing (after the 200; `process.ts`), from the outbox consumer and a plain-Postgres retry sweep (every 30 s; works with
Redis off):** re-fetch the order's status from the provider's API (the notice's own status words are never trusted: only
`order_id`, `status_code` and `gross_amount` are signed) → paid only for `settlement`, or `capture` with
`fraud_status = accept` → in ONE `withFinance` (`withBilling`) transaction, with the claim, the checkout and the invoice locked:
an `invoice_payments` row (`source 'gateway'`, `method 'online'`, `confirmed`, `recorded_by = confirmed_by =` the provider's
automation principal, `provider_payment_id` = Midtrans `transaction_id`, unique), the AR receipt + allocation through the SAME
`postConfirmedPayment` the staff confirmation uses (`receiptAccount: gateway_clearing`), the checkout `paid`, the invoice `paid`
when the AR invoice is, `invoice.payment.confirmed` (`via: gateway`), the claim `processed`. Then the client is told
(`invoice.payment.confirmed`) and staff (project owners + finance managers: `invoice.payment.received_online`).
**Ignored, no payment, Finance told** (`payment.online.needs_attention`, once per notice): `unknown_checkout`, `amount_mismatch`
(the provider's amount or currency differs from the checkout's, compared in `numeric`, no tolerance), `invoice_void`,
`invoice_paid`, `not_issued`, `exceeds_outstanding`, `checkout_already_paid`, and a refund/chargeback status (`reversed`).
**Retried** (1, 2, 4 … min, capped at 1 h; `failed` after 30 attempts, Finance told): provider unreachable, a ledger refusal
(no clearing account, no open period: Finance told at once), and a notice that SAYS settlement while the API still says
pending (lagging status or a lying notice; nothing is written meanwhile). Out of order is fine: a late `pending` notice
re-fetches `settlement`, finds the payment recorded and writes nothing.

**Not the staff decide route, not D14.** The bypass is deliberate (plan finding 14) and written in `webhook.controller.ts`'s
header: the second party is the provider's own status API, not a person.

**Reconciliation (a lost notice).** An unpaid checkout is never expired on our clock alone. Once past its expiry the sweep
asks the provider (`fetchStatus`), and keeps asking hourly for `PAYMENTS_RECONCILE_DAYS` (default 7) after it. A paid answer
becomes a synthetic claim `<order_id>:reconcile` in `provider_events` and goes through the same processing; it can never
write twice with a late real notice (`ux_invoice_payments_provider_payment` and `ux_invoice_payments_checkout`). An unpaid
open checkout is expired here and, best effort, at the provider (`POST /v2/{order_id}/expire`). A checkout retired because
the amount changed is expired at the provider the same way (outside the transaction; failures are logged, never block).
**Never unset or rotate the key while checkouts are open** (runbook §2).

**Environment.** `payment_checkouts.environment` (sandbox | production): a checkout is reused, re-checked or expired only
with its own environment's key. After a switch, the other environment's open checkouts are retired and a fresh one is opened.

**One checkout, one payment.** `invoice_payments.checkout_id` (FK, same tenant) is set on every gateway payment, with a
partial UNIQUE index.

**Unknown orders.** A notice whose `order_id` is not a `ck-` checkout of this company is `ignored: unknown_checkout` with no
status call; Finance is told only when the notice itself claims payment (settlement or capture). A status answer with no
`currency`, or one that is not the checkout's (IDR), is `ignored: amount_mismatch`.

**Who Finance is.** `finance_manager` and `owner` grants at company scope on the company or any company above it (its parent
chain); when none exists, its `company_admin`s, with a loud log; when there is still nobody, a loud log. Never silent.

| Status | Method | Path | Authz | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/payments/provider-events?status=failed\|ignored\|received\|processed` | `finance_config` · `read` | `{items: [{id, provider, orderId, status, error, lastError, attempts, outcome, receivedAt, processedAt}]}`, newest first, 200 at most; `status` defaults to `failed`. Authorized before validation (bad `status` 400). |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/payments/provider-events/:eventId/redrive` | `finance_config` · `update` (checked FIRST: 403 for anyone else, whatever the id) | Bodyless. Only a `failed` payment claim: back to `received`, attempts 0, processed at once through the normal path. **200** `{ok, outcome}`; **404** when there is no failed claim with that id in this company (an `ignored` claim was refused on purpose and is not re-driven). Writes an activity `redriven` (audit). |

#### Simulated Midtrans (review stage, PV-D41) — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED (DB suite `src/payments/online-payment-simulated.db.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate, real HTTP on loopback)**

Owner ruling PV-D41 (2026-10-14, "simulate midtrans for now"), in the spirit of PV-D40: online payment works end to end on
the review stage with no keys and no money. **Labelled, audited, flag-gated, and OFF before the ERP holds real data.**

- **Switch:** `PAYMENTS_SIMULATION_ENABLED=1` AND `MIDTRANS_ENVIRONMENT=simulated` AND a placeholder
  `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY` (`SIM-` + random) AND `MIDTRANS_TENANT_ID`. Boot refuses either half alone, and the flag with
  sandbox/production; boot logs `[payments:simulation-enabled]` once.
- **The real path runs.** The real Midtrans adapter calls an in-process simulator over HTTP (loopback,
  `PAYMENTS_SIMULATOR_INTERNAL_URL` + `/internal/payments/midtrans-sim`, not routed by nginx) with HTTP Basic: Snap create,
  `GET /v2/{order}/status`, `POST /v2/{order}/expire`, Midtrans' shapes. The simulator's orders live in
  `payment_simulator_orders` (migration `202610150130`, FORCE RLS, read only for `MIDTRANS_TENANT_ID`). On an action it
  delivers a Midtrans-shaped notice, signed with the key (`gross_amount` as `"150000.00"`), by HTTP POST to
  `/api/webhooks/payments/midtrans`, after answering the click, with retries (0, 0.5, 2, 5 s). Signature check, dedupe,
  status re-fetch and posting are the normal ones. Checkouts carry `environment = 'simulated'` and never mix with sandbox
  or production ones.
- **Hosted page:** Snap's `redirect_url` is `/portal/pay/simulated/:orderId` (platform-ui), titled "Simulated payment",
  lead "Simulated payment (review stage): no real money moves", with the invoice number, the amount and three actions:
  "Pay (simulated)" (settlement), "Leave pending" (pending), "Payment fails" (deny). Afterwards the payer goes back to
  `/portal/invoices/:id?checkout=finished`.

| Status | Method | Path | Authz | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/portal/payments/simulated/:orderId` | `portal` · `pay` (FIRST) | **404** unless the simulated Midtrans is the provider for this company, and unless the order's checkout invoice is in the caller's portal scope (`invoiceInPortalScope`; never 403). `{simulated: true, orderId, invoiceId, invoiceNo, amount, currency, transactionStatus (null \| pending \| settlement \| deny \| expire), canAct, returnUrl}`. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/portal/payments/simulated/:orderId/act` | `portal` · `pay` (FIRST) | `{action: "pay" \| "pending" \| "fail"}` (400 otherwise, after the 404 checks). **409** `reason: already_final \| expired` once settled, denied or expired. **200** `{ok, simulated: true, transactionStatus, returnUrl}`. Writes an activity `payment.simulated` (actor, order, amount, currency, action) on the invoice, then delivers the notice. Writes no payment itself. |

**Labels.** A payment through a simulated checkout has `invoice_payments.reference` starting `SIMULATED Online payment`
and `note` "SIMULATED payment (review stage, PV-D41): no real money moved."; its AR receipt's reference therefore reads
SIMULATED too. Every notification of the payment path (client, staff, Finance) is titled `SIMULATED: …` while the
simulation is on.

**Known v1 behaviour: a manual claim while a checkout is open.** A client can still record a bank-transfer claim while an
online checkout for the same invoice is open. The next "Pay online" then charges only what the claims leave (and retires the
old checkout); but a payer still on the old page could pay the old amount. If that payment lands it is recorded only when it
still fits the outstanding balance, else `ignored: exceeds_outstanding` and Finance refunds or applies the difference.

**Tenant resolution.** `provider_events` is FORCE RLS with `tenant_id NOT NULL`; nothing is loosened. The company is
`MIDTRANS_TENANT_ID`, the company that owns the merchant account (the key that verified the signature is that account's), as
the GitHub receiver uses `GITHUB_REPO_SYNC_TENANT_ID`. Only that company's invoices are offered online.

**Journals Finance posts by hand (v1).** The receipt above books **DR gateway clearing / CR AR** (the clearing code is
`company_billing_profiles.gateway_clearing_account_code`, data). When Midtrans pays out, Finance posts a manual journal
**DR Bank (the billing profile's receipt account, e.g. 1120) / CR gateway clearing** for the net payout, and **DR a
payment-fee expense account (and DR PPN Masukan 1170 for the VAT on the fee, if Midtrans invoices it) / CR gateway
clearing** for the fee, so the clearing account returns to zero per payout. Refunds and chargebacks are reversed by hand too.

**[UNVERIFIED until the sandbox drive]:** the dedupe key `order_id:transaction_status:status_code` (vs. the transaction id;
unknown status words normalise to `other`); the notice field formats (`gross_amount` as `"150000.00"`, `status_code` a string,
times `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` GMT+7); the status API's 404 for an order nobody has paid; the Snap `expiry {unit: "minutes",
duration}` and `callbacks.finish` being honoured in redirect mode; the sandbox key prefix `SB-` (only a boot warning keys on
it); Midtrans' retry behaviour after our 200.


### 30a. Issued-invoice PDFs and the sealed signed copy (PV5-07, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/document-{jobs,render,seal,read-fields}.ts`, migration `202610132000_pv5_document_files_seal.sql` — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED (DB suite `src/core/document-jobs.db.test.ts` + unit suite `document-seal.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; never driven against the real renderer or a real key on a server)**

**PDF footer (PV5-F1, PROTOTYPED).** The renderer's footer is no longer the fixed "GAIADA — Report". `POST /render` takes an optional `footerText` (escaped, capped at 120 characters); document renders pass `{issuer legal name} - {invoice number | contract reference}`, report exports pass none and get the neutral "Report". See `report-renderer/README.md`.

Decision 19: each document is rendered ONCE after commit (outbox `invoice.issued` / `contract.signed`, plus a sweep
that retries anything still owed) and stored as a `files` row with a role and a SHA-256. It is never re-rendered on
download. Decision 21 / PV-D25: a signed contract's copy is ONE PDF (the agreement, then the evidence page) carrying
a PAdES seal made with the company's own self-issued key.

**New read fields (additive; PV5-08 and PV5-09 consume exactly these names):**

| Read | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/:t/invoices`, `GET /api/:t/invoices/:invoiceId` (staff, §4) | `pdfFileId: string \| null` | The live `invoice_pdf` file of an ISSUED invoice. `null` = not issued, or issued and **being prepared**. |
| `GET /api/:t/portal/invoices`, `GET /api/:t/portal/invoices/:invoiceId` (§16b) | `pdfFileId: string \| null` | Same. Download with `GET /api/:t/portal/files/:pdfFileId`. |
| `GET /api/:t/contracts`, `GET /api/:t/contracts/:contractId` (staff, §16e) | `signedCopyFileId: string \| null` | The live `contract_signed_copy` file (the sealed copy). `null` = not signed, or signed and **being prepared**. **PV5-11:** for a `certified` contract it is the live `contract_certified_copy` instead (the provider's signed PDF, §30d); a certified contract is never sealed. |
| `GET /api/:t/portal/contracts`, `GET /api/:t/portal/contracts/:contractId` (§16b) | `signedCopyFileId: string \| null` | Same. Download with `GET /api/:t/portal/files/:signedCopyFileId`. |

Staff download: `GET /api/:t/files/:fileId/content` (authorizes `invoice` / `contract` read on the parent, unchanged).
`DELETE /api/:t/files/:fileId` on a role file answers **409** (and the database refuses it too).

**Rules a consumer must not get wrong**
- `null` on an issued invoice or a signed contract means **"being prepared"**, never "there is no document". Show it
  as such; do not offer to generate one (there is no on-demand render route, by design).
- A role file is a record: it cannot be deleted, replaced or changed (`trg_files_guard_role_file`), and there is at
  most one live file per parent and role (`ux_files_live_role`).
- The sealed copy verifies in any PAdES-aware reader as "unmodified since sealed", and shows the signer's identity as
  **not verified** (the certificate is self-issued, not from a certification authority). That is expected; the
  evidence page says so in plain words. Do not describe the copy as a certified signature anywhere in the UI.

**Why a document is still "being prepared"** is in `document_jobs` (`status`, `last_error` = `<reason>: <words>`),
and an owner of the company is notified once per stuck document (`document.preparation_blocked`). Reasons:
`renderer_not_configured`, `render_failed`, `render_unverified` (the renderer returned a page that was not this
document), `seal_keys_dir_not_configured`, `seal_key_missing`, `seal_key_unreadable`, `seal_certificate_missing`
(blocked or failed: retried); `content_mismatch`, `content_missing`, `no_fixed_content`, `signatures_incomplete`,
`signature_hash_mismatch` (refused: never sealed, not retried).

**Internal only (not a BFF route):** `GET /internal/documents/print-payload/:jobToken` (no `/api`, no guards, the
one-shot token is the whole authorization, GETDEL; TR-21's shape) feeds the platform-ui print routes
`/print/invoices/[jobToken]` and `/print/contracts/[jobToken]`, which only the `report-renderer` sidecar opens.

### 30b. Documents: the portal list, the staff list and the `documents.list` tool (PV5-08, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/{client-documents,portal-documents.controller,client-documents.controller}.ts` — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED (unit suite `client-documents.test.ts` and the portal-visibility guard run anywhere; DB suite `client-documents.db.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; UI vitest only, axe is run by the lead on the Linux server)**

Plan decision 18: the Documents list holds **legal and money documents only**. Deliverables stay under Projects. Three kinds:

| `kind` | Row | `fileId` | `ready` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `signed_contract` | a contract with `status = 'signed'` | the sealed copy (`contract_signed_copy`, §30a); until that exists, the contract's attached document if it has one, else `null` | `true` only when the sealed copy exists. `false` = **being prepared** (show the original as "not yet sealed", or no link) |
| `signed_contract`, certified (PV5-11) | a `certified` contract with `status = 'signed'` | the provider's certified copy (`contract_certified_copy`, §30d), stored at completion together with the status, so it is never "being prepared" | `true` |
| `invoice` | an ISSUED invoice (`issued_at` set; void issued invoices stay) | the live `invoice_pdf` (§30a), `null` while it is being rendered | `fileId != null` |
| `receipt` | an invoice payment with a stored proof file | that proof file | `true` |

Every item: `{id, kind, title, date, fileId, ready, certified, simulated, certificateFileId}`. **PV5-11:** `certified` is true for a signed contract signed through a certified provider; `simulated` is true when that provider was the SIMULATED PSrE (PV-D43): the UI labels it **"Certified (simulated)"** from these two fields only; `certificateFileId` is the provider's certificate stored with the copy (download it like any `fileId`). All three are `false`/`null` on every other item. `id` is the source row (contract, invoice or payment); `title` is the contract title, the invoice number, or "Payment proof, <invoice number>"; `date` is ISO 8601 (the signing time, the issue time, or the paid-on date). **Newest first**, ties by kind then id. At most 200 rows per kind. A `fileId` is only ever one the matching download route will serve to the same caller (the list repeats that route's parent-entity test), so the list never offers a link that 404s.

| Status | Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ | GET | `/api/:t/portal/documents` | `portal` `read`; **not** module-gated (like the invoice and contract reads). The WHERE of each kind is `contractInPortalScope`, `invoiceInPortalScope`, and `invoiceInPortalScope` + `invoicePaymentClientVisible("pp", "detail")` (a receipt is reached through its invoice, as the receipt download is). **There is no row-visibility literal in the controller**; `portal-visibility.test.ts` fails the build if one is added. Rows outside the caller's scope never list (another client's, a draft contract, an unissued invoice, a payment on a draft invoice; a project-scoped contact gets only what the predicates admit). Returns `{items}`. Authorization runs first (staff get 403). |
| ✅ | GET | `/api/:t/clients/:clientId/documents` | The staff counterpart for the hub's Contracts & billing page. `client` `read` (the overview carries the same money items under it); 404 for an unknown client. The same three kinds over ALL of the client's live rows, each with **`clientVisible: boolean`**, computed from the same row-state builders (`staffClientVisible` over `contractClientVisible`, `invoiceClientVisible`, `staffInvoicePaymentClientVisible`). Meaning, as §22d: a client-wide contact of this client sees this row in the portal (a project-scoped contact may see less). The staff list holds rows the portal does not (a receipt filed against a draft invoice reads `false`). **Parity is a test, not a promise:** `client-documents.db.test.ts` proves the `clientVisible: true` ids equal the portal's ids for that client. The download is a separate call, `GET /api/:t/files/:fileId/content` (the UI's `/api/files/[fileId]`), which authorizes on the file's parent. |

**UI.** Portal: `/portal/documents` (`app/(portal)/portal/documents/page.tsx`), the third sub-tab of Contracts & billing (`lib/portalNav.ts`; every existing path is kept). Links go to `/api/:t/portal/files/:fileId`, never the staff route. A document still being prepared says so in words, and a failed read says it could not load (`listPortalDocuments` returns `null`), never "no documents". Staff: a Documents section on `/clients/[id]/billing` (`components/clients/billing/ClientDocuments.tsx`), links through `/api/files/[fileId]`, marker from `clientVisible` only (§22d, trap 9).

**MCP tool.** `documents.list` (core, read, `verified`): `GET /api/:tenantId/clients/:clientId/documents`, args `{tenantId, clientId}`. It lists and links; it never returns file bytes. There is no write counterpart. Golden case: `client-documents.db.test.ts`. Counted in `docs/modules/CAPABILITY-INVENTORY.md`.

**Known limit.** Portal scope comes from `resolvePortalScope`, which flattens a contact's project scope across their clients (on the board under "Before real clients use the portal"). This list is built only from the shared predicates and does not work around it, so the kernel fix covers it too.

### 30d. Certified signing: simulated provider (review stage, PV-D43) (PV5-11, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/signatures/{provider,registry,simulated-psre,simulated-provider,certified-signing,process,webhook.controller,certified-signing.controller,simulated-psre.controller,signer-checks}.ts`, migration `202610150300_pv5_certified_signing_simulated.sql` — **STATUS: PROTOTYPED against a SIMULATED PSrE (unit suite `src/signatures/simulated-psre.test.ts` runs anywhere; DB/HTTP suite `src/signatures/certified-signing.db.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; never driven against a real PSrE)**

**Owner ruling PV-D43 (2026-10-14):** certified signing is unparked for the REVIEW stage with a **simulated PSrE**, labelled, audited, flag-gated, and switched OFF before the ERP holds real data. The real PSrE (VIDA, PV-D25) is a second `SignatureProvider` adapter later. Runbook: `infra/runbooks/certified-signing-simulated.md`.

**Flag.** `SIGNATURE_SIMULATION_ENABLED` (compose `${SIGNATURE_SIMULATION_ENABLED:-0}`). Off: exactly the pre-PV5-11 behaviour (`mark-certified` and a certified `send` answer **409 `no_certified_provider`**; every simulator route and `POST /api/webhooks/signatures/simulated` answer **404**). On: the simulated PSrE (provider key `simulated`, label "Simulated PSrE (review stage)") is the certified provider; boot logs `[signatures:simulation-enabled] …` once.

**Flow.** Staff mark a draft certified → `send` fixes `content_sha256` and the tier `certified` (no envelope yet: a PSrE charges per signature) → the CLIENT presses "Sign with <label>" → the envelope is created from the fixed content (its bytes re-hashed and compared with `content_sha256`; the provider's own hash compared again), naming the client signer and our countersigner; `contracts.signature_provider` + `provider_envelope_id` are written and frozen → the client signs on the provider's page → the provider sends a notice → the ERP re-fetches the envelope and records the signature → an owner countersigns on the provider's page → on completion the ERP downloads the signed PDF and the certificate, checks them, stores both as files with SHA-256, sets the contract `signed` and emits `contract.signed` (PV5-07's sealing job skips a certified contract). Documents and every `signedCopyFileId` then point at the certified copy.

| Status | Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/portal/contracts/:contractId/certified-signing` | **The client reaches the sign step.** Body `{contentSha256}` (the hash the GET returned). Order: Cerbos `portal` `sign` (403) → a person (403 `signer_must_be_a_person` for an agent or bot channel, an `actFor` call, an `automation` or `bot` account) → the contract through `contractInPortalScope` (**404** out of scope, never 403) → signer capability on THIS contract's client (403 view-only) → body: no hash **400 `content_hash_required`**, a different hash **409 `content_changed`** → provider off **409 `no_certified_provider`** → not certified **409 `not_certified`**, the client already signed **409 `already_signed`**, not sent **409 `not_sent`**, term ended **409 `term_ended`** → the stored bytes no longer match `content_sha256` **409 `content_mismatch`** (nothing reaches the provider) → provider down **503 `provider_unavailable`** / refused **502 `provider_refused`**. **200** `{envelopeId, provider, label, simulated, signingUrl}`; idempotent (one envelope per contract; the provider also dedupes on our partner reference `"<tenant>:<contract>"`). Activity `certified_envelope_created` `{provider, simulated, envelopeId, contentSha256}`. UI: `portalStartCertifiedSigning`, then the browser goes to `signingUrl`. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/portal/contracts/:contractId/certified-signing/refresh` | Bodyless. `portal` `read`, contract in portal scope (404). Runs the re-fetch-and-apply step a notice runs. **200** `{status, outcome, contractStatus}` (`status`: `pending` · `completed` · `skipped` · `retry` · `refused`). A read authorization is enough: what it writes is decided entirely by the provider's re-fetched status. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/contracts/:contractId/certified-signing/refresh` | The staff counterpart: `contract` `read`. Same answer. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/webhooks/signatures/:provider` | **The provider's notice.** No session, no Cerbos. Unknown or switched-off provider **404**. **Authenticated by a SHARED CREDENTIAL ONLY** (VIDA's webhook has no HMAC; the simulator presents HTTP Basic with a credential generated in process memory), compared in constant time: a wrong or missing credential is **401 with nothing written**. The body `{eventId, event, envelopeId, partnerTrxId, signerRole?, occurredAt}` is a trigger only: the company comes from `partnerTrxId` (a reference naming no live company is acknowledged `200 {ok, ignored:"unknown_partner_ref"}` and dropped); the claim `INSERT INTO provider_events (… kind 'signature' …) ON CONFLICT (provider, event_id) DO NOTHING` and the outbox event `signature.notice.received` (stream `provider_event`) are one transaction; the answer is **200 `{ok:true}`**, or on a replay **200 `{ok:true, duplicate:true}`** with nothing reprocessed. **Processing** (the consumer, or the 60 s sweep): the envelope must be a contract of that company (else `ignored: unknown_envelope`, no status call); the envelope is **RE-FETCHED** from the provider and only that is written. It must name our envelope, our partner reference and the contract's `content_sha256` (else `ignored` with the reason, and the company's owners are told). Each signer the provider reports signed becomes a `contract_signatures` row with `provider`, `provider_envelope_id`, the contract's hash and the provider's `signedAt` (no IP hash or user agent: the provider holds that evidence). On completion the signed PDF and the certificate are downloaded and checked (the PAdES signature verified against the delivered certificate with the PV5-07 seal verifier, the certificate is the provider's, the exact signed content is embedded) BEFORE they are stored as `contract_certified_copy` (`application/pdf`) and `contract_certified_certificate` (`application/x-pem-file`), both with `sha256`, and the contract becomes `signed` in the same transaction. A notice that claims more than the provider says writes nothing (its claim is kept in the outcome text). The sweep also re-fetches every open certified envelope every 5 minutes, so a lost notice still records the signature. Activities: `certified_signed` per signature, `certified_completed` with the two file ids and hashes; each carries `simulated` and `provider`. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/portal/simulated-psre/envelopes/:envelopeId` | **The simulated PSrE's client page (review stage only; 404 while the flag is off).** `portal` `read`; the envelope's contract through `contractInPortalScope` (**404** for another client's contact or anyone out of scope). **200 `SimulatedEnvelopeView`:** `{envelopeId, provider:"simulated", label, simulated:true, notice:"Simulated certified signature: not a real PSrE signature", title, status:"pending" \| "completed", completedAt, contractId, clientId, contractStatus, contentSha256, documentFilename, documentContentType, documentSha256, documentText (a text document up to 256 KiB, else null), documentPath, signers:[{role, displayName, state, signerName, signerTitle, signedAt}], yourRole:"client", canSign, reason}`. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/portal/simulated-psre/envelopes/:envelopeId/document` | The simulator's own copy of the document, as an attachment (`nosniff`, sandbox CSP). Same reach as above. |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/portal/simulated-psre/envelopes/:envelopeId/sign` | Body `{agree:true, signerName, signerTitle?, documentSha256}`. `portal` `sign` → a person → portal scope (404) → signer capability (403) → body (400 `agree` / `signerName`, 400 `content_hash_required`, **409 `content_changed`** when the hash differs from the one the simulator holds) → contract not `sent` 409. Records the client's signature AT THE SIMULATOR (never in `contract_signatures`: only the re-fetch writes there), then the simulator sends its notice(s) to the webhook. **200** `{ok, simulated:true, outcome:"signed" \| "already_signed", completed, noticesDelivered}`. |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/simulated-psre/envelopes/:envelopeId` | **The countersigner's page.** `contract` `read`; the envelope's contract in this company (404). The same view with `yourRole:"countersigner"`; `canSign` only for whoever may countersign (an owner of this company or `platform_admin`; a soft Cerbos probe). |
| PROTOTYPED | GET | `/api/:t/simulated-psre/envelopes/:envelopeId/document` | As the portal one, for staff (`contract` `read`). |
| PROTOTYPED | POST | `/api/:t/simulated-psre/envelopes/:envelopeId/countersign` | Same body. **Cerbos `contract` `countersign` FIRST** (on the company, then on the contract): a `company_admin` gets **403** for any body; then a person (403 `signer_must_be_a_person`); then the body as above. Records our countersignature at the simulator and sends the notice(s). |

**The simulated PSrE (`src/signatures/simulated-psre.ts`).** In-process; it keeps its own store in `simulated_psre_envelopes` (FORCE RLS, tenant-scoped; no DELETE for the runtime role): its copy of the document by storage key and SHA-256, the signer slots, and on completion the signed PDF (storage key + SHA-256) and the PUBLIC certificate. The signed PDF is the agreement (a PDF's own pages, or a readable rendering of a text agreement), the exact signed bytes embedded as an attachment, an evidence page headed "SIMULATED CERTIFIED SIGNATURE: NOT A REAL PSrE SIGNATURE", the line "SIMULATED PSrE SIGNATURE (review stage) - not a real certified signature" stamped on every page, and a PAdES signature (PV5-07's code) by the simulator's key. **Key custody:** the key is generated in process memory on first use and never written anywhere (repo, database, env, file, log); its self-issued certificate (subject "SIMULATED PSrE (review stage) - not a certification authority") is stored with every document it signs, so each stays verifiable against its own certificate, and a restart only starts a new simulated identity. The notice credential is generated in memory too.

**Database rules (migration `202610150300`).** `contracts.signature_provider` / `provider_envelope_id`: both or neither, only on a certified contract with fixed content, one envelope per contract (partial unique), frozen once set (`PV5_CONTRACT_ENVELOPE_FIXED`). `contract_signatures`: a certified contract takes provider signatures only (`PV5_CERTIFIED_NEEDS_PROVIDER`), and a provider signature must name the contract's provider and envelope (`PV5_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH`). `files.role` gains `contract_certified_copy` and `contract_certified_certificate` (records under the PV5-07 role-file guard).

**Agents never sign.** Every signing route above refuses an agent or bot channel, an `actFor` call, and `automation` / `bot` accounts (403 `signer_must_be_a_person`); the D14 executable `contracts.countersign` refuses a certified contract at its precondition (`contract_certified_tier`); no MCP tool starts, signs or countersigns a certified envelope.
