**For the real PSrE (VIDA) adapter, later.** A text-only (`bodyMd`) agreement must be rendered to a PDF before VIDA can take it, and `content_sha256` covers the text, not that PDF: either require an attached PDF for certified contracts, or record the rendered PDF's hash beside it. The countersigner must be a named, KYC-verified person at envelope creation (the simulator binds the slot when someone signs). VIDA's status endpoint and retry rule are `[UNVERIFIED]` (blueprint §5); without a status endpoint the re-fetch becomes "download the signed document and verify it" on every notice. Certificate checks become chain validation to the PSrE's root, not a subject match.

## 31. Campaign parts — shared campaigns gain departments (DW-5a, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/modules/agency/` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite campaign-parts.test.ts written; needs the Linux CI gate)**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §7.1 and §7.3, ruling DW-D13 (campaigns are multi-department). One campaign (today's `agency_campaigns`, owned by the Office of the GM or a lead department) gains **parts**: one per taking-part department, each with an owner, a status, an optional budget allocation, and the work linked to it (the department's own SEO or Social campaigns, and the requests of §32). The plan's trap 6 says a part's money is ruled here, never in the UI: see §31.3.

### 31.1 Data model (one migration, timestamp-named after main's newest)

- **`agency_campaigns` gains**
  - `lead_unit_id text NULL`: the lead department's org-node id (the `projects.department_id` convention: free text, no FK). `NULL` means the Office of the GM, or the company, leads.
  - `starts_on date NULL` and `ends_on date NULL`, with `CHECK (ends_on IS NULL OR starts_on IS NULL OR ends_on >= starts_on)`.
- **`agency_campaign_parts`** (new):
  - Columns: `id uuid PK`, `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL → companies`, `campaign_id uuid NOT NULL → agency_campaigns`, and `unit_id text NOT NULL` (a **department** node id of this tenant's org tree).
  - Owner and status: `owner_id uuid NULL → users`, and `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned' CHECK (status IN ('planned','active','blocked','done','cancelled'))`.
  - Work fields: `brief text NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` (≤ 4,000 characters, also a CHECK) and `due_on date NULL`.
  - Money: `budget_minor bigint NULL CHECK (budget_minor IS NULL OR budget_minor >= 0)`.
  - Bookkeeping: `created_by uuid NULL → users`, `origin_site text NOT NULL`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `deleted_at`.
  - `UNIQUE (campaign_id, unit_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`: one part per department per campaign.
  - Index `(tenant_id, unit_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.
  - RLS: ENABLE plus FORCE, with the standard `tenant_isolation` policy on `app_current_tenants()`.
- **The department's own campaigns link to a part:**
  - `search_campaigns.agency_part_id uuid NULL → agency_campaign_parts(id)` and `social_campaigns.agency_part_id uuid NULL → agency_campaign_parts(id)`, each indexed `WHERE agency_part_id IS NOT NULL`.
  - A department campaign belongs to at most one part, and a part may have many.
  - The column is simply `NULL` where the agency module is off.
- **Requests (§32) link to a part** through `work_requests.campaign_part_id`.
- A part has **no currency column**. Its allocation is in the campaign's currency (§31.3).
- The campaign's client is its project's `client_id` (`agency_campaigns.project_id` is NOT NULL today). There is no new client column.

### 31.2 Authorization: new Cerbos kind `agency_campaign_part` (module `agency`)

A new kind is six artifacts, plus the pinned count literals (policy, `cerbos.ts` type and attribute allow-list, permission catalog, permission groups, the seeding migration with its DO-block self-assertion, and both role-bundle resolvers). Budget it as an IAM change, and restart and then probe Cerbos on the gate.

| Action | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | company_admin, manager, member, viewer (`inTenant && notLow`) | Mirrors `agency_campaign` `read` |
| `create`, `delete` | company_admin, manager | Adding or removing a department from a campaign |
| `allocate` | company_admin, manager | Any write that sets or changes `budgetMinor`. Kept apart from `update` so that a part's owner or head can never move money |
| `update` | company_admin, manager; **its own rule** for the part's owner (`request.resource.attr.ownerId == request.principal.id`); **its own rule** for `org_unit_lead` (`unitAncestors` of the part's `unit_id`, from `org_unit_closure`, the HIER-2 shape) | Status, owner, brief, due date and links. Each attribute-dependent rule stands alone, never mixed with a scope role (the HIER-2 authoring rule) |

- Permission catalog: `agency.campaign_part.read|create|update|delete|allocate`, plus the generic permission arm (`inTenant && notLow && inRoot`). The arm does not mirror the owner or lead rules.
- Resource attributes sent: `tenantId`, `module`, `ownerId`, `unitAncestors`. `ownerId` and `unitAncestors` must be added to the `resourcePayload()` allow-list.
- **`PATCH /campaigns/:id`** (below) uses the existing kind `agency_campaign` `update`, which company_admin and manager already hold.

### 31.3 Money rules (trap 6, decided here)

1. **The campaign budget is the one spend authority.** It is `agency_campaigns.budget_minor` plus `currency`. A part never has a currency of its own.
2. **A part's `budget_minor` is an allocation from it.** `NULL` means no allocation. Values are integers ≥ 0, and all arithmetic is `bigint` in SQL, never a float.
3. **An allocation needs a campaign budget.** Setting any part's `budgetMinor` while the campaign's `budget_minor` or `currency` is `NULL` answers **409 `campaign_has_no_budget`**.
4. **Allocations never exceed the budget.** The sum of `budget_minor` over the campaign's parts that are neither `cancelled` nor deleted must stay ≤ the campaign's `budget_minor`.
   - It is checked in the same transaction as the write, after `SELECT … FROM agency_campaigns WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`. That lock serialises concurrent allocations on one campaign.
   - A refusal is **409 `allocation_exceeds_budget`** with `{budgetMinor, allocatedMinor, requestedMinor}`.
5. **The campaign budget cannot drop below its allocations.** `PATCH /campaigns/:id` takes the same lock.
   - Lowering `budgetMinor` below the allocated sum, or clearing it while allocations exist, answers **409 `budget_below_allocations`**.
   - Changing `currency` while any allocation exists answers **409 `currency_locked_by_allocations`**.
6. **Cancelling a part releases its allocation.** A cancelled part's allocation leaves the sum. Moving the part out of `cancelled` checks rule 4 again.
7. **The server does the sums.** Reads return `allocatedMinor` and `unallocatedMinor`, computed in SQL. The UI never adds money.
8. **Spend is not rolled up.** A linked SEO campaign keeps its own `budget_minor` and `currency`, which may differ. A read lists it beside its part, but it is never added into the shared campaign's figures.

### 31.4 Routes (`api/:tenantId/modules/agency`, `AuthGuard` + `ModuleEnabledGuard("agency")`)

**Shared rules for every write in §31.4:**
- **Unit ids** are validated against this tenant's `company_org_structure` blob. The node must exist and be of kind `department`, or the answer is **400 `unit_invalid`**.
- **Owners** must be active members of this tenant, or the answer is **400 `owner_invalid`**.
- **Never from the body:** `tenantId`, `campaignId` and `status` defaults are never read from the body.

**Reads**
- `GET campaigns`: today's rows gain `leadUnitId`, `startsOn`, `endsOn`, `clientId` (from the project) and `partCount`.
  - **`?unitId=<dept>`** returns only the campaigns where that department has a live part or leads.
  - Each such row carries `part: {id, status, ownerId, ownerName, dueOn} | null`: `null` when the department only leads.
  - This feeds the Campaigns › Shared tab and the Overview's Campaigns block (DW-3f).
- `GET campaigns/:campaignId` (new; today the UI finds a campaign by listing them all):
  - **The campaign:** `{id, name, status, projectId, clientId, leadUnitId, leadUnitName, startsOn, endsOn}`.
  - **The money:** `money: {budgetMinor, currency, allocatedMinor, unallocatedMinor}`, where `unallocatedMinor` is `null` when there is no budget.
  - **Each part:** `parts: [{id, unitId, unitName, unitMissing, ownerId, ownerName, status, brief, dueOn, budgetMinor, links, requests}]`.
    - `links` is `{searchCampaigns: [{id, name, status, budgetMinor, currency}], socialCampaigns: [{id, name, status}]}`.
    - `requests` is `{open, delivered, declined}`, counted from §32.
  - **404 `campaign_not_found`** when the campaign is absent or in another tenant (RLS).
  - **Unit names come from the org blob.** A unit that has since left the tree reads `unitName: null` and `unitMissing: true`, never a stale name.

**Writes**
- **`PATCH campaigns/:campaignId`** takes `{name?, status?, budgetMinor?, currency?, leadUnitId?, startsOn?, endsOn?}`.
  - Gate: `agency_campaign` `update`.
  - Money rule 5 applies. `status` takes today's values (`active|paused|completed`).
- **`POST campaigns/:campaignId/parts`** takes `{unitId, ownerId?, brief?, dueOn?, budgetMinor?}` and answers **201 `{id}`**.
  - Gate: `agency_campaign_part` `create`, plus `allocate` when `budgetMinor` is present.
  - A live part for the same unit answers **409 `part_exists`**.
- **`PATCH campaigns/:campaignId/parts/:partId`** takes `{status?, ownerId?, brief?, dueOn?, budgetMinor?}`.
  - Gate: `update` for the non-money fields, and `allocate` when `budgetMinor` is present. Both are checked when both kinds of field are sent.
  - A part from another campaign answers **404 `part_not_found`**.
- **`DELETE campaigns/:campaignId/parts/:partId`** is a soft delete, gated by `delete`.
  - It answers **409 `part_has_links`** while any department campaign or request (§32) points at the part. Cancelling is the normal path.
- **`POST campaigns/:campaignId/parts/:partId/links`** takes `{kind: 'search_campaign' | 'social_campaign', refId}`.
  - Gate: part `update`, plus `read` on the child: `resource_search_campaign`, or `social_engagement` for a social campaign.
  - The child must be live in this tenant, or the answer is **400 `link_target_invalid`**.
  - A child already linked to another part answers **409 `already_linked`**.
  - When that module is off for the tenant, the answer is **409 `link_kind_unavailable`**.
- **`DELETE campaigns/:campaignId/parts/:partId/links/:kind/:refId`** removes a link. Gate: part `update`.

### 31.5 Side effects

- **Activity:** `writeActivity` on every write, with entity types `agency_campaign` and `agency_campaign_part`.
- **Outbox events** (in the write's own transaction, ids only): `agency.campaign.updated`, `agency.campaign_part.created`, `agency.campaign_part.updated`, `agency.campaign_part.deleted`.
- **Notifications:** `notify(…, "campaign_part.assigned", {title: "<Department> has a part in <campaign>", entityType: "agency_campaign_part", entityId, href: "/agency/<campaignId>"})`.
  - It goes to the owner when a part is created with one, and to the new owner when the owner changes.
  - It is best-effort and never fails the write.
- No MCP tools and no new rollup metrics in DW-5a.

### 31.6 Proofs required before DW-5a is ticked (Linux CI gate, real Postgres and Cerbos)

- **Money:** rules 3 to 6, each refused with its code. Two concurrent allocations on one campaign, which together exceed the budget, leave exactly one committed. Lowering the budget or changing the currency under allocations is refused.
- **Access:** a member reads but cannot create, allocate or delete. A part's owner updates status and brief, but `budgetMinor` answers 403. A manager does everything. Another tenant's campaign or part answers 404. A seeded `org_unit_lead` grant on the part's unit may update, and one on a sibling unit may not.
- **Org:** a division or unknown node id answers 400 `unit_invalid`. A unit removed from the tree reads as `unitMissing`.
- **Links:** linking another tenant's SEO campaign is 400. Linking a campaign that is already linked is 409. Deleting a part that has links is 409.
- **IAM:** the new kind's catalog, groups, bundles and the four count literals are green, and the policy is probed after a Cerbos restart.

### 31.7 Built (DW-5a, 2026-10-14)

Files: `migrations/202610140500_agency_campaign_parts.sql` (schema), `migrations/202610140510_iam_agency_campaign_part_permissions.sql` (IAM seed),
`src/modules/agency/agency-campaign-parts.service.ts` (money rules, parsers, org check, SQL helpers),
`src/modules/agency/agency.controller.ts` (the routes of §31.4), `src/modules/agency/index.ts` (the five permission keys),
`cerbos/policies/resource_agency_campaign_part.yaml` and four `perm_agency_campaign_part_*` roles in `derived_roles.yaml`,
`src/rbac/permission-catalog.json`, `permission-groups.json`, `role-permission-bundles.json` (regenerated), the four pinned count literals
(105 kinds / 451 pairs / 436 grantable / 101 non-exempt kinds), `src/http-error.filter.ts` (the additive `detail` field), `docs/modules/CAPABILITY-INVENTORY.md`.
Proof files: `agency-campaign-parts.service.test.ts` (36 pure unit tests, run locally), `cerbos-agency-campaign-part.test.ts` (static pin plus a live matrix),
`campaign-parts.test.ts` (the HTTP suite for every bullet of §31.6, including the concurrent-allocation race; DB and Cerbos, Linux gate only).

Deviations from §31, each deliberate:

1. **No permission mirror for `update`.** §31.2 says the generic arm "does not mirror the owner or lead rules"; the arm is wired for `read`, `create`, `delete` and `allocate` only. A `perm_*update` rule fails the permission-arm hazard scan (Pattern B: the owner rule is self-scoped) and the mirror-reach invariant (the lead rule is attribute-dependent), the same call `time_entry` makes. Consequence: the permission-native `owner` role holds the `update` key in its bundle but cannot act on it through Cerbos unless it also holds company_admin or manager.
2. **The owner rule is on `member`.** "Its own rule for the part's owner" is `derivedRoles: ["member"]` with `variables.owns`, so a viewer who owns a part still cannot update it. `member·agency.campaign_part.update` is a `selfScoped` pair in the bundles and the seed.
3. **The `org_unit_lead` rule carries `update` only** (no `read`), as §31.2 lists. A department head also holds `member` in practice.
4. **None of the five keys is `sensitive`.** `allocate` moves money but only within the campaign's own budget, and flagging it would route every department-head grant of `manager` through the sensitive-grant override path (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §12.2). Flip it additively if the owner wants it.
5. **Error carrier.** The contract's codes travel in `reason` (the `{error}` reshape keeps `error` as the prose message). The `{budgetMinor, allocatedMinor, requestedMinor}` figures of `allocation_exceeds_budget` travel in a new additive `detail` object, which `http-error.filter.ts` now forwards; it has the same only-when-set rule as `field`, `reason` and `existing`. `allocatedMinor` is the sum over the campaign's OTHER live, non-cancelled parts and `requestedMinor` is the part's new allocation.
6. **`GET campaigns/:campaignId` adds `linkAccess`** (`{searchCampaigns, socialCampaigns}`, each `ok | module_off | forbidden`). A link list is empty both when nothing is linked and when the caller may not read that kind of campaign or the module is off; the extra key keeps an empty list from reading as "nothing linked". The detail read needs `agency_campaign` `read` AND `agency_campaign_part` `read`; the list read needs the part `read` only when `?unitId=` is sent.
7. **`requests` counts and the request half of `part_has_links` were stubs; DW-5c replaced the seam (2026-10-14).** The two functions in the service (`requestCountsByPart`, `countRequestsOnPart`) now read `work_requests` (§32.1): `requests` is the real `{open, delivered, declined}` per part (a cancelled request counts in none of the three), and ANY request on a part, cancelled included, blocks the part's delete with 409 `part_has_links`. The DW-5a controller is unchanged. Proof: `src/core/work-requests.test.ts`, "campaign part requests".
8. **Linking a campaign that is already linked answers 409 `already_linked` even when it is linked to the SAME part** (one reading of "already linked"; no idempotent 201).
9. **`PATCH` part returns `{id}`, `DELETE` part and links return `{id}` / `{id, kind, refId}`** with 200; `PATCH campaigns/:id` returns `{id, money}`. `POST links` answers 201.
10. **Extra refusals the contract implies but does not name:** 400 `budget_invalid`, `date_invalid`, `dates_invalid`, `currency_invalid`, `brief_too_long`, `status_invalid`, `name_invalid`, `link_kind_invalid`, `nothing_to_update`; 404 `link_not_found` (unlinking something not linked); 409 `part_changed` (the part's owner moved between the authorization read and the locked write).
11. **Authorization runs before body validation** on every write (a caller who may not write gets 403 whatever they sent), and `unitAncestors` / `ownerId` are read from the part row, never from the body.

**UI (DW-5b, 2026-10-14).** Readers: `platform-ui/src/lib/campaigns-data.ts` (server-only, every read a `ReadResult`: 403 `forbidden`, 5xx and a module that is off `unavailable`, never an empty list), pure types and helpers in `lib/campaigns.ts` (refusal `reason` to sentence, money display from the server's minor units, typed-amount conversion), writes in `lib/campaignActions.ts` (a value, never a thrown refusal; the `detail` figures are read from `PlatformError.body`). Pages: `/departments/[deptId]/campaigns` (Campaigns › Shared, reads `GET campaigns?unitId=<dept>`; a department that only leads shows "Lead, no part"), `/departments/[deptId]/campaigns/social` (Social Media's Social campaigns tab: the §19 campaign list, create through `createCampaign`, and link or unlink into a shared campaign where the department has a part, reading each such campaign's detail to find which social campaign sits where), and `/agency/[campaignId]` (now `GET campaigns/:id`, a 404 is `notFound()`: the money block as returned, lead department and dates, and a Parts section that respects `linkAccess` and shows each part's `requests` counts). Controls are cosmetic and the server decides: the new UI capability `agency.campaign.manage` (company_admin, manager, owner, platform_admin) offers add or remove a department, set an allocation, and edit the campaign's budget, currency, lead and dates; a part's status, owner, brief and due date are also offered to the part's owner and to the department head (`isLeadOf` over the org tree, read only when it can change the answer). The UI never adds or subtracts money and uses `allocatedMinor` and `unallocatedMinor` as returned. No new endpoints.

---

## 32. Requests between departments (DW-5c, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/work-requests.{controller,service}.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite work-requests.test.ts written; needs the Linux CI gate)**

Plan: §7.2 and §7.3, ruling DW-D14 (Creatives supplies the assets, and Web Dev handles anything that needs a software engineer). **A request is the ask; the work stays where each receiver already works.** That is why there is no second queue:

- **An asset request (`kind: 'assets'`) is a PM task.** The task is owned by the receiving department (`assignee {kind: 'department', refId: <unit>}`), in that department's intake project (§32.1). It therefore appears on the receiver's board through today's `belongs()`. Once someone is made responsible for it, it appears in that person's Needs you through today's PM-task leg of the queue.
- **An engineering request (`kind: 'engineering'`) is a Web Dev change request** with `source = 'internal'` (the MI-05 intake). It lands in Web Dev › Requests beside client maintenance and goes through today's triage (`pm_task`, `mini_run`).
- **One thin row, `work_requests`, carries the ask:** who asked, from which department, to which department, by when, for which campaign part, and the request form. It also carries the ask's own lifecycle (`open`, `delivered`, `declined`, `cancelled`). Progress inside that lifecycle is read live from the work item and is never copied.

### 32.1 Data model (one migration)

- **`work_requests`**:
  - Identity: `id uuid PK`, `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL → companies`, `kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('assets','engineering'))`.
  - Routing:
    - `to_unit_id text NOT NULL`: the receiving department node.
    - `from_unit_id text NULL`: the requester's department, derived by the server (§32.3). `NULL` means the requester sits in no department, for example an owner.
    - `requested_by uuid NOT NULL → users`.
  - The ask: `title text NOT NULL` (1 to 200 characters), `brief text NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` (≤ 10,000 characters, PAN and national ids scrubbed like change requests, plain text), `needed_by date NULL`, `campaign_part_id uuid NULL → agency_campaign_parts`, and `form jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` (§32.4).
  - Lifecycle: `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open','delivered','declined','cancelled'))`, `closed_by uuid NULL → users`, `closed_at timestamptz NULL`, `decline_reason text NULL` (≤ 2,000 characters).
  - The work item: `pm_task_id uuid NULL → pm_tasks` and `change_request_id uuid NULL → webdev_change_requests`.
    - `CHECK ((kind = 'assets' AND pm_task_id IS NOT NULL AND change_request_id IS NULL) OR (kind = 'engineering' AND change_request_id IS NOT NULL AND pm_task_id IS NULL))`.
    - `UNIQUE (pm_task_id)` and `UNIQUE (change_request_id)`.
  - Bookkeeping: `origin_site text NOT NULL`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`.
  - Indexes `(tenant_id, to_unit_id, status)`, `(tenant_id, from_unit_id, status)` and `(tenant_id, requested_by)`.
  - RLS: ENABLE plus FORCE, with `tenant_isolation`.
- **`work_request_assets`** links delivered assets:
  - Columns: `request_id uuid → work_requests`, `asset_id uuid → creative_assets`, `tenant_id`, `added_by uuid → users`, `added_at`. PK `(request_id, asset_id)`.
  - RLS as above. An asset may serve more than one request.
- **`work_request_intakes`** holds each receiving department's requests project, which serves BOTH kinds (the asset task lives in it, and an engineering request's change request names it as its `project_id`):
  - Columns: `tenant_id`, `unit_id text`, `project_id uuid → projects`, `created_at`. PK `(tenant_id, unit_id)`. RLS as above.
  - The service creates the project lazily on the department's first request of either kind, as an internal project: `is_internal = true`, `department_id = unit_id`, named `"<Department> · Requests"`, with no client.
  - It uses `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and then a re-select, so two concurrent first requests create one project.
  - The table leaves `projects` untouched and is the future home of per-department request settings (SLA, accepted kinds).

### 32.2 Authorization: new Cerbos kind `work_request` (core)

Six artifacts, as in §31.2.

| Action | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | company_admin, manager, member, viewer (`inTenant && notLow`) | Same reach as `pm_task` `read`: every member already reads every PM task |
| `create` | company_admin, manager, member | Any workspace can ask (§7.2). Viewers cannot |
| `cancel` | company_admin, manager; **its own rule** for the requester (`request.resource.attr.requestedBy == request.principal.id`) | Only while `open` (409 otherwise) |
| `deliver` | company_admin, manager; **its own rule** for `org_unit_lead` over `to_unit_id` (`unitAncestors`); **its own rule** for the work's assignees (`request.principal.id in request.resource.attr.assigneeIds`: the PM task's responsible person and any person assignees) | Assets only |
| `decline` | company_admin, manager; **its own rule** for `org_unit_lead` over `to_unit_id` | Assets only. Engineering requests are declined by Web Dev triage (§32.6) |

- `EFFECT_DENY` on `create`, `cancel`, `deliver` and `decline` when `principal.attr.kind in ['automation','bot']`, after the PV-4 precedent. Agents may triage later, under the separate AI plan.
- Resource attributes sent: `tenantId`, `requestedBy`, `assigneeIds`, `unitAncestors`. All of them are new entries in the `resourcePayload()` allow-list.
- Catalog: `core.work_request.read|create|cancel|deliver|decline`, plus the generic permission arm. The arm does not mirror the requester, assignee or lead rules.
- **The deliberate widening:**
  - `webdev_change_request` `create` stays manager-only. This route writes the change-request row itself (`source = 'internal'`), so any member can ask Web Dev, but only through this envelope.
  - Likewise, the asset task is created by the service with a department assignee, which a member could not do through `POST pm/tasks` (that needs `manage`).
  - Both bypasses are confined to this service and covered by §32.7.

### 32.3 Server-derived fields (never read from the body)

- **`requested_by`** is the principal.
- **`from_unit_id`** is the requester's open primary membership in this tenant (`org_unit_memberships`, `is_primary` and `valid_to` NULL or ≥ today).
  - It is walked up the org blob to its **department** ancestor, so a person in a division counts for that division's department.
  - It is `NULL` when there is no membership.
- **`status`**, `closed_*`, `pm_task_id`, `change_request_id` and `tenant_id` are server-derived as well.
- **`to_unit_id`** must be a department node in this tenant's org blob, or the answer is **400 `to_unit_invalid`**. Same company only in v1: a group company that has no Creatives of its own cannot ask another company's Creatives yet (§32.8).

### 32.4 The request form (`form`, validated per kind; unknown keys refused)

- **`assets`** takes:
  - `deliverables`: 1 to 10 items of `{format: 'image'|'video'|'copy'|'document'|'other', size: string ≤ 60 (for example "1080×1350"), quantity: 1..50}`;
  - `channel?: string ≤ 60`;
  - `references?`: 0 to 10 `http(s)` URLs, each ≤ 500 characters;
  - `notes?: string ≤ 2,000`.
- **`engineering`** takes `kind: 'content'|'design'|'feature'|'bug'` (the change-request kinds, required) and `affectedUrl?` (an `http(s)` URL ≤ 500 characters).
- Any failure answers **400 `form_invalid`** with `{field}`. The form is shown back verbatim as data and never interpreted.

### 32.5 Routes (`api/:tenantId/requests`, `AuthGuard`)

**Writes**
- **`POST requests`** takes `{kind, toUnitId, title, brief?, neededBy?, campaignPartId?, form}` and answers **201 `{id, work: {type: 'pm_task'|'change_request', id}}`**. Gate: `create`. Everything happens in one transaction.
  - **`assets`:** the service ensures the intake project, then creates the PM task through the PM module's exported `normalizePmTaskInput` and `createPmTaskInTx`:
    - title = the request title;
    - description = the brief, plus a plain-text summary of the form and a "Requested by <name> (<department>)" line;
    - `dueDate` = `neededBy`; priority `normal`;
    - assignee `{kind: 'department', refId: toUnitId, refName}`.
  - **`engineering`:** the service inserts the change request: `source 'internal'`, `kind` = `form.kind`, `title`, `body` = the brief, `affected_url` from the form, `project_id` = the receiving department's intake project (the same one assets use, ensured as above), `requested_by` = the principal, and status `new`. Web Dev's `pm_task` triage therefore needs no extra input and lands the task in "<Department> · Requests". It emits `webdev.change_request.created` as the internal-create route does.
  - **Then** it inserts the `work_requests` row.
  - **Module checks:** when the receiving module is off for the tenant (`pm` for assets, `webdev` for engineering), the answer is **409 `request_kind_unavailable`**.
  - **Campaign part:** `campaignPartId` must be a live, not-cancelled part in this tenant, or the answer is **400 `campaign_part_invalid`**.
- **`POST requests/:id/deliver`** takes `{assetIds: uuid[1..20]}`. Gate: `deliver`. Assets only, or **409 `wrong_kind_for_action`**.
  - Each asset must be a live `creative_assets` row in this tenant, or the answer is **400 `asset_invalid`**.
  - It links the assets, idempotently.
  - On an `open` request it sets `delivered`, `closed_by` and `closed_at`, and moves the PM task to its project's done status: the project's status-registry done row when the status set is materialized, else `'done'`, the same rule as the PM reads.
  - On an already `delivered` request it only adds assets ("deliver more").
  - Any other status answers **409 `request_not_open`**.
- **`POST requests/:id/decline`** takes `{reason}` (1 to 2,000 characters). Gate: `decline`. Assets only. `open` only.
  - It sets `declined` and closes the PM task as above, so a declined ask leaves the board.
- **`POST requests/:id/cancel`** takes no body. Gate: `cancel`. `open` only.
  - **Assets:** it closes the PM task as above.
  - **Engineering:** cancelling is allowed only while the change request is `new`. Otherwise the answer is **409 `already_in_progress`**, because Web Dev has accepted the work. The change request is set `declined` with `declined_reason = 'Cancelled by the requester'`.

**Reads.** Every read is gated by `read`. Unit names come from the org blob; a unit gone from the tree reads `null`, with `unitMissing: true`.
- **`GET requests?box=incoming|sent|mine&unitId=&status=open|closed|all&kind=`:**
  - `incoming` and `sent` need `unitId`, a department node (400 otherwise). They filter `to_unit_id` and `from_unit_id` respectively. `mine` filters `requested_by`.
  - The default `status` is `open`.
  - Order: `incoming` lists the oldest first (the oldest waiting is the one to act on); `sent` and `mine` list the newest first. At most 200 rows.
  - Row shape:
    - the ask: `{id, kind, title, status, neededBy, createdAt, closedAt}`;
    - routing: `fromUnit: {id, name} | null`, `toUnit: {id, name}`, `requestedBy: {id, name}`;
    - the campaign: `campaign: {id, name, partId} | null`;
    - the work item, live: `work`.
      - For a PM task: `{type: 'pm_task', id, projectId, status, isDone, responsibleName}`.
      - For a change request: `{type: 'change_request', id, status, route}`.
      - A work item that has been deleted reads `work: null`, which the UI shows as "work removed".
    - `assetCount`.
- **`GET requests/summary?unitId=`** returns `{incoming: {open, oldestOpenAt}, sent: {open}}`.
  - It feeds the Overview's Requests block (DW-3f) and the "requests waiting" pulse tiles.
  - It is an honest reader: it answers with numbers or fails. The UI shows a failure as "unavailable", never 0.
- **`GET requests/:id`** returns the row above, plus `brief`, `form` and `declineReason`, plus `assets: [{id, name, contentType, href}]`.
  - `href` is the existing creative-asset content route.
  - Another tenant's request answers **404 `request_not_found`**.

### 32.6 Keeping the ask and the work in step (no stored copy of progress)

- **Assets:** progress is read live from the PM task. If the receiver finishes the task without delivering, the ask stays `open` and the read shows `isDone: true`. The UI then offers Deliver; the server does not auto-deliver an empty request.
- **Engineering:** the change-request routes call `syncWorkRequestFromChangeRequest(c, changeRequestId)` inside their own transactions: triage, verify and unverify.
  - Triage `decline` sets the ask to `declined` (with the triage reason).
  - `verify` (status `verified`) sets it to `delivered`. Note that nothing in the codebase writes `done` on a change request (see the comment above `verify` in `webdev-change-requests.controller.ts`), so `verified` is the only "finished" state.
  - `unverify` (`verified` back to `in_progress`) reopens the ask: `open`, with `closed_*` cleared.
  - Every other change-request status leaves the ask `open`; the read shows it live.
  - A change request that came from no `work_requests` row is untouched.

### 32.7 Side effects

- **Activity:** `writeActivity` on every write, with entity type `work_request`.
- **Outbox events** (in the write's transaction, ids only, never text): `work_request.created`, `work_request.delivered`, `work_request.declined`, `work_request.cancelled`.
- **Notifications:** best-effort, and a failed notification never fails the write. Types are deliberately not `mention`-shaped, so they never double into Needs you. Assigned work reaches Needs you through the PM task.
  - **`request.received`** goes to the receiving department's heads, the active holders of a `positions.is_lead = true` seat on `to_unit_id` (migration 0109). It links to `/departments/<toUnit>/requests`. With no head, nobody is notified, and the board still shows the request.
  - **`request.delivered`** and **`request.declined`** go to the requester and link to `/requests/<id>`.
  - **`request.cancelled`** goes to the PM task's responsible person, if any.

### 32.8 Known limits (each on the board, none hidden)

- **Same company only.** Routing through the group's service assignments (ORG-13) is out of DW-5 (owner, 2026-10-14): requests are offered to agency-pack companies only, and only the agency company has Creatives and Web Dev today. It is recorded as a later item under DW-10 on the board.
- **Deleting a linked PM task is refused (guard built, 2026-10-14).** `DELETE /api/:t/pm/tasks/:id` answers **409 `task_has_open_request`** with `detail: {requestId}` while an `open` ask points at the task, so the receiver declines or delivers instead. Closed asks (delivered, declined, cancelled) do not hold the task. The task page's Delete now shows that refusal in place (`components/pm/DeleteTaskButton.tsx`); it used to redirect as if the delete had worked. Proof: `work-requests.test.ts` "PM delete guard". A task removed before the guard, or by a direct database change, still reads `work: null`.
- **No attachments on the request itself.** References are links (`form.references`). File attachments come with DW-8h.
- **Asset versions and review rounds** are DW-6h. Delivery here links finished library assets.

### 32.9 Proofs required before DW-5c is ticked (Linux CI gate)

- **Creation:**
  - A member creates both kinds; a viewer gets 403, and a bot or automation principal gets 403.
  - The asset task appears in the receiver department's tasks (`assignee.kind = 'department'`) and in the intake project.
  - Two concurrent first requests to one department make one intake project.
  - The engineering request appears in `GET webdev/change-requests` with `source 'internal'`.
- **The lifecycle:**
  - The assignee delivers. A member who is neither assignee nor head gets 403.
  - A seeded `org_unit_lead` on the receiving unit declines; one on a sibling unit gets 403.
  - The requester cancels only while `open`; another member gets 403.
  - An engineering cancel after triage answers 409.
  - Triage decline, verify and unverify move the ask through `syncWorkRequestFromChangeRequest`.
- **Isolation and derivation:**
  - Another tenant's request, part, asset or unit answers 404 or 400 as listed.
  - `from_unit_id` resolves a division member to their department, and is `NULL` for an unplaced owner.
- **Notifications:** recipients exactly as in §32.7, and none goes to the actor.
- **IAM:** the new kind's six artifacts and the count literals are green, and the policy is probed after a Cerbos restart.

### 32.10 Built (DW-5c, 2026-10-14)

Files: `migrations/202610140600_work_requests.sql` (schema), `migrations/202610140610_iam_work_request_permissions.sql` (IAM seed),
`src/core/work-requests.service.ts` (form validator, status rules, org walk, intake project, sync, reads and SQL helpers),
`src/core/work-requests.controller.ts` (the routes of §32.5), `src/modules/pm/pm.controller.ts` (one new export, `closePmTaskInTx`),
`src/core/webdev-change-requests.controller.ts` (the three sync hooks of §32.6 and nothing else),
`src/modules/agency/agency-campaign-parts.service.ts` (the DW-5a seam), `src/app.module.ts` (registration),
`cerbos/policies/resource_work_request.yaml` and `perm_work_request_{read,create}` in `derived_roles.yaml`, `src/rbac/cerbos.ts` (`requestedBy`, `assigneeIds`),
`src/rbac/permission-catalog.json`, `permission-groups.json`, `role-permission-bundles.json` (regenerated), the four pinned count literals
(106 kinds / 456 pairs / 441 grantable / 102 non-exempt kinds), `docs/PERMISSION-CONTRACT.md` §36, `docs/modules/CAPABILITY-INVENTORY.md`.
Proof files: `work-requests.service.test.ts` (39 pure unit tests, run locally), `cerbos-work-request.test.ts` (static pin plus a live matrix),
`work-requests.test.ts` (the HTTP suite for every bullet of §32.9, including the concurrent first-request race; DB and Cerbos, Linux gate only).

Deviations from §32, each deliberate:

1. **The asset task's department assignee is set after `normalizePmTaskInput`.** PM's `validAssignee` accepts an assignee only when it names a responsible person, which a department with nobody on it yet cannot. The service therefore normalizes everything else through PM's own function, then sets `assignee = {kind: 'department', refId, refName, responsibleId: null, responsibleName: null}` and calls `createPmTaskInTx`. A null `responsibleId` is read as "nobody yet" by PM's dual-write (no responsible row, no drift), its assignment ledger (`responsible_id` is a uuid column, so `""` would be a 500) and Needs you; setting someone responsible later is an ordinary PM assignee patch.
2. **`closePmTaskInTx` (new PM export) is the one "move a task to its project's done status" helper**, reused by deliver, decline and cancel. It uses the project's effective status set: the materialized registry's first `is_done` row by position, else the synthesized `done`. It sets progress 100, emits `pm.task.updated` (`wasDone`/`isDoneNow`) and promotes dependents exactly as `patchTask` does. It never throws for an ordinary state: a task already done, deleted, or in a project whose registry has no done row is reported and left, and the ask still moves.
3. **The permission arm covers `read` and `create` only.** `cancel`, `deliver` and `decline` have no mirror (the requester and assignee rules are self-scoped; the head rules are attribute-dependent). Verified by experiment: adding a `decline` mirror fails `iam-04-reg1-mirror-reach-invariant` (`work_request.decline` held by `org_unit_lead` is narrower than the mirror). Same call as DW-5a's `update`. `owner` therefore holds all five keys and reaches only `read` and `create` through Cerbos unless it also holds `company_admin` or `manager`. None of the five keys is `sensitive`.
4. **The intake FK is DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED** (tenant-scoped composite `(project_id, tenant_id)`), so the service can insert the intake row first and create the project only when it won the insert. A loser creates nothing and re-selects. If the intake's project was later deleted, the answer is 409 `intake_project_unavailable`.
5. **Two lifecycle CHECKs on `work_requests`** (a closed ask carries `closed_at`, an open one does not; a declined one carries its reason). `change_request_id` and `campaign_part_id` are plain FKs (their parents have no `(id, tenant_id)` unique); `pm_task_id` is the tenant-scoped composite.
6. **Error carrier.** The contract's codes travel in `reason` and figures in `detail` (the DW-5a shape). Codes beyond the ones §32 names: 400 `body_invalid`, `kind_invalid`, `title_invalid`, `brief_invalid`, `brief_too_long`, `date_invalid`, `reason_invalid`, `box_invalid`, `status_invalid`, `unit_invalid` (a box filter or summary that does not name a department); 400 `asset_invalid` also covers a malformed `assetIds` list (field `assetIds`; `detail.invalid` lists unknown ids); 404 `request_not_found`; 409 `request_not_open` (`detail.status`), `intake_project_unavailable`. `form_invalid` carries `field` as `form.<key>` or `form.deliverables[<i>].<key>`.
7. **Authorization runs before body validation** on every write; `requestedBy`, `assigneeIds` and `unitAncestors` are read from the request row and its task, never from the body. When the request is absent (or another tenant's), a caller who may not even read requests is answered 403 first, so the 404 is never an existence oracle for an outsider.
8. **Text is scrubbed like change requests** (`scrubText`: PAN, national ids and e-mail addresses) in the title, the brief, `form.notes` and the decline reason, and NULs are stripped (plain text). References and URLs are not scrubbed.
9. **Unit objects always carry `unitMissing`** (`{id, name, unitMissing}`), not only when the unit has left the tree. `GET requests/summary` requires `unitId` and answers 400 `unit_invalid` without a department.
10. **Events and notifications beyond the letter of §32.7.** A reopen (unverify) emits `work_request.reopened`, a fifth event type, so the outbox shows the move. "Deliver more" emits `work_request.delivered` with `more: true` and notifies the requester again (`request.delivered`, "More assets were delivered"). The change-request routes no longer double-notify a staff requester (see the review round below).
11. **`closed_by` is the person who delivered, declined or cancelled** (for an engineering request, the triager or verifier); the ask has no separate `created_by`, since `requested_by` is the principal.

Review round (2026-10-14):

- **Engineering requests carry a project.** The intake project serves both kinds, so `ensureIntakeProject` runs for an engineering request too and its id is written to the change request's `project_id`. Web Dev's `pm_task` triage works with no extra input (suite: `work-requests.test.ts`, "route pm_task"); `mini_run` still works.
- **A deliberate, scoped change to the change-request routes.** On triage decline and verify ONLY, when the change request carries a work request, its `requested_by` is dropped from the recipients of `webdev.change_request.declined` / `.verified` (their `/portal/requests` href is wrong for a staff requester, and `request.declined` / `request.delivered` already tells them). Client recipients are untouched; a change request with no work request notifies exactly as before.

Note:

- `campaignPartId` is context for the ask, not a routing rule: the part's department is not required to match `toUnitId`.

**UI (DW-5c UI, DW-5f and DW-5h, 2026-10-14).** Readers: `platform-ui/src/lib/requests-data.ts` (server-only, every read a `ReadResult`: 403 `forbidden`, 5xx, a 4xx and a route that is not served `unavailable`, never an empty list; a 404 on `GET requests/:id` is `notFound()`), pure types, normalisers and helpers in `lib/requests.ts` (every typed `reason` of this section as a sentence, `requestErrorText`; the request form model and a client-side validator that mirrors §32.4 bound for bound and uses the server's `form.deliverables[0].size` field names), writes in `lib/requestActions.ts` (create, deliver, decline, cancel: a value, never a thrown refusal; they revalidate `/requests`, `/requests/<id>` and the `/departments` layout). Pages: `/requests` (My requests, `box=mine`, open by default with a Closed and an All switch), `/requests/new?to=creatives|web-dev` (the receiving department is the active company's department whose workspace is that key, found with `departmentForWorkspace` over the shell's own `workspaceFor` name match; no such department says so and offers no form; the org chart is read first, so an unreadable tree is "unavailable", never "no Creatives department"; the kind follows the target, `assets` or `engineering`; the campaigns offered are `GET campaigns?unitId=<receiving department>` rows with a live part, sent as `campaignPartId`), `/requests/[id]` (the ask, its status, the work item read live with `work: null` shown as "The work item was removed", brief and form as plain text, `http`/`https`-only reference links, delivered assets, the decline reason, and the actions) and `/departments/[deptId]/requests/sent` (DW-5h, `box=sent&unitId=<dept>`). `/departments/[deptId]/requests` (Incoming) is untouched. `/requests` and everything under it is area `shared` (§2.3 of the plan). Controls are cosmetic and the server decides (a 403 or 409 renders as a sentence): Cancel to the requester while `open` (an engineering request only while its change request is `new`); Deliver and "Deliver more" (assets only) to a manager or the receiving department's head, or to one of the work's assignees (the PM task's responsible person, a person assignee or a contributor, read with `GET pm/tasks/:id`; an unreadable task is never assumed to make the caller an assignee); Decline (assets only, `open` only, with a reason) to a manager or the head. The new UI capability `work_request.decide` mirrors `core.work_request.deliver` + `decline` (`all`): company_admin, manager and platform_admin by role, `org_unit_lead` through `canInUnit` over the receiving department's path. `owner` is deliberately left out: its bundle carries both keys but the policy's permission arm honours only `read` and `create` (deviation 3), so the parity register carries a sourced `KNOWN_NON_DRIFT` entry. The registry gains Requests › Sent in the SEO, Social Media and Office of the GM workspaces (and Creatives, where Incoming and Delivered stay with DW-5d), and the "Ask Creatives for assets" and "Ask Web Dev" quick actions lose their ticket and are gated by a new gate kind, `hasWorkspace` (evaluated in `gateAllows` from `GateContext.workspaces`, the keys `workspaceKeysOf` reads off the departments the shell already resolved; unknown hides). One new route, not a backend one: `GET /api/creative-assets/:assetId` (`app/api/creative-assets/[assetId]/route.ts`) proxies the platform's `creative/assets/:id/content` with the caller's session and the same four download headers as `/api/files/:fileId`, because the `href` §32.5 returns is the platform's own path, which a browser cannot call. No new endpoints on the platform. DW-5d and DW-5e (2026-10-14): `/departments/[deptId]/requests` follows the department's workspace key (the shell's `workspaceFor` match): Creatives shows Incoming (`box=incoming&kind=assets`, open, oldest first), Web Dev keeps the MI-05 triage queue and adds an Origin column (a UI-side join of `box=incoming&kind=engineering&status=all` rows by `work.id` to the change request id; a failed read says "Unavailable", never blank), and any other department is unchanged; `/departments/[deptId]/requests/delivered` lists `status=closed` rows filtered to `delivered`, newest first, with a note counting the declined or cancelled ones it leaves out.

## 33. Department filters: a department's clients, deliverables and projects (DW-6d, DW-6g, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/department-filter.ts` (new), `modules/clients/clients.controller.ts`, `core/client-work.controller.ts`, `core/core.controller.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `core/department-filter.api.test.ts` + unit `core/department-filter.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate)**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §4.2 (DW-6d, DW-6g). Every agency workspace has a Clients row (§4), and Web Dev's Build row has a Deliverables tab. Both need "this department's" rows. There is no department column on `clients` or `deliverables`, so this section defines the one link they have and one query parameter that uses it. No migration, no new Cerbos kind.

### 33.1 What "the department's" means

- **Projects are the link.** A department owns a project through `projects.department_id`: an org-node id, free text, no FK (migration `0029`). It is the only department link a client or a deliverable has.
- **The node and everything under it.** `departmentId=<node>` matches a project whose `department_id` is that node or any node under it in the company's org tree:
  - `p.department_id = $node OR p.department_id IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM org_unit_closure WHERE tenant_id = $tenant AND ancestor_id = $node)`;
  - `org_unit_closure` (migration `0101`) is rebuilt on every org-tree save and includes the node itself at depth 0;
  - the extra equality keeps the node's own projects for a company whose closure has not been rebuilt yet.
- **One company only.**
  - Node ids are unique only per company, and every query runs under `withTenants([tenantId])`, so a node id from another company matches nothing.
  - Clients a department serves for another group company through a service assignment are not listed. This is a default the owner may overrule (plan §4.2), and DW-5 takes the same line for requests (§32.8).
- **Which projects count.**
  - A deleted project (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`) does not count.
  - The project's status does not matter. A client whose projects with the department are all finished is still one of its clients.
- **Clients with no project are invisible here.** A client served only through an engagement or a site, with no project, is not one of any department's clients. The department's Clients page says so (§33.4).

### 33.2 The parameter

- `departmentId` is optional on the three lists in §33.3.
- It is parsed **after** `authorize`, so a denial stays a denial, whatever the query string.
- **Absent or empty:** no filter. The list is exactly what it is today.
- **Present:** trimmed, then 1 to 200 characters with no control characters. Anything else answers **400** `{ error, field: "departmentId" }`.
- **An id that names no node** returns an empty list, never a 400 or a 404. That is the same as `?clientId=` for a client with no rows.
- **A repeated parameter** (`?departmentId=a&departmentId=b`) is ambiguous and answers the same 400.
- **It is a filter, not a boundary** (the rule in `core/client-filter.ts`).
  - It narrows what is displayed. The caller could already read every row unfiltered, and each list's authorisation is unchanged.
  - Do not merge it with portal scope, or with any authorisation helper.
- **One helper,** `core/department-filter.ts`:
  - `parseDepartmentFilter(raw)` returns `{ kind: "all" }` or `{ kind: "unit", nodeId }`, and throws the 400.
  - `departmentFilterSql(filter, column, tenantParam, nextParam)` returns `{ sql, params }`, shaped like `clientFilterSql`. `tenantParam` is the placeholder the caller already bound to the company id; `nextParam` is the next free placeholder, which takes the node id (`params` is that one value; "all" yields `TRUE` and none).
  - Every list uses it. Nobody writes the closure subquery by hand.

### 33.3 The lists

| Method | Path | Change | Authorisation (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/:t/clients?departmentId=` | Clients with at least one project matching §33.1: `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects p WHERE p.client_id = cl.id AND p.deleted_at IS NULL AND <filter on p.department_id>)`. Same row shape. | `client` · `read`; module `clients` |
| GET | `/api/:t/deliverables?departmentId=` | Combines with `projectId` and `clientId` (AND). Matches on the deliverable's **project** (`dp.department_id`), the way `clientId` already does; a deliverable whose project is missing, or deleted (`dp.deleted_at`), never matches. Same row shape. | `deliverable` · `read` |
| GET | `/api/:t/projects?departmentId=` | Combines with `clientId` (AND). Same row shape. | `project` · `read` |

MCP hub tools are unchanged by this section.

### 33.4 UI

- **Readers.** In `lib/entities.ts`, `listClients`, `listDeliverables` and `listProjects` take an optional `departmentId`. For the new pages they are read as `ReadResult`, so a failed read says "unavailable", never "no clients".
- **DW-6d: the Clients row.** The page is `/departments/[deptId]/clients`. It needs an `AREA_RULES` entry if `areaFor` does not already cover it.
  - It shows the department's clients, with name, status and business type, each linking to `/clients/[id]`.
  - It also shows how many of the department's projects each client has. That count comes from one `listProjects({ departmentId })` read, never one read per client.
  - An empty list reads "No clients with projects in this department yet", with one line saying the list comes from the department's projects.
  - The registry's `CLIENTS_ROW` and its tab drop the `DW-6d` ticket. The row keeps its gate (`agencyRow: clients`).
- **DW-6g: Web Dev › Build › Deliverables.**
  - The placeholder is replaced by `listDeliverables({ departmentId })`: name, project (linked), client, status and due date, ordered as the list already is.
  - An empty list says no deliverables are recorded on the department's projects, and links to `/deliverables/new`.
- **Not in this section.** The department console's owned-projects reader (`getOwnedProjectsPm` in `lib/departments.ts`) still matches exactly, in the browser. Switching it to `?departmentId=` would also widen DW-3f's Projects block to the units under the department, so that switch is DW-3's call.

### 33.5 Tests (the Linux CI gate: Postgres and Cerbos)

- **Unit:** `parseDepartmentFilter`. Absent, empty and whitespace mean all; 200 characters is accepted; 201 characters and a control character answer 400.
- **HTTP suite:** one company with a department node, a division under it and a second department. Projects sit at the department, at the division, at the other department, and one is deleted. Each project has a client and a deliverable. The suite checks:
  - `?departmentId=<department>` lists the clients and deliverables of the department's and the division's projects. It lists nothing from the other department, nothing whose only project is deleted, and nothing with no project.
  - `?departmentId=<division>` lists only the division's.
  - The same node id used in a second company matches nothing of the first.
  - Absent gives the same rows as today.
  - It combines with `clientId` and `projectId`.
  - A caller refused `read` gets 403 even with a malformed `departmentId`.
- **The closure is built by the real org save path** (`putOrg`), not inserted by hand, so the suite proves the tree the product writes.

## 34. Pull requests and CI status on tasks (DW-6f, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/github-pull-requests.ts` (new), `core/github-webhook-handlers.ts`, `modules/pm/pm.controller.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (suites github-pull-requests.test.ts, github-pull-requests.db.test.ts and PullRequests.test.tsx; the DB suite needs the Linux CI gate)**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §4.2 (DW-6f) and §14.1 ("launch and return": a pull request appears on the task). Code is written outside the ERP, in VS Code and Claude Code. Its result comes back as the pull requests and their CI status on the task the work is for.

### 34.1 What exists, and what this adds

- **What exists:**
  - The GitHub App webhook receiver already handles `pull_request` and `workflow_run` (`github-webhook-handlers.ts`, `handlePullRequest`, `handleWorkflowRun`).
  - Each delivery is recorded once (`github_webhook_deliveries`) and stamped with the org tenant (`GITHUB_REPO_SYNC_TENANT_ID`, the company that owns the GitHub organisation).
  - Today these events only bump repo-level counters on `github_repos` and write `work_activity` rows. **No pull request is stored, and nothing links a pull request to a task.**
- **What links them:** a task already has a key. A project has a `short_code` (unique per company, migration `0050`), and a PM task has a `seq` within its project. So `WEB-12` names one task.
- **This section adds:**
  - one table of pull requests, filled by the existing handlers;
  - a rule that links a pull request to a task through that key;
  - one read on the task.
- **No new Cerbos kind.** The read is authorised exactly like the task (`pm_task` · `read`).

### 34.2 v1 is one company: the company that owns the GitHub organisation

- GitHub data stays in the org tenant (the GitHub tenant-scope ruling, `docs/blueprints/github-tenant-scope-ruling.md` §0).
- A pull request links only to a task **in that same company**. That is where Web Dev's projects live.
- So the link, the table and the read all sit in one tenant. The read is an ordinary `withTenants([tenantId])` query, and it never crosses a tenant.
- **Gap that stays visible:** a task in another company is never linked. Its panel says so (§34.6). Linking across group companies needs the tenant-scope ruling's resolver and is later work.

### 34.3 Data model (one migration, timestamp-named after main's newest)

**`github_pull_requests`** (new). RLS is ENABLE plus FORCE, with the standard `tenant_isolation` policy on `app_current_tenants()`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid PK` | |
| `tenant_id` | `uuid NOT NULL → companies` | Always the org tenant (the receiver's stamp) |
| `repo_full_name` | `text NOT NULL` | `org/name`, as `github_repos.full_name` |
| `number` | `int NOT NULL` | |
| `title` | `text NOT NULL` | |
| `state` | `text NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('open','closed'))` | GitHub's own two states |
| `merged` | `boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` | |
| `draft` | `boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` | |
| `head_ref` | `text NOT NULL` | The branch |
| `head_sha` | `text NULL` | Updated on `synchronize` |
| `html_url` | `text NOT NULL` | |
| `author_login` | `text NULL` | |
| `gh_updated_at` | `timestamptz NULL` | GitHub's `updated_at`; the ordering guard (§34.4) |
| `pm_task_id` | `uuid NULL → pm_tasks(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` | The linked task |
| `task_key` | `text NULL` | The key that linked it, as written, for display and audit |
| `ci` | `jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` | One entry per workflow name (§34.4) |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | `timestamptz` | |

- `UNIQUE (tenant_id, repo_full_name, number)`.
- Index `(tenant_id, pm_task_id) WHERE pm_task_id IS NOT NULL`.
- Index `(tenant_id, repo_full_name, head_sha)`.
- No backfill. Pull requests appear as their events arrive, so one opened before the deploy shows up on its next event (any push to it, an edit, a review request).

### 34.4 How the handlers fill it (in the same delivery, after today's writes)

**`pull_request`.** Any action, including opened, reopened, edited, synchronize, closed, ready_for_review and converted_to_draft:
- Upsert the row on `(tenant_id, repo_full_name, number)`.
- Apply it only if the payload's `pull_request.updated_at` is at or after the stored `gh_updated_at`. Out-of-order deliveries never roll a row back.
- Re-run the link (§34.5) on every applied event, so editing a title to add or remove a key changes the link.

**`workflow_run`.**
- Find the pull requests it belongs to: the numbers in `workflow_run.pull_requests[]` for this repo, or else the rows whose `head_sha` equals `workflow_run.head_sha`.
- On each, set `ci[<workflow name>] = { runId, status, conclusion, url, at }`.
- An entry is replaced only when the new run's `run_started_at` (else `created_at`) is at or after the stored `at`.
- The update merges into the object. Never `jsonb_set` a missing path; it creates no ancestors.

**The CI summary,** computed on read, never stored:
- `failing` when any workflow's latest conclusion is `failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled` or `action_required`;
- else `running` when any is not `completed`;
- else `passing` when all are `success`, `skipped` or `neutral`;
- `none` with no entries.

**Robustness.**
- A handler failure in this new part must not fail the delivery's existing writes. Each part logs and records its own note.
- The delivery is idempotent on `delivery_id`, as today.

### 34.5 The link rule (`linkTaskKey`, pure, exported)

- **Candidate keys:** every match of `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{1,9}-[0-9]{1,6}` that sits between non-alphanumeric characters (or at either end).
  - First in the title, then in `head_ref`; in each, left to right.
  - Case-insensitive, compared upper-cased.
- **A key resolves** only when `projects.short_code` (case-insensitive, live project) and `pm_tasks.seq` (live task) both exist **in the org tenant**.
- **The first candidate that resolves wins.** One pull request links to at most one task.
- **When nothing resolves,** `pm_task_id` and `task_key` are set to `NULL`. The pull request stays in the table and on its repository, never hidden. A word like `FIX-2` that names no project links nothing.
- **A deleted task** clears the link (FK `SET NULL`).
- **Ambiguity:** a pull request that names two tasks links only the first. That gap is accepted for v1.
- **Exports for other tickets:** the resolver is exported so DW-4h can attach the same pull request's `work_activity` rows to the task later. 6f does not change `work_activity`.

### 34.6 The read

`GET /api/:t/pm/tasks/:taskId/pull-requests`
- **Authorisation:** `pm_task` · `read` on the task, identical to `GET /api/:t/pm/tasks/:taskId`. Then RLS: a task id from another tenant finds nothing and answers 404.
- **Response:**
  `{ taskKey: string | null, linkable: boolean, repoLinked: boolean, pullRequests: Array<{ repo, number, title, state: "open" | "closed", merged, draft, headRef, url, authorLogin, updatedAt, ci: { summary: "passing" | "failing" | "running" | "none", runs: Array<{ name, status, conclusion, url, at }> } }> }`
- **Field meanings:**
  - `taskKey`: the task's key (`<short_code>-<seq>`), or `null` when its project has no short code.
  - `linkable`: `t` is the org tenant (§34.2). When it is `false`, the list is always empty.
  - `repoLinked`: some live `github_repos` row has `project_id` = the task's project. The UI uses it to decide whether to teach the key convention.
- **Order:** open pull requests first, then by `updatedAt` descending.
- **Status:** 200 with an empty list is a real "none". A server that cannot read answers 5xx; it never pretends "none".

### 34.7 UI (`platform-ui`)

- The PM task page (`TaskDetailView`) gains a **Pull requests** section, read with a `ReadResult` reader (`lib/pm.ts`).
- **Each pull request** shows:
  - a link `repo#number` and the title, opening GitHub in a new tab;
  - its state: Open, Draft, Merged or Closed;
  - the branch;
  - a CI chip (Passing, Failing, Running, or none), whose tooltip lists each workflow and its result.
- **What shows when, from the response:**
  - **Pull requests exist:** the list.
  - **None, and `repoLinked` with a `taskKey`:** one quiet line, "No pull requests yet. Put WEB-12 in a branch name or pull request title to link one."
  - **None, and not `linkable`:** nothing at all, so the convention is not taught in a company it cannot work in.
  - **None otherwise:** nothing.
  - **The read failed:** "Pull requests unavailable".
- Not pilot-gated: the task page is shared by both layouts, and the section is new information, not a layout change.

### 34.8 Before building, and tests

- **Check first, read-only:** that the App is subscribed to `pull_request` and `workflow_run`. Count recent rows per event in `github_webhook_deliveries` on the live ERP. If either is missing, the App's subscription is an owner step, added to DW-11.
- **Unit tests:**
  - `linkTaskKey`: title before branch; branch only; lowercase in a branch (`feature/web-12-nav`); several keys, where the first that resolves wins; no key; a key naming no project; a key naming a deleted task.
  - The CI summary over every conclusion.
- **DB/HTTP suite (Linux CI gate: Postgres and Cerbos):**
  - Upsert from `opened`. Then `edited`, adding and removing a key, re-links. An older `updated_at` delivered after a newer one changes nothing.
  - `workflow_run` matches by `pull_requests[]` and by `head_sha`, keeps one entry per workflow name, and refuses an older run.
  - The read: authorised like the task. A caller refused `read` gets 403. A task from another tenant gets 404. `linkable: false` in a non-org tenant. Open pull requests come first.
  - A replayed delivery (same `delivery_id`) writes nothing twice.
- **Fixtures** are taken from real GitHub payload shapes (`pull_request` and `workflow_run`), trimmed. No invented field.

### 34.9 As built (2026-10-13)

- **Migration** `202610140720_github_pull_requests.sql`. `pm_task_id` is a plain FK to `pm_tasks(id)` with `ON DELETE SET NULL`, not the tenant-scoped composite the other pm_* tables use: a composite `SET NULL` would also null the `NOT NULL` `tenant_id`. The link is resolved inside the org tenant under RLS before the id is written.
- **`linkTaskKey` is split.** `extractTaskKeys` and `candidateTaskKeys` (title, then branch) are pure and unit-tested without a database; `resolveTaskKey` and `linkTaskKey(client, tenantId, { title, headRef })` do the lookup in the org tenant. `task_key` stores the matched key as written (`web-12`); the task's own key on the read comes from the task.
- **The same run's late events.** A run's events share one start time, and GitHub does not promise their order. So besides "at or after", a stored `completed` entry is never replaced by a not-completed event of the SAME run id. A re-run, which has a new run id, still replaces it. Pinned in the DB suite.
- **Handler notes.** The delivery's `note` carries `pr_store=applied|stale|skipped(...)|failed(...)`, `link=<key>|none` and `ci_store=<rows updated>`. A failure in the new part is caught, logged and named in the note; the existing writes are already done.
- **CI summary.** `failing` covers any completed run whose conclusion is not `success`, `skipped` or `neutral` (so `startup_failure`, `stale` and a completed run with no conclusion count as failing as well as the four the contract names). `running` is any entry not `completed`. The summary is `summarizeCi` in `github-pull-requests.ts`; the read answers it per pull request next to the per-workflow `runs`.
- **UI.** `lib/pmPullRequests-data.ts` (`getTaskPullRequests`, a `ReadResult`) and `components/pm/PullRequests.tsx`, mounted in `TaskDetailView`. A refused read (403, not expected: same authorisation as the task) shows "You don't have access to pull requests." The demo backend answers `linkable: false`, so the section stays out of demo mode.

## 35. Asset versions and review rounds (DW-6h, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/creative.controller.ts`, `core/creative-reviews.ts` (new) — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (backend: HTTP suite `core/creative-reviews.test.ts` and Cerbos matrix `rbac/cerbos-creative-asset.test.ts` on the Linux CI gate; UI, §35.6: built, vitest on the CI gate; the request page's review status line, DW-5's, is not part of this ticket)**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §4.2 (DW-6h) and §14.3 (Creatives: "review with versions"). Creatives deliver assets to other departments (DW-5, §32). This section gives an asset a version history and gives review explicit rounds, so delivery and review happen in the ERP even when the design work happens elsewhere. It applies to the Asset Library's `creative_assets` (migration `0031`). It does not apply to the agency module's campaign-bound `agency_creative_assets`, which keeps its own review.

### 35.1 What exists

- `creative_assets` has `department_id` (an org-node id), the graded file (`graded_key`), an optional original, the grade parameters, and a soft delete.
- It has no versions and no review.
- Every route authorises as the generic `file` kind (`creative.controller.ts`), and `GET /creative/assets` ignores the department.
- DW-5 links delivered assets to requests (`work_request_assets`, §32.1).
- The generic comments (`/api/:t/comments`) accept any `entityType`.

### 35.2 Versions (one migration, timestamp-named after main's newest)

**`creative_assets` gains:**
- `version_group_id uuid NULL → creative_assets(id)`. `NULL` on a group's first version; later versions carry the first version's id.
- `version_no int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`.
- `supersedes_id uuid NULL → creative_assets(id)`, the version it replaces.

**The group key** is `COALESCE(version_group_id, id)`.
- Existing rows are each a group of one at version 1.
- No backfill `UPDATE` is needed, so the RLS zero-row trap of a backfill does not arise.

**Indexes:**
- unique `(tenant_id, COALESCE(version_group_id, id), version_no) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`;
- index `(tenant_id, COALESCE(version_group_id, id))`.

**Rules:**
- **A new version** is saved through today's `POST /api/:t/creative/assets` with an optional `versionOf: <assetId>`.
  - The server resolves that asset's group in the tenant: 404 `asset_not_found` if missing, 409 `asset_deleted` if deleted.
  - It locks the group's first row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) and takes `version_no = max + 1`. It sets `version_group_id` to the group key, `supersedes_id` to the current latest, and `department_id` from the group unless the body sets one.
  - The unique index is the second wall against two concurrent saves.
- **The latest version** is the live row with the highest `version_no` in its group. Deleting the latest makes the previous one latest again.
- **The original row is never edited.** A version's file never changes after it is saved. New bytes always make a new version, so a review can name exactly what it saw (§35.3).

### 35.3 Review rounds

**`creative_asset_reviews`** (new). RLS is ENABLE plus FORCE, with the standard `tenant_isolation` policy.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid PK` | |
| `tenant_id` | `uuid NOT NULL → companies` | |
| `group_id` | `uuid NOT NULL → creative_assets(id)` | The group key |
| `asset_id` | `uuid NOT NULL → creative_assets(id)` | The version under review |
| `round` | `int NOT NULL` | 1, 2, 3… per group |
| `status` | `text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('open','approved','changes_requested','withdrawn','superseded'))` | |
| `content_sha256` | `text NOT NULL` | The SHA-256 of the version's graded file when the round opened |
| `requested_by` | `uuid NOT NULL → users` | |
| `requested_at` | `timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` | |
| `note` | `text NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` | Up to 2,000 characters (CHECK) |
| `decided_by` | `uuid NULL → users` | |
| `decided_at` | `timestamptz NULL` | |
| `decision_comment` | `text NULL` | Up to 4,000 characters (CHECK); required for `changes_requested` |

- `UNIQUE (tenant_id, group_id, round)`.
- A partial unique index on `(tenant_id, group_id) WHERE status = 'open'`: one open round per asset at a time.

**Lifecycle:**
- **Open.** A round opens on the **latest** version only. The round number is the group's highest + 1.
- **Close.** An open round closes as `approved`, `changes_requested` (with a comment), or `withdrawn` by the person who opened it or a manager.
- **A new version supersedes it.** Saving a new version while a round is open closes that round as `superseded`, in the same transaction. The next round then reviews the new version.
- **History is kept.** Decided rounds never reopen.

### 35.4 Authorization: a new Cerbos kind `creative_asset` (review actions only)

**The existing routes keep the `file` kind and their gates unchanged.** Moving them would be an access change, which this section does not make. The new kind gates only the new review actions.

**It is six artifacts plus the pinned count literals:**
- the policy;
- the `cerbos.ts` type and attribute allow-list;
- the permission catalog;
- the permission groups;
- the seeding migration with its self-assertion;
- both role-bundle resolvers.

The deploy restarts Cerbos and then probes it.

| Action | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | company_admin, manager, member, viewer (`inTenant && notLow`) | Versions, rounds |
| `request_review` | company_admin, manager, member (`inTenant && notLow`) | |
| `decide_review` | company_admin, manager. **Its own rule** for `org_unit_lead` over the asset's department (`unitAncestors` of `department_id`, from `org_unit_closure`). **Its own rule** for a requester of a request the asset was delivered against (`request.principal.id in request.resource.attr.requesterIds`, from `work_request_assets` → `work_requests.requested_by`) | **`EFFECT_DENY` when `request.principal.id == request.resource.attr.reviewRequestedBy`**: nobody approves a review they opened. Also `EFFECT_DENY` for `principal.attr.kind in ['automation','bot']` |
| `withdraw_review` | company_admin, manager. **Its own rule** for `reviewRequestedBy == principal.id` | |

- Resource attributes sent: `tenantId`, `module`, `unitAncestors`, `requesterIds`, `reviewRequestedBy`. Each is added to the `resourcePayload()` allow-list.
- Every attribute-dependent rule stands alone, never mixed with a scope role.
- Catalog entries: `core.creative_asset.read|request_review|decide_review|withdraw_review`, plus the generic permission arm, which does not mirror the lead, requester or self-approval rules.

### 35.5 Routes

| Method | Path | Body or query | Answer | Authz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/:t/creative/assets` | `?departmentId=` (§33's helper, on the asset's own `department_id`, node or subtree); `?versions=latest` (default) or `all` | Today's rows, each plus `versionNo`, `versionGroupId`, `versionCount`, `isLatest`, `review: { round, status } \| null` (the group's latest round) | `file` · `read` (unchanged) |
| POST | `/api/:t/creative/assets` | today's body, plus optional `versionOf` | Today's row, plus the version fields | `file` · `create` (unchanged) |
| GET | `/api/:t/creative/assets/:id/versions` | | The group's live versions, newest first, each with the same fields | `file` · `read` |
| GET | `/api/:t/creative/assets/:id/reviews` | | The group's rounds, newest first | `creative_asset` · `read` |
| POST | `/api/:t/creative/assets/:id/reviews` | `{ note? }` | 201, the round | `creative_asset` · `request_review`. 409 `not_latest_version`, 409 `review_open`, 409 `asset_deleted` |
| POST | `/api/:t/creative/assets/:id/reviews/:round/decision` | `{ decision: "approved" \| "changes_requested", comment? }` | 200, the round | `creative_asset` · `decide_review`. 409 `review_not_open`; 400 `{ field: "comment" }` when `changes_requested` has none |
| POST | `/api/:t/creative/assets/:id/reviews/:round/withdraw` | | 200, the round | `creative_asset` · `withdraw_review`. 409 `review_not_open` |

- Authorise first, then validate the body.
- Error tokens go at the start of `message` (the error filter turns it into `{ error }`).
- Writes record activity (`writeActivity`) and notify. Opening a round notifies the asset's department lead and the requesters of linked requests. A decision notifies whoever opened the round.

### 35.6 UI

- **The Asset Library** shows each asset's latest version, with a "v3" badge when there is more than one and a review chip: In review, Approved or Changes requested. The department filter uses `?departmentId=`.
- **The asset detail**:
  - the version history (thumbnail, number, who and when);
  - the rounds, each with its decision and comment;
  - the asset's thread, using generic comments with `entityType: "creative_asset"` and `entityId` set to the group key, so one thread follows every version;
  - actions, each shown only to those allowed: Upload new version, Request review, Approve, Request changes, Withdraw.
- **Uploading a new version** works from the Library's upload, and from Image Studio's save as "a new version of …".
- **DW-5's request page** shows each delivered asset's latest review status. Delivery is not blocked by review in v1.
- **Client review of library assets is not in v1.** Clients review posts through the social flow.

### 35.7 Tests (the Linux CI gate: Postgres and Cerbos)

- **Versions:**
  - `versionOf` appends version 2 and then 3;
  - two concurrent saves never share a number;
  - a deleted latest makes the previous one latest;
  - an asset from another tenant answers 404;
  - `versions=latest` and `versions=all`, and `versionCount`;
  - `departmentId` with a subtree.
- **Rounds:**
  - only the latest version may open one;
  - one open round at a time;
  - a new version supersedes the open round;
  - the round number increments;
  - `changes_requested` needs a comment;
  - decided rounds never reopen.
- **Cerbos matrix:**
  - a member may request but not decide;
  - a lead decides only for its own department's assets;
  - a requester of a linked request may decide;
  - **the person who opened a round cannot decide it, whatever their role**;
  - a bot cannot decide;
  - withdraw: the opener or a manager only.
- **Cerbos restart:** the policy count rises by one, and Cerbos is probed after a restart on the gate.
- **UI vitest:** the chip mapping, the version badge, and actions hidden by capability.

### 35.8 As built (backend, DW-6h, 2026-10-13)

**Where it is.**
- Migrations `202610140730_creative_asset_versions_reviews.sql` (the schema, with a DO-block self-assertion) and `202610140740_iam_creative_asset_permissions.sql` (the permission seed, 22 role rows, with a DO-block self-assertion that includes owner ≡ company_admin and the self-scoped marker).
- Routes in `core/creative.controller.ts`; rules, parsing and SQL in `core/creative-reviews.ts`.
- The Cerbos kind: `cerbos/policies/resource_creative_asset.yaml`, two `perm_creative_asset_*` derived roles, `requesterIds` and `reviewRequestedBy` in `cerbos.ts` (type and allow-list), 4 catalog keys (107 kinds, 460 pairs, 445 grantable), 1 permission group (`creative_asset_reviews`), bundles regenerated. Recorded in `docs/PERMISSION-CONTRACT.md` §37. Policy files: 106 → 107 resource policies (108 → 109 files with `derived_roles.yaml` and `_variables.yaml`).
- **The deploy must restart Cerbos** (test and live sidecar) and probe it; nothing hot-reloads.

**Tests.** `core/creative-reviews.test.ts` (22 HTTP tests over real Postgres and Cerbos: every §35.7 bullet for versions and rounds, and the matrix over the real routes) and `rbac/cerbos-creative-asset.test.ts` (12 static pins that always run, plus 32 live cases that need `CERBOS_URL`). The UI vitest belongs to the UI ticket.

**Deviations and clarifications, each with its reason.**
1. **A version number is never reused.** `version_no` is the group's highest number over EVERY row, deleted ones included, plus one. Deleting v3 and saving again gives v4, not a second v3, so a round that reviewed "version 3" keeps naming the same bytes. The unique index stays partial on live rows, as specified.
2. **`versionGroupId` is the group key, never null.** Rows answer `COALESCE(version_group_id, id)`, so a first version reports its own id. The UI uses it as the comment thread's `entityId` (§35.6). Rows and the save answer also carry `supersedesId`.
3. **The inherited department** is the department of the group's latest live version.
4. **`requesterIds` covers the whole group**: the `requested_by` of every work request that is not deleted and that any version of the group was delivered against. A round reviews the group, so the person who asked for v1 may decide on v2. Request status is not filtered (a delivered request is the normal case).
5. **`unitAncestors` comes from the version the action is about**: the round's version for a decision or a withdrawal, the named version for `read` and `request_review`. An asset with no department feeds `[]`, so no lead matches.
6. **The self-approval DENY has the invoice `approve` shape** (`has() && != "" && reviewRequestedBy == principal.id`, on `roles: ["user"]`). It fires whenever the opener is known, for every role, platform_admin included. It does not fail closed on an unfed attribute, because the handler always feeds it from the NOT NULL `requested_by` of the round, and a fail-closed form would make the platform_admin scope-level sweep in `authz-permissions.controller.test.ts` (which sends no round) report `decide_review` as unreachable.
7. **The bot DENY covers `decide_review` only**, as the §35.4 table says. A bot or automation principal may read, request and withdraw within its role.
8. **Deleting the version under an open round closes that round as `withdrawn`** (`decided_by` = the deleter), in the delete's transaction under the group lock. Without this, a round left open on a deleted version would block every later round on the group (one open round per group). The delete route's authorisation is unchanged (`file` · `delete`).
