9. **`POST /creative/assets` now authorises before it validates.** Its gate is unchanged (`file` · `create`); only the order changed, so a caller without `create` gets 403 rather than a 400 for a bad body (§35.5's rule; the existing suite still passes).
10. **Extra error tokens**, each at the start of `message` and repeated in `reason`: 404 `review_not_found` (an unknown or malformed `:round`), 409 `version_conflict` (the unique index refused a concurrent save; the lock makes it unreachable in practice), and the 400s `version_of_invalid`, `versions_invalid`, `note_invalid`, `decision_invalid`, `comment_invalid`, `comment_required` and `body_invalid`, each with its `field`. `?departmentId=` keeps §33's helper and its messages.
11. **Reads of a deleted version.** `GET …/:id/versions` and `GET …/:id/reviews` answer 404 `asset_not_found` for a deleted `:id`. A decision or a withdrawal resolves the group through any version id, deleted or not. A missing `:id` on a review route is checked against `creative_asset` · `read` first, so a 404 is never an existence answer for a caller who may not read.
12. **The schema adds guards the contract implies**: a version-shape CHECK (a first version has no group and supersedes nothing; a later one has both), the round lifecycle CHECKs (an open round has no decision; a closed one has `decided_at`; approved, changes_requested and withdrawn name a decider; changes_requested has a non-blank comment), a lowercase-hex CHECK on `content_sha256`, and the house `origin_site` column.
13. **The hash.** `content_sha256` is taken from `storage().get(graded_key)`, as `GET …/content` serves the bytes, after a pre-check (deleted, latest) so a refusal never costs a storage read; the transaction re-checks under the group lock. A storage failure is a 500.
14. **Activity and notifications.** Activity on `creative_asset` with the group key as the entity: `review_requested`, `review_approved`, `review_changes_requested`, `review_withdrawn` and `review_superseded`; the save's `graded` activity carries `versionOf` and `versionNo`. Notifications through `notifyBestEffort` (never the actor): `creative_review.requested` to the department's lead-seat holders and the requesters, `creative_review.decided` to the opener. A withdrawal and a supersession notify nobody.
15. **`GET /creative/assets/:id` is unchanged** (no version fields); the version history is `GET …/:id/versions`.
16. **A failed save removes the bytes it stored**, best effort, so a 404 or 409 on `versionOf` leaves no orphan in storage.

**UI (DW-6h, 2026-10-13).**
- **Asset Library** (`departments/[deptId]/assets`): reads `?departmentId=<deptId>` (latest versions, the default) through `readCreativeAssets` (a `ReadResult`; a refusal or outage is shown as such). Each card shows a quiet `vN` badge when `versionCount > 1` and a review chip from `review` (In review, Approved, Changes requested; nothing for no round, withdrawn or superseded). The name opens the detail.
- **Asset detail** (new page `departments/[deptId]/assets/[assetId]`; `[assetId]` may be any version): version history (thumbnail from `/api/creative-assets/:id`, `vN`, uploaded by you or not, when; the list answers `uploader_id` only, so no other names), review rounds (round, status, note, decision, comment, who and when), and the thread (generic comments on `creative_asset`, `entityId` = `versionGroupId`). Actions: Upload new version, Request review (latest version, no open round), Approve (open round, hidden from the person who opened it), Request changes (comment required), Withdraw. A 403 reads "You can't do this on this asset."; the 409 and 400 tokens become sentences (`lib/creativeReviews.ts`). If the rounds cannot be read, only Upload is offered.
- **New version:** from the detail, a file upload sends `POST /creative/assets` with `versionOf` = the latest version and the identity grade; from Image Studio, `?versionOf=<assetId>` (linked from the detail as "Edit in Image Studio") offers "Save as a new version of <name>", which sends `versionOf`. Studio still starts empty (the asset's pixels are not preloaded).
- Files: `lib/creativeReviews.ts` (pure), `creativeReviews-data.ts` (readers), `creativeReviewActions.ts` (actions), `components/creative/AssetDetail.tsx`, tests beside each.

## 36. Figma links on tasks, requests and campaign parts (DW-6k, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/core/figma/` (new) — **STATUS: BACKEND AND UI BUILT, PROTOTYPED (stubbed Figma client; the UI reads well with Figma not connected; live proof waits for DW-11)**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §4.1 (Figma, owner ruling DW-Q6: "use Figma too"), §4.2 (DW-6k) and §14.1 (launch and return). Editing still happens in Figma, because a design tool cannot run inside the ERP. This section adds the connected half:
- link a file or frame to the work it belongs to;
- see its thumbnail, when it last changed and its open comments;
- export it into the Asset Library as a version.

That way delivery and review stay in the ERP, and every delivered design exists as a file the ERP holds (the vendor doctrine's exit, §2.6).

### 36.1 The connection

- **Provider.** The credential vault gains the provider `figma`: the `integration_connections` provider CHECK is widened by migration, and `CONNECTION_PROVIDERS` in `core/integrations.service.ts` is updated.
- **Scope.** The connection is per company (`owner_kind = 'company'`). Its token is sealed like every other token.
- **Token types.**
  - A personal access token is sent as the `X-Figma-Token` header.
  - An OAuth token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. The OAuth app itself is the owner step in DW-11.
- **Who manages it.** Connecting and disconnecting needs `company.manage`, on the Tools & connections page, where the Figma kind loses its `DW-6k` ticket. Everyone sees whether it is connected.
- **Who it serves.** Only the company's own Figma team files are reachable: whatever the token can read.

### 36.2 Data model (one migration, timestamp-named after main's newest)

**`figma_links`** (new). RLS is ENABLE plus FORCE, with the standard `tenant_isolation` policy.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid PK` | |
| `tenant_id` | `uuid NOT NULL → companies` | |
| `target_kind` | `text NOT NULL CHECK (target_kind IN ('pm_task','work_request','campaign_part'))` | |
| `target_id` | `uuid NOT NULL` | `pm_tasks.id`, `work_requests.id` (§32) or `agency_campaign_parts.id` (§31). There is no FK across three tables; the route checks that it exists in the tenant |
| `file_key` | `text NOT NULL` | From the URL |
| `node_id` | `text NULL` | A frame, in the API form `1:2`. `NULL` means the whole file |
| `url` | `text NOT NULL` | As pasted, normalised |
| `title` | `text NULL` | Cached: the file name, and the frame name when there is one |
| `last_modified` | `timestamptz NULL` | Cached from the file |
| `open_comments` | `int NULL` | Cached: comments with no `resolved_at` (on the node, when one is set) |
| `cached_at` | `timestamptz NULL` | |
| `asset_group_id` | `uuid NULL → creative_assets(id)` | The Asset Library group its exports go into (§35) |
| `created_by` | `uuid NOT NULL → users` | |
| `created_at`, `deleted_at` | `timestamptz` | |

- Unique: `(tenant_id, target_kind, target_id, file_key, COALESCE(node_id, '')) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.
- Index: `(tenant_id, target_kind, target_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.

**Parsing the URL.**
- Hosts: `www.figma.com` and `figma.com`.
- Paths: `/design/<key>/…`, `/file/<key>/…` and `/proto/<key>/…`.
- The optional `node-id` query uses `-` in the URL and `:` in the API (`1-2` becomes `1:2`).
- Anything else answers 400 `{ field: "url" }`. The parser is a pure function with its own tests.

### 36.3 Reading Figma (server side only)

- **Calls.** Figma's REST API under the company token:
  - the file (`GET /v1/files/:key`, shallow depth) for the name and `lastModified`;
  - the nodes (`GET /v1/files/:key/nodes?ids=`) for a frame's name;
  - comments (`GET /v1/files/:key/comments`);
  - renders (`GET /v1/images/:key?ids=&format=&scale=`).
- **Cache.** A link's cached fields refresh when they are older than 10 minutes and someone reads the link. A failed refresh keeps the old values and marks the link `stale`.
- **Thumbnails** are rendered by Figma and expire, so they are **proxied and never stored**. `GET …/figma-links/:id/thumbnail` streams a small PNG with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=600`.
- **Failures.** No connection answers `figma_not_connected`. A token Figma refuses answers `figma_refused`. Neither is ever shown as "no comments" or as an empty file.
- **Rate limits.** Figma rate-limits its API. A 429 sets `stale` and is retried on a later read, never in a loop.
- **The client.** Everything goes through one thin client module whose responses are typed from Figma's documented shapes. Tests use recorded, trimmed fixtures of those shapes, never invented fields.

### 36.4 Exports into the Asset Library

`POST …/figma-links/:id/export` with `{ format: "png" | "svg" | "pdf", scale?: 1 | 2 | 3 }`:
- The server renders the frame (or the file's first page when there is no node), downloads the result, and saves it as a `creative_assets` row:
  - `content_type` is the format's own type;
  - `grade` is `{ "source": "figma", "fileKey", "nodeId", "lastModified" }`;
  - `department_id` is the target's department where it has one.
- The **first** export starts a version group and records it on the link (`asset_group_id`). Every later export is a new version of that group (§35.2), so the Asset Library holds the design's history and a review round can review it (§35.3).
- **Linking to a request.** When the target is an `assets` work request (§32), the export is not delivered automatically. Delivering stays DW-5's explicit step. The request page offers the exported asset to deliver.

### 36.5 Routes and authorization

There is **no new Cerbos kind**. A link is part of the work it is on, so it is authorised by that work's own kind.

| Method | Path | Authz |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/:t/figma-links?targetKind=&targetId=` | `read` on the target (`pm_task`, `work_request` or `agency_campaign_part`) |
| POST | `/api/:t/figma-links` `{ targetKind, targetId, url }` | Writing to the target: `pm_task` · `update`; `agency_campaign_part` · `update`; `work_request` · `deliver` **or** `cancel` (the receiving side or the asker) |
| DELETE | `/api/:t/figma-links/:id` | The same write check on the link's target |
| GET | `/api/:t/figma-links/:id/thumbnail` | `read` on the link's target |
| POST | `/api/:t/figma-links/:id/export` | The write check on the target **and** `file` · `create`, today's Asset Library save gate |

- Authorise first, then validate.
- Error tokens go at the start of `message`: `figma_not_connected`, `figma_refused`, `target_not_found`, `bad_figma_url`.
- A target from another tenant answers 404.

### 36.6 UI

- **Where it shows.** The PM task page, the request page (§32) and the campaign part (§31) each gain a **Designs** section.
- **Each link shows:**
  - its thumbnail and title;
  - "changed <relative time>";
  - "<n> open comments", which opens Figma at the frame;
  - "Open in Figma";
  - Export (PNG, SVG or PDF), which lands in the Asset Library and shows the new version number.
- **Adding a link.** Paste a Figma URL; it is checked before it is saved.
- **When Figma is not connected,** the section shows its links with the cached values and one line: "Figma isn't connected for this company". It never shows empty comments. Managers see a link to Tools & connections.
- **Thumbnails** load lazily, with alt text set to the title.

### 36.7 Tests

- **Unit:**
  - URL parsing across `design`, `file` and `proto`, with and without `node-id`, and other hosts refused;
  - the open-comment count (resolved, on-node and off-node comments).
- **DB/HTTP suite (Linux CI gate: Postgres and Cerbos), with the Figma client stubbed from recorded fixtures:**
  - create, list and delete per target kind;
  - the write check per kind, including a `work_request` asker (cancel) and receiver (deliver), and a stranger refused;
  - another tenant's target answers 404;
  - the 10-minute refresh, and `stale` on a failed or 429 refresh;
  - an export creates version 1 and then version 2 in the link's group;
  - `figma_not_connected` when there is no connection.
- **Live proof** waits for Figma API access (DW-11 item 7): one file linked, a thumbnail shown, comments counted, one export landing in the Asset Library, observed on the live ERP.

### 36.8 As built (backend, DW-6k, 2026-10-14)

**Where it is.**
- Migration `202610140840_figma_links.sql`:
  - the provider CHECK on `integration_connections` is rebuilt from its LIVE definition (the 202610130210 idiom, never a typed list) and a DO block asserts the full list;
  - provider list before (12): `github`, `google_drive`, `claude`, `google_search_console`, `google_analytics`, `google_ads`, `semrush`, `cpanel`, `ftp`, `ssh`, `wp_admin`, `bing_webmaster`; after (13): the same twelve plus `figma`;
  - `figma_links` exactly as §36.2 (RLS enable plus force, the `tenant_isolation` policy, the unique partial index over `COALESCE(node_id, '')`, the target index), with a DO-block self-assertion.
- `core/figma/`:
  - `url.ts`: the pure parser;
  - `rules.ts`: the pure rules (cache age, open-comment count, title, export body);
  - `client.ts`: the injectable REST client, its types taken from Figma's published OpenAPI description (`github.com/figma/rest-api-spec`, `openapi/openapi.yaml` 0.44.0) and the `developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/` pages, cited in its header;
  - `service.ts`: the links, the cache, the connection and the export;
  - `figma.controller.ts`: the routes.
- `core/creative-save.ts` (new): the body of `POST /creative/assets`, moved unchanged, so an export saves through the SAME path as an upload. The route's behaviour is unchanged (`creative-reviews.test.ts` is its guard).
- `CONNECTION_PROVIDERS` gains `figma`. `factsResource` (work-requests.controller.ts) and `partResource` (agency.controller.ts) are now exported, so the link's authorisation uses the very resources those targets' own routes send.

**Routes** (all under `/api/:t`; every one is authorised by the target's own kind, there is still no new Cerbos kind):

| Method | Path | Answer | Authz as built |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/figma-links?targetKind=&targetId=` | `{ figmaConnected, items: [FigmaLink] }`, each due link refreshed first | `read` on the target |
| POST | `/figma-links` | 201 `FigmaLink` | the write check below |
| DELETE | `/figma-links/:id` | `{ id, deleted: true }` (soft delete: the slot is freed, exported assets stay) | the write check on the link's target |
| GET | `/figma-links/:id/thumbnail` | the PNG, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=600` | `read` on the link's target |
| POST | `/figma-links/:id/export` | 201 `{ linkId, assetId, assetGroupId, versionNo, name, contentType, byteSize }` | the write check AND `file` · `create` |
| GET | `/integrations/figma` | `{ connected, tokenType }` (never the token) | `pm_task` · `read`: anyone who reads PM tasks |
| PUT | `/integrations/figma` `{ token, tokenType?: "pat" \| "oauth" }` | `{ connected, tokenType }` | `integration_connection` · `manage` (company_admin, manager: `company.manage`) |
| DELETE | `/integrations/figma` | `{ disconnected }` | `integration_connection` · `manage` |

- **The write check per kind:**
  - `pm_task`: `update` on `{ id }`, which is all that task's own routes send (the PM policy has no owner, lead or assignee rule, so none applies);
  - `agency_campaign_part`: `update` on `{ id, ownerId, unitAncestors }`, so the part's owner and the lead of its department pass;
  - `work_request`: `deliver` OR `cancel` on the request's `factsResource` (requestedBy, assigneeIds, unitAncestors). Two questions go through `can()`, which answers without throwing, then the one authoritative `authorize()` runs on the action that passed (it audits, enforces the session and the act-for intersection). When neither passes it asks `deliver`, so the refusal is the standard audited 403.
- **FigmaLink:** `{ id, targetKind, targetId, fileKey, nodeId, url, title, lastModified, openComments, cachedAt, assetGroupId, createdBy, createdAt, stale, refreshError }`. `openComments`, `title`, `lastModified` and `cachedAt` are `null` when never read: never `0` standing in for "unknown".
- **`stale` and `refreshError`:** `stale: true` means the cache was due and could not be refreshed, so the numbers are the old ones. `refreshError` names why: `figma_not_connected`, `figma_refused`, `figma_rate_limited`, `figma_not_found` or `figma_unavailable`. A link that is not yet due is `stale: false` even when Figma is not connected.

**Tests.** `core/figma/url.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts` and `client.test.ts` (pure, no database); `core/figma/figma-links.test.ts` (the HTTP suite: real Postgres and Cerbos, Figma stubbed at `fetch` with JSON trimmed from the documented shapes, so the real client is exercised); the provider-CHECK test in `db/module-search-rls.test.ts` now pins all thirteen values. The capability inventory's suite counts moved (agency 21, core 66, pm 13) because the new suite is another driver of those route families; no MCP tool was added.

**Deviations and clarifications, each with its reason.**
1. **Three routes not in §36.5: the connection.** No HTTP path stored a company token (Phase 1's generic connections API accepts no tokens, see the vault note at the top of the connections section), and §36.1 needs one. They reuse the vault's own path (`createConnection` then `setConnectionTokens`, as the Bing connector does) and `meta.tokenType` records the kind. The token is not verified against Figma at connect (verification would be a fifth Figma read); a refused token surfaces as `figma_refused` on first use. The generic `POST /integrations/connections` now also accepts `provider: "figma"` as a token-less mapping row, like every provider.
2. **Response shapes** (the list's `{ figmaConnected, items }`, `FigmaLink`, the export answer) were not in §36; they are defined above.
3. **A link can be created without a working connection.** It is saved with an empty cache, and the 201 carries `stale: true` and the reason. Only the thumbnail and the export need Figma to answer, and they refuse with the tokens below.
4. **HTTP statuses for the Figma failures.** `figma_not_connected`, `figma_refused` and `figma_not_found` are 409; `figma_rate_limited` is 503; `figma_unavailable`, `figma_render_failed` and `export_too_large` are 502. A 4xx 401/403 would read as the ERP's own authentication failing, so none is used for Figma's.
5. **Extra tokens, each at the start of `message` and repeated in `reason`:** `link_exists` (409: the same file and frame on a target twice; a whole-file link is one slot), `too_many_links` (409: 25 live links per target, so one read never refreshes an unbounded set), `link_not_found` (404), `bad_target` (400, `field: "targetKind"`), `bad_export` (400, `field: "format"` or `"scale"`), `bad_token` and `bad_token_type` (400).
6. **Open comments** are threads: replies (`parent_id` set) are not counted, so a resolved thread's replies cannot inflate the number. With a frame in the link, only a comment pinned to exactly that frame counts; a comment on bare canvas is off-node.
7. **A frame Figma no longer has** is `figma_not_found` and the link is stale; it is not shown as a frame with no comments.
8. **The order of the first gate.** The target kind names which kind to authorise, so it is read first. An unusable kind is answered 400 only after the caller has passed the `pm_task` read gate. A missing link is answered 404 only after that same gate.
9. **Thumbnail and export sizes.** The thumbnail is a PNG at scale 0.5, buffered (capped at 8 MB) and sent with the cache header, not piped; an export is capped at the Asset Library's 25 MB. A frame link's thumbnail makes no read of the file.
10. **`grade.nodeId` is the node that was actually rendered,** so a whole-file link records its first page (`document.children[0]`), not null.
11. **A deleted group starts a new one.** When every version of the link's group was deleted, the next export starts a fresh group and records it on the link; the save path would otherwise refuse with `asset_deleted`. The link row is locked (`FOR UPDATE`) inside the save's transaction, so two first exports cannot start two groups.
12. **A link whose target was deleted** answers 404 `target_not_found` on delete, thumbnail and export (the target's kind cannot be authorised without it).
13. **Title** is `File name / Frame name`, or the file name alone.
14. **URL normalisation.** `http` is accepted and stored as `https`; the stored link is `https://www.figma.com/<kind>/<key>` plus `?node-id=1-2`, with the slug and every other parameter dropped. A node id of the nested-instance form (`I1-2;3-4`) is accepted. The file key must be alphanumeric (it is put into a Figma API path).
15. **Audit.** Activity rows on `figma_link` (`created`, `deleted`, `exported`) and on `integration_connection` (`connected`, `disconnected`, never the token). No outbox event and no notification.

**UI (DW-6k, 2026-10-14, `platform-ui`).**
- **Readers and writes.**
  - `lib/figma.ts` (pure): the shapes, the normalisers (a malformed count is `null`, never `0`), the route URLs and every sentence, including the error-token map: every token in deviations 4 and 5 above, read from the start of `error` (or from `reason`), each with its own plain sentence. A 403 is always the calm permission sentence.
  - `lib/figma-data.ts`: `readFigmaLinks` and `readFigmaConnection`, both `ReadResult`s. `lib/figmaActions.ts`: add, remove, export, connect and disconnect; the token crosses it once, inbound, and is never returned.
- **Designs section** (`components/figma/Designs.tsx`) on three pages:
  - the PM task page (`TaskDetailView`, both layouts);
  - the request page (`app/(app)/requests/[id]`);
  - each part card of the campaign page (`app/(app)/agency/[campaignId]`, `CampaignParts`).
  Each link shows its thumbnail, title, "changed <relative time>", "<n> open comments" (opens Figma at the frame), "Open in Figma", a "Stale" note, Export (PNG, SVG or PDF, with a success line naming the new version) and Remove. A comment count of `null` reads "Comments not read yet". With `figmaConnected: false` the links keep their cached values, with one line, "Figma isn't connected for this company", and a Tools & connections link for `company.manage` holders. Add, Remove and Export are offered to everyone who can read the section; the server decides and a refusal is a sentence.
- **Thumbnail proxy.** The `<img>` points at `GET /api/figma-links/:linkId/thumbnail` on platform-ui (`app/api/figma-links/[linkId]/thumbnail/route.ts`), which forwards the caller's session to the platform's thumbnail route for the active company, passes on only a PNG, and sets `Cache-Control: private, max-age=600`, `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. It loads lazily, with `alt` = the title; a failed load shows "Preview unavailable".
- **Tools & connections** (`FigmaConnectionBlock`, pilot branch): the `DW-6k` ticket is removed from `CONN.figma`. Everyone sees whether Figma is connected and the token type (never the token). `company.manage` holders get a password field, the type (Personal access token or OAuth), Connect (Replace token while connected) and Disconnect.
- **"Open in".** `CONTEXT_BUILDERS.figma` links each of the task's links by its stored `url`, with the title as the detail; none, or none usable, opens Figma's home. The task page reads the links once and passes the same answer to the Designs section and to `OpenInSlot`.
- **Demo mode** answers `figma-links` and `integrations/figma` as not connected with nothing linked.
- **UI deviations.**
  1. The link is read once per page; on the campaign page that is one read per part (a campaign holds one part per department).
  2. No Designs section is drawn for a part card whose links were not read.
  3. The Tools & connections link is offered only when a department is known (the request's receiving department, the part's department, the task's project department), and only when Figma is known not to be connected.
- **Tests.** `lib/figma.test.ts`, `lib/figma-data.test.ts`, `lib/figmaActions.test.ts`, `components/figma/Designs.test.tsx`, `components/departments/FigmaConnectionBlock.test.tsx`, `app/api/figma-links/[linkId]/thumbnail/route.test.ts`; additions to `lib/toolContext.test.ts`, `components/agency/CampaignParts.test.tsx` and `components/departments/ConnectionBlocks.test.tsx`; `e2e/workspace-departments.spec.ts` asserts the Figma block's "not connected" line.

**Not yet done.** The live proof (DW-11 item 7).

## 37. A unit's roster on the person-grain report overview (DW-4b, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/reports.controller.ts` (`getOverview`), `person-scope.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (DB suite tr25-person-axis.db.test.ts on the Linux CI gate)**

**Why.** A head's Team report must list everyone in their unit. `GET /reports/overview?grain=person` lists only people who have fact rows in the range, so a quiet team member would silently drop off the page. An empty or short list is a claim; this one would be false. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §5.1 and §5.6.

**Request.** `GET /api/:t/reports/overview?grain=person&unit=<orgNodeId>&periodKind&start[&end]`. `unit` is optional. Without it, the endpoint is unchanged and its scopes carry no `activity` field.

**Validation and authorization, in this order:**
1. `unit` with any grain other than `person` → 400 `{error: "unit is only valid with grain=person", field: "unit"}` on the wire (thrown as `{message, field}`; the shared error filter renders `message` as `error`, as for every report 400).
2. The range, as for every report read (§6.2 of the reporting blueprint).
3. Cerbos `read_person` on `report_document`, as today. A plain member is refused (403).
4. A caller narrowed to their led units (`requiresUnitNarrowing`) must lead `unit`: `assertUnitInLedScope` as of today, else 403 "outside your reporting line". This runs before the existence check, so a narrowed caller learns nothing about units outside their line.
5. `unit` is not a node of the company's org structure → 404 `{error: "unit_not_found", field: "unit"}` on the wire.

**Roster.** Every user whose primary `org_unit_memberships` row is valid TODAY (in `REPORTS_TZ`) on a node in `unit`'s subtree (`collectUnitSubtree`). Today, not the range end: the same rule as the TR-25 narrowing, so choosing a past range can never widen who a head sees. Someone who left the unit mid-range is not listed, and their numbers stay in the department's report.

**Response.** `{periodKind, start, end, unit, scopes: [{scopeRef, scopeName, kpis, activity}]}`, ordered by `scopeName`.
- `activity: true`: the person has fact rows in the range, and `kpis` are byte-identical to the same person's entry without `unit`, built by the same `buildHeadlineKpis` over the same rows.
- `activity: false`: no fact rows in the range. `kpis` is `[]`, never zero-filled.
- The existing TR-25 narrowing still filters the result as a second guard.

**UI consumer.** `lib/reports-data.ts::getReportOverview(…, { unit })` on `/reports/team`. The demo backend (`demoReports.ts`) serves the same shape.

**MCP.** No tool lists the overview today; none is added.

## 38. A department head's Team progress, and their access to Learning (DW-4g, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/modules/lms/lms-learn.controller.ts` (`compliance`) — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (lms-l1-acceptance.test.ts on the Linux CI gate)**

**Why.** DW-D15 (owner): a head gets `org_unit_lead` on their own department, derived from their lead position, so they can add learning material and see their team's progress, but never waive mandatory training. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §5.4 and §5.6.

**What already exists, and stays.**
- The grant. A lead position's role set carries `org_unit_lead` at `scope_kind = 'own_unit'` (`seed/positions.ts`), and the position reconciler materialises it as an `org_unit`-scoped `user_roles` grant. No new grant path is added. A head without a lead position has no lead power; that is data, fixed in Positions.
- Authoring. `lms_course` create, update, publish and retire match `org_unit_lead` only when the course's unit is inside the head's unit (`unitAncestors`), and a general-track course stays `company_admin` only. Proven by `lms-l1-acceptance.test.ts` case 1.
- Waiving. `POST …/enrollments/:id/waive` is allowed only for `hr_people_ops`, `module_manager` and `company_admin` (`resource_lms_enrollment.yaml`). Unchanged.

**The gap.** `GET /api/:t/modules/lms/compliance` authorizes `lms_enrollment` read with no unit attributes, so `org_unit_lead` can never match and a head is refused. Its aggregate is also company-wide. And the Learning pages gate on company-wide `can()`, which by design never counts a unit-scoped grant, so a head who sees the "Add material" and "Team progress" tabs is refused when opening them.

**The unit-scoped read.** `GET /api/:t/modules/lms/compliance?unit=<orgNodeId>`. Without `unit`, the endpoint is unchanged.
1. Cerbos `lms_enrollment` read, with the resource's `unitAncestors` loaded for `unit` (`loadUnitAncestors`). A head of that unit or an enclosing one passes; anyone else without a company-wide grant gets 403. An id that is not in the org tree has no ancestors, so a head is refused (403) before anything reveals whether it exists.
2. A caller who passed Cerbos through a company-wide grant, asking for an id that is not in the org tree, gets 404 `{error: "unit_not_found", field: "unit"}` on the wire.
3. Learners: every user whose primary `org_unit_memberships` row is valid TODAY (`REPORTS_TZ`) on a node of the unit's subtree, the same roster rule as §37.
4. Response: `{unit, learners, paths: [{pathKey, title, isMandatory, assigned, completed, outstanding, overdue, waived}]}`. Each count covers only those learners' enrolments. `learners` is the roster size, so "0 assigned" can never be read as "nobody here".

**The UI.**
- Registry Learning row: `add` → `/learning/authoring?unit={dept}`, `team` → `/learning/compliance?unit={dept}`. Their gates stay `unitCap`.
- `/learning/authoring`: opens for a company-wide `lms.authoring` holder as today, and for a head through `canInUnit` on the unit in `?unit` (or, with no `unit`, on any unit they lead). A head can create only department-track courses, and only for units they lead (the server is the authority). Publishing follows `lms.publish` the same way.
- `/learning/compliance?unit=`: opens through `canInUnit(lms.progress.view)` for that unit and reads the unit-scoped endpoint through an honest reader. A 403 shows the refusal, a 404 says the department does not exist, and nothing is ever an empty list for a failed read. Without `unit` the page is unchanged.

**Proof (live Postgres + Cerbos on the CI gate, added to `lms-l1-acceptance.test.ts`):**
- the Web Dev head is refused when waiving (403);
- `compliance?unit=d-web` as the Web Dev head → 200, counting only Web Dev learners (a learner placed elsewhere is not counted);
- `compliance?unit=d-seo` as the Web Dev head → 403;
- an unknown unit → 403 for the head, and 404 for a company-wide caller;
- without `unit`, the head is still refused (unchanged).

## 39. A department head's Team appraisals (DW-4d, 2026-10-13) — `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/appraisals.controller.ts` (`listRoute`) — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (appraisals.controller.db.test.ts on the Linux CI gate)**

**Why.** Plan §5.3: the Appraisals row's Team tab is for heads ("score my people; who is written, scored and signed"). Today `GET /api/:t/appraisals` serves three tiers:
- broad (HR, admin): every appraisal;
- `manager`/`team_lead`: only rows whose `managerUserId` is the caller;
- everyone else: their own, from `submitted` on.

A department head therefore sees only the appraisals assigned to them personally, never their department's: a division lead's reports are invisible to the head above. A caller whose only head role is `org_unit_lead` is refused outright (403), because the bulk Cerbos check carries no `unitAncestors` (the controller's own "HIER-2 boundary" note), while the registry's Team tab admits them (`unitCap appraisal.read`). A tab must never open a refusal (DW-D20).

**The head's list.** For a caller who holds `org_unit_lead` in this company (whether or not they also hold `manager`) and has no broad tier:
1. Their led scope is `loadLedUnitScope(c, tenant, userId, today, principal)`: the subtrees of every unit they lead, through a lead placement or an `org_unit_lead` grant, as of today in `REPORTS_TZ`. An empty scope falls through to the existing branches, never "everything". This is the same scope that narrows a head's report reads (TR-25), so a head sees the same people under Team appraisals as under Team reports.
2. Cerbos: `appraisal` read once, with the `unitAncestors` of one led unit. This confirms the caller is a lead there before anything is read; the subtree narrowing below is the server's job, as for the TR-25 report listing.
3. Rows: every appraisal whose subject's primary unit, as of today, is in the led scope, UNION every row whose `managerUserId` is the caller (their `manager` semantics are kept). The filters `cycleId` and `subjectId` apply to both. A subject outside the scope with no manager link to the caller is never returned. The `subjectId` filter cannot widen the scope.
4. The response shape is unchanged: `{appraisals: [{id, cycleId, subjectUserId, managerUserId, status, composite}]}`.

**Unchanged.** The broad tier, a plain member's own list, `GET /appraisals/mine`, `GET /appraisals/:id` (already ancestor-wired), and every write: scoring stays manager-of-subject, and finalising stays HR. Reading a list never grants a write.

**The UI.** `/appraisals` opens for a company-wide holder as today, or for a head through `leadsAnyUnitWith(me, "appraisal.read", tenant)`. A head sees the list and opens a row (the single read already admits them). Scoring controls keep their own gates.

**Proof (live Postgres + Cerbos on the CI gate, added to `appraisals.controller.db.test.ts`):**
- an `org_unit_lead`-only head of `d-web` gets 200 with exactly the `d-web` subtree's appraisals (a `d-web` division member's appraisal included, a `d-seo` subject's excluded);
- a head who also holds `manager` gets their unit's rows plus their manager rows, with no duplicates;
- `subjectId` of an out-of-scope subject returns an empty list;
- a plain member's list and the broad tier's list are unchanged.

## 40. Department KPIs: targets, condition and standing (DW-4e, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/dept-kpis*.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (4e-1: dept-kpis.test.ts, dept-kpis.controller.db.test.ts, src/rbac/cerbos-dept-kpi-target.test.ts and platform-ui dept-workspace-slugs.test.ts on the Linux CI gate)**

**Why.** Owner ruling DW-Q4: each department has its own KPIs. They are highlighted so everyone sees the department's condition and standing, and the head is always aware of it. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §5.5 and §5.6. This section is the engine (4e-1). The head's banner, the KPI tiles and the staff strip (DW-3k), the GM's departments by condition (DW-3i), the HOD notifications and digest (DW-4j) and the department appraisal (4e-3) read it.

### 40.1 The catalogue: one source, on the server
- `dept-kpis.ts` holds every KPI definition: `{key, label, unit: percent|count|minutes, direction: up_good|down_good, reader, suggestedTarget, suggestedTolerance}`. The starting sets are plan §5.5's table, keyed by workspace slug, exactly the `kpis` keys in `platform-ui/src/lib/workspaces.ts`; a parity test pins the two lists. The UI registry keeps labels for display order only. Values, targets and conditions come from this API.
- **A department's workspace** is resolved on the server the way `workspaceFor` does on the client: `deptSlug(node.name)`, then the functional slugs (HR, Finance, IT), then the company's pack, else generic. Both sides pin one golden table of names to slugs.
- **Readers.** A KPI's `reader` is either `report_fact` (a department-grain metric of the report document: `metricKey`) or `module` (a module read that does not exist yet). In 4e-1 only these have a reader:

  | KPI | Reader |
  |---|---|
  | projects-on-time | `delivery.milestone_hit_rate` (department) |
  | reopened-work-rate | `flow.reopen_rate` (department) |
  | overdue-tasks | `discipline.overdue_open` (department, point in time) |
  | check-in-compliance | `discipline.checkin_compliance` (department) |
  | utilization (GM) | `effort.capacity_utilization` (company) |
  | departments-in-good-condition (GM) | derived: the share of departments whose condition is on track |

  Every other starting-set KPI has `reader: module` and reads **unavailable** until its own ticket adds the read. A KPI is never given a number it does not have.

### 40.2 Targets: the head proposes, the approver approves
- **Table** `dept_kpi_targets`: `tenant_id, unit_node_id, kpi_key, effective_from (a month start), target numeric, tolerance numeric, status (proposed|approved|rejected|superseded), note, proposed_by, proposed_at, decided_by, decided_at`. RLS, origin_site, tenant-scoped like every reports table.
- **In force for a period.** The latest `approved` row for (unit, KPI) whose `effective_from` is on or before the period's start. A newer proposal changes nothing until it is approved, so "last period's target stays in force". With no approved row the KPI reads `targetSource: "none"` and has no condition. The catalogue's suggested target only pre-fills a proposal; it is never in force.
- **Targets are levels** (a rate, or a point-in-time count). The same target applies to a month, a quarter, a semester or a year, so the period selector needs no per-kind targets.
- **Who may act.** A new Cerbos kind `dept_kpi_target`, resource attributes `unitAncestors`, with these actions:
  - `read`;
  - `propose`: `org_unit_lead` of the unit or an enclosing one, plus the company-wide tier;
  - `approve` and `reject`: the approver. **Default approver: the `company_admin` tier, which `owner` mirrors.** Every head's lead position also carries `manager` company-wide, so `manager` cannot mean "the GM". Whether the Office of the GM's lead seat should also approve is an owner decision, recorded here as open.
  - A proposer can never approve their own proposal (checked in the service, 409).
- **Endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/:t/dept-kpis/targets {unitNodeId, kpiKey, effectiveFrom, target, tolerance, note?}` → 201 `{id, status: "proposed"}`. A KPI not in the unit's set → 400. A month that is not a month start → 400.
  - `POST /api/:t/dept-kpis/targets/:id/approve` or `/reject {note?}` → 200. Approving supersedes the previous approved row from the same `effective_from` on. Every proposal and decision writes an activity row.
  - `GET /api/:t/dept-kpis/targets?unitNodeId=` → each KPI's in-force row, open proposals and history.

### 40.3 Condition
- **Per KPI**, given a value and an in-force target (with `direction`):
  - **on track**: at or better than the target;
  - **at risk**: worse than the target, but within `tolerance`;
  - **off track**: worse by more than `tolerance`;
  - **unavailable**: no reader, no data (a ratio with denominator 0, or a window with no facts), or no target. Its `reason` says which.
- **The department**: off track if any KPI is off track or two are at risk; at risk if one is at risk; on track if at least one KPI has a condition and none is worse; unavailable if no KPI has a condition. "Trending to miss" (plan §5.5) is deferred: it needs a projection rule, and none is guessed.
- **Read:** `GET /api/:t/dept-kpis?unitNodeId=&periodKind&start[&end]` → `{unit, workspace, period, condition, kpis: [{key, label, unit, direction, value, numerator?, denominator?, target, tolerance, targetSource, condition, reason?}]}`. The period follows the reporting blueprint's rules (all calendar kinds, custom up to 400 days). Values come from the department report document for that unit and period, so the numbers match the Reports page.
  - **Who may read:** the people placed in the unit (the "quiet strip" for staff), its heads, and the company-wide tiers. Anyone else gets 403. A department's KPIs are never shown to another department's staff (§5.5: no league table for staff).
- **Standing (GM and HR only):** `GET /api/:t/dept-kpis/overview?periodKind&start` → every department of the company with its condition, worst first, then by name. Only the company-wide tiers may read it.

### 40.3a As built (4e-1, 2026-10-14)

Files: `dept-kpis.ts` (catalogue, slug resolution, condition rules; pure), `dept-kpi-targets.ts` (targets and reads), `dept-kpis.controller.ts` (routes), migrations `202610140800_dept_kpi_targets.sql` and `202610140810_iam_dept_kpi_target_permissions.sql`, policy `resource_dept_kpi_target.yaml` (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §38). Where the text above left a choice open, this is what was built:
- **Scales.** `percent` values, targets and tolerances are fractions (0.85 = 85%), the scale of the report document's `value`; a percent proposal outside 0..1 is 400. `minutes` is a duration (`client-approval-turnaround`, `time-to-hire`). `assets-delivered` is a volume, so it has no suggested target (`null`).
- **Readers.** `reader` is `report_fact`, `module`, or `derived` (`departments-in-good-condition` only). The GM's derived KPI counts the OTHER departments, each with its condition computed without any derived KPI (so two GM-workspace units can never depend on each other).
- **No data.** A report_fact KPI is `no_data` when the metric is absent, when a ratio's denominator is 0, or when the whole window precedes the tenant's first fact date (`warnings.precedesFactHistory.affectedDays >= dayCount`). A count of 0 is a real 0. Reason precedence: `no_reader`, then `no_data`, then `no_target`. Comparisons allow 1e-9 so a gap exactly equal to the tolerance (0.85 vs 0.8 with 0.05) is at risk.
- **Codes.** Conditions are `on_track`, `at_risk`, `off_track`, `unavailable`; `targetSource` is `approved` or `none`.
- **Unit read** `GET /dept-kpis?unitNodeId=&periodKind&start[&end]` → `{unit: {id, name}, workspace, period: {periodKind, start, end}, condition, kpis: [{key, label, unit, direction, value, numerator?, denominator?, target, tolerance, targetSource, condition, reason?}]}`. `value`, `target` and `tolerance` are `null` when absent. `unitNodeId` missing → 400 (`field: "unitNodeId"`).
- **Who may read a unit.** Cerbos `read` (tenant-wide: company_admin, manager, member, viewer, the HR read tier, owner through its permission arm), then the handler: the caller's primary unit TODAY is in the unit's subtree (a division's staff read their department, never the reverse), or the caller is in the `unit_scoped` person-axis tier and `loadLedUnitScope` holds the unit, or the caller is company-wide (`personAxisTier` unrestricted/company_wide, plus `owner` of the company). Else 403 `outside your reporting line`; then an id outside the org tree is 404 `{error: "unit_not_found", field: "unitNodeId"}`.
- **Overview** `GET /dept-kpis/overview?periodKind&start[&end]` → `{period, departments: [{unit, workspace, condition, kpis}]}`: every `department` node (nested ones included), `off_track`, `at_risk`, `on_track`, then `unavailable` last; ties by name, then id. Company-wide tiers only (the same set as above); anyone else 403.
- **Targets list** `GET /dept-kpis/targets?unitNodeId=` (the unit read's gate) → `{unit, workspace, asOf, kpis: [{key, label, unit, direction, suggestedTarget, suggestedTolerance, inForce, proposals, history}]}`. `asOf` is the current month start in `REPORTS_TZ`; `history` is every decided row (approved, rejected, superseded), newest month first. Rows of a KPI no longer in the unit's set are not listed. A row: `{id, unitNodeId, kpiKey, effectiveFrom, target, tolerance, status, note, proposedBy, proposedAt, decidedBy, decidedAt}`.
- **Propose** authorizes first (the unit's ancestry from the closure), then validates the body (`effectiveFrom` not `YYYY-MM-01` → 400, `tolerance < 0` → 400), then the unit's existence (404) and its set (400). `owner` cannot propose unless it also holds company_admin or leads the unit (no propose mirror: PERMISSION-CONTRACT §38). The HR tier cannot propose.
- **Approve / reject** → 200 with the row and `superseded: [ids]`. Order: Cerbos `read` (tenant gate), the row (404), the proposer approving their own → 409 `cannot_approve_own_proposal` (before the approve check, so a proposing head meets the 409), Cerbos `approve`/`reject` (403), a row no longer `proposed` → 409 `not_proposed`. **Supersede rule:** approving marks every approved row of the same (unit, KPI) whose `effective_from` is on or after the new row's month `superseded`; earlier approved rows stay approved and keep governing their months. The decision `note` is kept in the activity row's metadata (the table has one `note`, the proposer's).

### 40.4 Not in 4e-1
- The UI: the targets screen and the KPI tiles (4e-2, with DW-3k and DW-3i).
- Module readers for the other KPIs (one ticket each, owned by the module's tracker). **DW-D25 (owner, 2026-10-14):** the delivery departments' readers are DW-6's, written as §40.5; the functional departments' and the GM's are DW-7's, written as §40.6. Each plugs into the catalogue's `reader` and returns `{value, numerator?, denominator?}` or null.
- The department appraisal per cycle: HOD commentary and GM assessment (4e-3, its own section).
- Condition snapshots, change notifications and the weekly digest (DW-4j, §43).

**Proof (live Postgres + Cerbos on the CI gate):**
- the catalogue/registry parity and the slug golden table;
- a head proposes for their unit (201) and is refused another unit (403);
- the head cannot approve their own proposal (409);
- a non-approver's approve is refused (403);
- an approved target is in force from its month and the previous one before it;
- a KPI's condition at each boundary (equal to target, inside tolerance, outside);
- the department rule (one at risk, two at risk, one off track, all unavailable);
- `unavailable` for a module KPI, for a ratio with a 0 denominator and for no target;
- staff of the unit may read and staff of another unit may not;
- the overview is company-wide tiers only, worst first.

### 40.5 Delivery-department readers (DW-6n, 2026-10-14) — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (all twelve readers and the seam, each with a live-Postgres test on the Linux CI gate; see §40.5.8)**

**Why.** DW-D25 moved the delivery departments' twelve `module` KPIs to DW-6. Today each one reads `unavailable` (`no_reader`). This section gives each a reader over data the modules already write, so the §40 engine, targets, conditions, the §41 appraisal and the §43 watch pick the numbers up with no other change. DW-D27 (owner, 2026-10-14) settles the four definitions the data could not settle on its own.

#### 40.5.1 The seam (shared with §40.6; reviewed by DW-4)
- **Catalogue.** `KpiReader`'s `module` arm gains an optional `readerId`: `{ kind: "module"; readerId?: string }`.
  - With no `readerId`, nothing changes: `unavailable`, `no_reader`.
  - With one, the KPI behaves like a `report_fact` KPI. A value gives a condition against the target; `null` gives `unavailable` with `no_data`.
  - Reason precedence stays `no_reader` > `no_data` > `no_target` (§40.3a), so `null` is `no_data` before `no_target`.
  - `dept-kpis.ts` stays pure: the id is a string.
- **Registry.** A new file, `modules/reports/dept-kpi-readers.ts`, holds `MODULE_KPI_READERS: Record<string, ModuleKpiReader>`.
  - `type ModuleKpiReader = (ctx: ReaderCtx) => Promise<KpiValue | null>`.
  - `ReaderCtx = { tenantId: string; unitId: string; periodKind: ReportPeriodKind; start: string; end: string; asOf: string }`.
  - `start` and `end` are the engine's range: ISO dates, both INCLUSIVE, in `REPORTS_TZ`.
  - DW-6's readers live in `dept-kpi-readers/delivery.ts` and DW-7's in `dept-kpi-readers/functional.ts`. The registry merges the two.
- **A reader is pure over its inputs.** It never reads the clock.
  - `evaluateUnits` computes `asOf` once per evaluation: the earlier of `end` and today in `REPORTS_TZ`.
  - Every "already due" test uses `asOf`. So the page, the §41 appraisal history and the §43 watch agree for the same inputs, and a past window is fixed for good.
  - **"Already due"** means a due date on or before `asOf` (for a timestamp, before the end of `asOf`'s day). An item due today and not delivered counts as late today.
- **Parity.** A test pins that every `readerId` in the catalogue has a registered reader, and every registered reader is named by exactly one catalogue entry. A typo is then a failed build, never a silent `no_reader`.
- **Engine.** `evaluateUnits`, pass 1: for a `module` KPI with a `readerId`, `v = await MODULE_KPI_READERS[id](ctx)`. `kpiRead` passes `numerator` and `denominator` through as it does for `report_fact`.
- **A reader that throws fails only ITS KPI.** It reads `unavailable` with a new reason, **`read_failed`**, and the error is logged with the reader id, never the row data.
  - The department's other KPIs, the page, the appraisal and the watch carry on. The department condition already treats `unavailable` as having no condition.
  - The §43 watch stores a move to `unavailable` silently, so a flaky reader never notifies a head.
  - `read_failed` joins `UnavailableReason` in `dept-kpis.ts` and the UI's reason words in `platform-ui/src/lib/deptKpiFormat.ts` (plus the demo catalogue).
  - It also needs a migration that widens `dept_kpi_conditions.reason`'s CHECK (`202610150200_dept_kpi_watch.sql`), or the watch's upsert would fail on the first one.
- **A module the tenant does not have is not an error.** The reader answers `null` (`no_data`).
  - It is GATED at registration on `isModuleEnabled(tenantId, module)` (`modules/registry.ts`: the company's own `enabled_modules` or an active service assignment, the platform's one rule).
  - The module wall is not enough on its own: `app_module_allowed()` checks only the scopes the query DECLARES, not whether the company has the module, so a company that turned a module off would otherwise still read its old rows (found while building n2/n7–n9).
- **The window.** A reader turns `[start, end]` into the instants `[start 00:00, end + 1 day 00:00)` in `REPORTS_TZ`. Every timestamp test below uses that half-open interval, and every date test (`needed_by`, a due date) uses the inclusive date range.
- **Each reader** queries through `withTenants([tenantId], fn, { modules })`, declaring its module walls.

#### 40.5.2 The department's scope (one definition for every reader)
- **S(u):** the unit itself and every `org_unit_closure` descendant of it in the tenant. This is the `departmentFilterSql` rule of §33 (`core/department-filter.ts`), so the clients and deliverables pages and these KPIs agree.
- **The department's clients C(u):** clients with at least one project, not deleted, whose `department_id` is in S(u), excluding internal clients (`clients.is_internal`). This is §33's client rule.
- **Rows that carry a unit directly** use it, never the client route: `work_requests.to_unit_id` and `creative_assets.department_id`.

#### 40.5.3 The twelve readers

| # | Workspace · key | Reader id | Value | Numerator / denominator | `null` (no data) when | Walls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| n1 | web-dev · `requests-within-sla`, relabelled **"Requests delivered by the date needed"** (DW-D27) | `webdev.requests_delivered_by_needed` | numerator ÷ denominator | Denominator: `work_requests` of kind `engineering`, `to_unit_id` in S(u), not deleted, status `open` or `delivered`, `needed_by` inside the window, and already due or delivered. Numerator: those `delivered` with `closed_at`'s date (`REPORTS_TZ`) on or before `needed_by`. | denominator 0 | tenant |
| n2 | web-dev · `client-site-uptime` | `monitoring.client_uptime` | the pooled ratio of `UPTIME_RATIO_SQL` (`monitoring.controller.ts`, reused, never copied) | Over `monitor_results` in the window, of enabled, not-deleted monitors whose client is in C(u). Numerator: results `up`. Denominator: results not `maintenance` or `unknown`. | no counted result | `monitoring` |
| n3 | seo · `clients-ranking-growth` | `search.clients_ranking_growth` | numerator ÷ denominator | For each client in C(u) with a `search_properties` row: the keywords `(keyword_id, engine, device)` ranked (position not null) both in the last non-simulated `search_rank_snapshots` at or before the window's first instant AND in the last one before its end. A client "grew" when its mean position over those keywords fell (a lower number is better). Denominator: clients with at least one such keyword. Numerator: those that grew. | denominator 0 | `search` |
| n4 | seo · `client-reports-on-time` | `search.client_reports_on_time` | numerator ÷ denominator | `search_reports` of engagements whose client is in C(u), with period `YYYY-MM`, due on **the 5th of the following month** (DW-D27, end of that day in `REPORTS_TZ`), the due date inside the window, and delivered or already due. Numerator: `delivered_at` on or before the due date. | denominator 0 | `search` |
| n5 | seo · `ad-budgets-on-pace` | `search.ad_budgets_on_pace` | numerator ÷ denominator | **DW-D27: a campaign's `budget_minor` is a MONTHLY budget.** Judged in the month that contains `asOf`, from its 1st to `asOf`. Over campaigns `live` in that month, with a budget above 0, of engagements whose client is in C(u), and at least one non-simulated daily metrics row in that month: spend is the sum of `cost_minor` from the 1st to the as-of day, and expected is `budget_minor × days elapsed ÷ days in the month`. **On pace: 0.9 ≤ spend ÷ expected ≤ 1.1.** A campaign whose metrics currency differs from its budget currency is left out. | denominator 0 | `search` |
| n6 | seo · `client-retention` | `clients.retention` | numerator ÷ denominator | **The cohort:** clients in C(u) that were active on the window's first day. Active on a day D means one of: a `signed` contract with its start `≤ D` and `ends_on` null or `≥ D`; or a project in S(u) with its start `≤ D` and status `active`, `planned` or `on_hold`. A project with no `start_date` starts on its `created_at` date, and a contract with no `starts_on` on its `signed_at` date (most projects are created without a start date). **Retained:** active on `asOf`. A superseding contract continues its predecessor. | empty cohort | tenant |
| n7 | social-media · `posts-on-schedule` | `social.posts_on_schedule` | numerator ÷ denominator | `social_post_variants` not deleted, not `native_import`, not `cancelled`, with `scheduled_at` inside the window, whose engagement's client is in C(u), and published or already due. Numerator: `published_at ≤ scheduled_at + 15 minutes`. The 15 minutes is a documented default, not a ruling. | denominator 0 | `social` |
| n8 | social-media · `client-approval-turnaround` | `social.client_approval_turnaround` | the mean of `decided_at − requested_at`, in minutes | No numerator or denominator (an average, not a share). Over `social_post_client_reviews` with status `approved` or `changes_requested`, `decided_at` inside the window, and the client in C(u). | no decided review | `social` (variant join) |
| n9 | social-media · `engagement-growth` | `social.engagement_growth` | `(cur − prev) ÷ prev` (can be negative) | Over `social_accounts` whose client is in C(u): `cur` is the sum of `social_metrics_daily.engagements` over the dates `[start, asOf]`, and `prev` the sum over the same number of days just before `start`. So a running month is compared like for like, never month-to-date against a whole month. Counts only accounts with a non-null `engagements` value in both windows; the sums are pooled across them. | no such account, or `prev` = 0 | `social` |
| n10 | creatives · `asset-requests-on-time` | `creatives.asset_requests_on_time` | numerator ÷ denominator | As n1, with kind `assets`. | denominator 0 | tenant |
| n11 | creatives · `revision-rounds` | `creatives.revision_rounds` | rounds ÷ groups | Version groups (`COALESCE(version_group_id, id)`) of `creative_assets` with `department_id` in S(u), whose APPROVED round's `decided_at` is inside the window. Value: the mean number of that group's rounds that ended `changes_requested`. `withdrawn` and `superseded` are not revisions, and a first-time approval counts 0. No numerator or denominator. | no approved group | tenant |
| n12 | creatives · `assets-delivered` | `creatives.assets_delivered` | a count | **DW-D27: a delivered asset is a version group approved in review** in the window, counted once, `department_id` in S(u). A count of 0 is a real 0 when the department has creative assets at all. | the department has no creative asset at all | tenant |

#### 40.5.4 What the numbers cannot say (said in the UI's notes, never hidden)
- **n1, n10** count only requests that carry a `needed_by` date.
- **n4** counts reports that exist. A month in which no report was drafted is not counted as late, because no record says one was due. A per-engagement cadence would close this gap; that is a later ticket, not in scope.
- **n5:** the SEO tracker's pacing view (design §630, `sm-budget-pacing`) must adopt the same rule when it is built (DW-D27).
- **n6** infers churn from contracts and projects; `clients.status` keeps no history.
- **n8** sees only each variant's LATEST approval round. A re-request overwrites the earlier one (`UNIQUE (variant_id)`), so a turnaround series over a period that included re-requests is understated. Logging the rounds would fix it; that is a later ticket.
- **n9:** each network defines "engagement" its own way, so this is growth on each network's own measure, pooled.
- **n12:** an asset never sent for review is not counted as delivered.
- **n6:** a window that has not begun (`asOf` before `start`) reads `null`.
- **n7:** a variant whose post was deleted is not counted.

#### 40.5.5 Labels
Only n1's label changes, and its key stays `requests-within-sla`, so stored targets, conditions and alerts carry over. The label changes in:
- the server catalogue (`dept-kpis.ts`);
- the UI registry row (`workspaces.ts`);
- the demo catalogue (`demoDeptKpis.ts`);
- the plan's KPI table;
- the sumopod e2e pin in `workspace-shell.spec.ts`.

#### 40.5.6 Proof (live Postgres + Cerbos on the Linux CI gate)
For each reader, seeded rows that exercise:
- a row inside the window and one outside it at each boundary (the first instant, the last instant, `end + 1 day 00:00`);
- a row of a unit outside S(u) and of a client outside C(u) (never counted);
- an internal client (never counted);
- another tenant's row (never counted);
- the `null` case;
- the walled module turned off for the tenant (`null`, never an error).

Plus:
- n2's value equal to `uptimeRatio()` over the same results;
- the seam's parity test, and a throwing reader reading `read_failed` while its department's other KPIs still read (with the watch storing it);
- the engine reading a registered reader (a value gives a condition; `null` gives `no_data`);
- unregistered `module` KPIs still giving `no_reader`.

#### 40.5.7 Tickets
One reader per ticket, in this order:
1. **n0:** the seam.
2. **The four READY readers:** n10, n11, n12, n7.
3. **Then:** n2, n1, n3, n4, n6, n5, n9, n8.

Each lands as its own fast-forward with green CI on its exact sha.

#### 40.5.8 As built (DW-6n, 2026-10-14)
Built by three agents in parallel, each from `dw/6n-base`, reviewed and wired by the integrator. Code is in `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/`.
- **The seam:**
  - `dept-kpi-readers.ts`: the registry, `setModuleKpiReadersForTests` and `readerParityProblems`.
  - `dept-kpi-readers/types.ts` and `scope.ts`: S(u), C(u) and the window.
  - The engine change in `dept-kpi-targets.ts`, as reviewed by DW-4:
    - `evaluateUnits(…, targetsAsOf, today)`, where the §43 watch passes the day of its own `now`;
    - a unit's module readers run concurrently, and one that throws reads `read_failed`.
  - Migration `202610150400_dept_kpi_conditions_read_failed.sql`.
  - The UI's reason words; `overviewDepartments`' allow-list also needed `read_failed`.
- **The readers** are in `dept-kpi-readers/delivery/`, registered in `delivery/index.ts`. Each one's test is a `*.db.test.ts` beside it, run on live Postgres:
  - `work-requests-on-time.ts` (n1, n10);
  - `monitoring-uptime.ts` (n2);
  - `search.ts` (n3, n4, n5);
  - `client-retention.ts` (n6);
  - `social.ts` (n7, n8, n9);
  - `creative-reviews.ts` (n11, n12).
- **The module gate.** Readers over a module's tables (n2 `monitoring`; n3, n4 and n5 `search`; n7, n8 and n9 `social`) are wrapped by `gated()` in `delivery/index.ts`. Its test is `delivery/index.test.ts`.
- **Decisions made while building:**
  - **n11** counts only the current approval cycle: the `changes_requested` rounds after the group's previous approved round and before this one.
  - **n11 and n12** take the department from the approved version's own asset, and a deleted approved version is not counted.
  - **n3** compares the last real (non-simulated) snapshot at or before the window's first instant with the last one before its end. Keywords are keyed `(keyword_id, engine, device)`.
  - **n5** uses exact integer arithmetic for the 0.9 to 1.1 band. A NULL metrics currency counts as a mismatch.
  - **n9** compares `[start, asOf]` with the same number of days before `start`.
- **Tests:** shared seeding for the social and uptime tests is `src/testing/dept-kpi-seed.ts`. Every timestamp test builds its boundaries from `REPORTS_TZ` (Asia/Makassar in the suites), so nothing assumes UTC.

## 41. The department appraisal per cycle (DW-4e-3, 2026-10-15) — `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/dept-appraisals*.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (backend: dept-appraisals.test.ts, dept-appraisals.controller.db.test.ts and src/rbac/cerbos-dept-kpi-target.test.ts on the Linux CI gate; UI: platform-ui deptAppraisalFormat.test.ts, demoDeptAppraisals.test.ts, deptAppraisals.test.ts, AppraisalView.test.tsx and rbac.test.ts on the CI gate)**

**Why.** Plan §5.3 and §5.5 (owner ruling DW-Q4): each department has its own appraisal. The cycle's department appraisal is the department's KPIs over the appraisal period, with the result against each target, the condition history, the head's commentary and the GM's assessment. The Appraisals › Department tab shows it next to how the people's appraisals went. It is not a person's score, and a department KPI is never pinned on one person.

### 41.1 What it reads (no new numbers)
- **The cycle** is a `report_appraisal_cycles` row: `name`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `status`.
- **KPIs over the cycle:** the §40 engine on a custom range `[period_start, period_end]` (capped at 400 days, as every report range is). The result against each target uses the target in force for the cycle's LAST month.
- **Condition history:** the §40 engine run for each calendar month inside the cycle, with that month's in-force target. Each entry is the month and the department's condition, plus each KPI's condition. It is computed on read; nothing is snapshotted, so it always agrees with the KPI page. Months before the tenant's first fact read `unavailable` (`no_data`).
- **The people's appraisals:** `report_appraisals` of this cycle whose subject's primary unit is in the department's subtree today (the §37 roster rule), aggregated only:
  - `total`, and the counts by `status` (`draft`, `submitted`, `acknowledged`, `disputed`, `finalized`);
  - the composite distribution: counts of submitted-or-later rows by rounded score band (1 to 5). It is withheld (`distribution: null, reason: "too_few"`) when fewer than 3 rows are scored, so no individual's score can be read from it;
  - no names, no individual scores, no commentary.

### 41.2 What it stores
- **Table** `dept_appraisals`: `tenant_id, cycle_id, unit_node_id, hod_commentary, hod_by, hod_at, gm_assessment, gm_condition (on_track|at_risk|off_track, nullable), gm_by, gm_at, origin_site, created_at, updated_at`. Unique on (tenant, cycle, unit). RLS with the tenant and the `reports` module wall, like `dept_kpi_targets`.
- The row is created on the first write. A read with no row returns null commentary and assessment.
- **Writes end when the cycle is `closed`.** Both writes then get 409 `cycle_closed`. A closed cycle's department appraisal is the record.

### 41.3 Who may act
- **No new Cerbos kind.** Two actions are added to `dept_kpi_target`:
  - `appraisal_comment`: `org_unit_lead` of the unit or an enclosing one (through `unitAncestors`), plus `company_admin`;
  - `appraisal_assess`: the approver tier (`company_admin`, which `owner` mirrors), the same tier that approves targets (§40.2).
  - The permission keys are `reports.dept_kpi_target.appraisal_comment` and `.appraisal_assess`. They take the same six-artifact path and pins as §40, with no new kind.
- **Who may read:** the unit's heads (their led scope) and the company-wide tiers, including HR's people-reader tier. Staff of the unit may not read it: they read the KPI page (§40.3), not the appraisal. Anyone else gets 403, and an unknown unit or cycle gets 404, with the same order as §37.

### 41.4 Endpoints
- `GET /api/:t/dept-appraisals/cycles` → `{cycles: [{id, name, periodStart, periodEnd, status}]}`, the company's cycles for the picker, newest first (period end descending, then name), **never `draft`** (HR's preparation, not yet anyone's appraisal). Company-wide metadata, so no unit parameter. Gate: Cerbos `dept_kpi_target` `read` (the tenant gate), then the caller must be company-wide (HR's people-reader tier included) or lead a unit today (a non-empty `loadLedUnitScope`); anyone else, a plain member or a unit's staff, gets 403. No new permission key, and the appraisal administrators' `GET /appraisals/cycles` (`cycle_admin`) is untouched.
- `GET /api/:t/dept-appraisals?cycleId=&unitNodeId=` → `{cycle: {id, name, periodStart, periodEnd, status}, unit, workspace, kpis (the §40 shape over the cycle), condition, history: [{month, condition, kpis: [{key, condition}]}], people: {total, byStatus, distribution|null, reason?}, hodCommentary: {text, by, at}|null, gmAssessment: {text, condition, by, at}|null}`.
- `PUT /api/:t/dept-appraisals/:cycleId/:unitNodeId/commentary {text}`: needs `appraisal_comment`. `text` is 1 to 4000 characters.
- `PUT /api/:t/dept-appraisals/:cycleId/:unitNodeId/assessment {text, condition}`: needs `appraisal_assess`, and `condition` is one of the three. The GM's condition is their judgement, shown beside the computed one and never replacing it.
- Every write records an activity row.

### 41.5 The UI (same ticket)
- `/appraisals/department` gains a cycle picker (the company's cycles, newest first). With a cycle chosen, the page shows the department appraisal: the KPI results over the cycle, the history as a row of months, the people block (counts, and the distribution or "too few to show"), the head's commentary (editable by `appraisal_comment` while the cycle is open) and the GM's assessment (editable by `appraisal_assess`). Without a cycle, the page is the §40 KPI view, as built in 4e-2.
- The demo serves the same routes with one open cycle and one closed cycle.

**Proof (live Postgres + Cerbos on the CI gate):**
- the history agrees month by month with `GET /dept-kpis` for each month;
- the result uses the last month's in-force target;
- a head comments on their unit and is refused another unit (403);
- a non-approver's assessment is refused (403);
- writes on a closed cycle get 409 `cycle_closed`;
- the distribution is withheld below 3 scored rows;
- a subject outside the unit's roster is not counted;
- a unit's staff get 403;
- an unknown cycle or unit gets 404 for a company-wide caller.

### 41.6 As built (4e-3, 2026-10-15)

Files: `dept-appraisals.ts` (the reads, the writes and the pure helpers), `dept-appraisals.controller.ts` (routes, the cycles list included), migrations `202610150000_dept_appraisals.sql` and `202610150100_iam_dept_appraisal_permissions.sql`, the two new actions on `resource_dept_kpi_target.yaml` (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §38a); UI: `platform-ui/src/app/(app)/appraisals/department/page.tsx`, `components/deptkpis/AppraisalView.tsx` and `AppraisalForms.tsx`, `lib/deptAppraisals.ts`, `deptAppraisalFormat.ts`, `deptAppraisalActions.ts`, `demoDeptAppraisals.ts`. Where the text above left a choice open, this is what was built:
- **The engine is called, not copied.** The KPIs over the cycle are `evaluateUnits` (dept-kpi-targets.ts) on the cycle as one custom range (`resolveRange("custom", period_start, period_end)`, so a cycle longer than 400 days is 422 `range_too_large`), with a new optional `targetsAsOf` argument (default: the range's start, so §40 is unchanged) set to the start of the month that holds `period_end`. The history calls the same function once per calendar month.
- **History.** `month` is the month start (`YYYY-MM-01`). The months are `enumerateCalendarStarts("month", period_start, period_end)`: every calendar month the cycle TOUCHES, so a cycle that starts mid-month includes that month (at most 15 for a 400-day cycle). Each entry is judged against its OWN month's in-force target, so it equals `GET /dept-kpis` for that month. A month with no approved target or no data reads `unavailable`.
- **People.** The roster is `loadUnitRoster` over `collectUnitSubtree` as of TODAY in `REPORTS_TZ` (the §37 rule: a division's people count, a person who has left the unit or sits in another unit does not). `byStatus` always carries all five keys, zeros included. `distribution` is an array of five `{band, count}` (bands 1 to 5, the composite rounded and clamped) over the rows that are not `draft` and have a composite; with fewer than 3 such rows it is `null` with `reason: "too_few"`, and no band appears anywhere in the payload. The block carries counts only.
- **Read gate** (`GET`). Cerbos `read` with the unit's ancestry, then the narrowing: company-wide (`personAxisTier` unrestricted or company_wide, which includes HR's people-reader tier, plus `owner` of the company) or `loadLedUnitScope` holds the unit (a head); there is no "placed in the unit" branch, so a unit's staff get 403 `outside your reporting line`. Then the unit (404 `unit_not_found`, `field: "unitNodeId"`), then the cycle (404 `cycle_not_found`, `field: "cycleId"`; a malformed id is the same 404). Missing `cycleId` or `unitNodeId` is 400, before anything else. So a caller who may not read a unit learns nothing about the unit or the cycle.
- **Writes.** `PUT .../commentary` and `.../assessment`: the unit's ancestry from the closure, Cerbos (`appraisal_comment` / `appraisal_assess`, 403), then the body (400 `field: "text"` or `"condition"`; the text is trimmed and 1 to 4000 characters), then the unit (404), then the cycle (404). `cycle_closed` (409) is decided inside the write's own transaction, which locks the cycle row `FOR SHARE`, so a concurrent close either lands first (the write is refused) or waits for the write. A first write creates the (cycle, unit) row; later writes replace that half only. Response 200: `{hodCommentary: {text, by, byName, at}}` or `{gmAssessment: {text, condition, by, byName, at}}`, the same objects as the GET. `byName` (the author's display name, or null) is added to the contract's `{text, by, at}` so the page can say who wrote it.
- **Activity rows** (`writeActivity`, entity `dept_appraisal`, id = the row's): verb `commented` with `{cycleId, unitNodeId}`, verb `assessed` with `{cycleId, unitNodeId, condition}`. Never the text.
- **Table.** `dept_appraisals` has a surrogate `id` (for the activity log) beside the natural key; each half is all-or-nothing (text, author and time, or none: CHECK), `gm_assessment` and `gm_condition` come together, `gm_condition` is `on_track | at_risk | off_track` (never `unavailable`, which is the engine's).
- **UI.** `/appraisals/department?unit=&cycle=`: the picker reads `GET /dept-appraisals/cycles` through an honest reader (ok / forbidden / error). A refusal is said as a refusal and a failed read as a failure, never shown as an empty picker; "no cycles yet" is said only when the read was allowed and empty. The forms mirror the capabilities `reports.dept_kpi_target.appraisal_comment` (`canInUnit` over the unit's path, or company-wide `can`) and `.appraisal_assess` (`can`), and appear only while the cycle is not closed. The demo (`demoDeptAppraisals.ts`) serves the cycles list with the same gate, `demo-cycle-h2` (open) and `demo-cycle-h1` (closed, with a written commentary and assessment).
- **Not changed.** The capability inventory (`docs/modules/CAPABILITY-INVENTORY.md`) is unchanged: no MCP tool is registered, and the new HTTP suite names no registered route family in its URLs, so the generator's driver count stays as committed.

## 42. Google Drive: connect, pick and attach (DW-6i, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/core/google-drive/` (new) — **STATUS: BACKEND AND UI BUILT, PROTOTYPED (Google stubbed; live proof waits for DW-11 item 6)**

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-13-department-workspaces.md` §4.2 (DW-6i) and §14.1 (launch and return). A person connects their own Google Drive, picks a file with Google's own Picker, and the file is attached to a PM task as a link. The file stays in Drive; the ERP keeps a reference to it. The owner chose (2026-10-14) to build this before the OAuth client exists, against stubs, so that going live needs only the client.

### 42.1 What exists

- `google_drive` is already a provider in the credential vault (`integration_connections`) and in the shared Google OAuth state machine (`core/google-oauth/registry.ts`, `GOOGLE_PROVIDERS`).
- No surface registers it. Search's flow keeps Drive out on purpose (`isSearchGoogleProvider`), and the only OAuth callback is search's own.
- The Tools & connections page has a manual "Google Drive" row today. It records an email address with no credential behind it.
- Files attach to a PM task through the generic files table (`files`, target `task`, the PM task's id). A reference attach (`url`, no bytes) already exists in `core/files.controller.ts`.

### 42.2 Scope and consent

- **One scope:** `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file`, plus `openid` and `email` to show which account is connected.
  - `drive.file` reaches only the files a person picks with the Picker or that the app creates. It cannot list or read the rest of their Drive.
  - That keeps the app clear of Drive's restricted scopes and their security assessment. Check Google's current scope classification when building, and record the source in §42.8.
- **The credential is the person's own:** `owner_kind = 'user'`, `owner_id` = the person. Nobody else's Drive is ever reached.
- **The OAuth client is its own:** `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_REDIRECT_URI`. It is separate from search's client.
- **The Picker** also needs a browser API key and the Cloud project number (`GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_PICKER_APP_ID`).
- **When any of these is unset,** the feature reports `drive_not_configured`, and the UI says so. No default value is ever invented.

### 42.3 Connect and disconnect

- **The surface.** Register a `google_drive` surface in the shared registry: `module: null` (core), the scopes above, `ownerKind: "user"`, and an `authz` that lets a person create their own connection (the same rule the "My connections" rows use today).
- **`GET /api/:t/integrations/google-drive/oauth/start`** answers `{ authUrl }`.
  - The state row goes through the shared state machine, and the state is signed as search's is.
  - Consent asks for `access_type=offline`, so a refresh token comes back.
- **`GET /api/google-drive/oauth/callback`.** The tenant and the person come from the verified state, never from the query.
  - It exchanges the code through the shared token client (`token-endpoint-client.ts`), then seals the tokens in the person's `google_drive` row.
  - **One row per person:** if the manual row already exists, the tokens are added to it. The account email comes from the ID token, verified through the shared client.
  - It then redirects to the page the flow started from, with a coarse outcome flag, as search's callback does.
  - Every failure lands as a typed state failure: `drive_state_invalid`, `drive_consent_denied` or `drive_exchange_failed`. Never a 500 page.
- **`DELETE /api/:t/integrations/google-drive`** revokes the token at Google (best effort; the result is recorded) and clears the sealed tokens. Attachments already made stay: they are links.
- **The connection's status** is read as part of the Picker read (§42.4), or through the existing connections list. The token is never returned there.

### 42.4 Pick

`GET /api/:t/integrations/google-drive/picker` answers `{ configured, connected, accountEmail, accessToken, expiresAt, apiKey, appId }`, for the calling person only.
- **The access token** is refreshed first when it expires within 5 minutes; a failed refresh marks the connection `needs_reconnect`.
  - The Picker runs in the browser and needs a live token, so a short-lived `drive.file` token is the one secret this route returns.
  - The refresh token never leaves the server.
- **`Cache-Control: no-store`.** The route never logs the token.
- **When not connected or not configured,** it answers `connected: false` or `configured: false` with no token.

### 42.5 Attach

`POST /api/:t/integrations/google-drive/attach` with `{ targetType: "task", targetId, fileId }`:
- **Authorise first,** exactly as `POST /files` does: `file` · `create`, then `read` on the target. Validate after.
- **Read the file's metadata from Drive** with the person's own token: `GET https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{fileId}?fields=id,name,mimeType,webViewLink`. This proves the person can reach the file, and takes the real name and link from Drive rather than from the browser.
  - A file the token cannot reach answers 404 `drive_file_not_found`.
  - A refused or expired token answers 409 `drive_needs_reconnect`.
  - A Drive outage answers 502 `drive_unavailable`.
- **Write a reference file row** through the same path `POST /files` uses: `filename` = the Drive name, `content_type` = the MIME type, `url` = `webViewLink`, with no bytes. It answers 201 with the file row.
- **The same Drive file on the same task twice** answers 409 `drive_already_attached`.
- **Targets in v1:** PM tasks only (`task`). Other file targets can follow; the route checks `targetType` against a list of one.

### 42.6 UI

- **Tools & connections** (pilot page): the Google Drive block shows one of:
  - "Connect Google Drive", which starts §42.3;
  - the connected account's email with Disconnect;
  - "Reconnect", when `needs_reconnect`;
  - "Google Drive isn't set up for this ERP yet", when `configured: false`.
  - The manual email row is replaced by this block in the pilot. The classic page is unchanged.
- **The PM task's Attachments** gain "Attach from Google Drive" when the person is connected and the feature is configured.
  - It loads Google's Picker script (`https://apis.google.com/js/api.js`) only on click, opens the Picker with `drive.file` access, and posts each picked file to §42.5.
  - The new attachment shows with a Drive mark and opens in a new tab.
  - The global CSP today is only `frame-ancestors 'self'`, so the Picker needs no CSP change. If a stricter CSP arrives later, it must allow `apis.google.com`, `docs.google.com` and `drive.google.com`.
- **Every refusal is said in plain words.** None crashes the page.
