### 42.7 Tests (the Linux CI gate: Postgres and Cerbos), with Google stubbed at `fetch`

- **Unit:** the state round trip; the not-configured answers; refresh within 5 minutes; the token never in a response other than the Picker's, never in an error, never in an activity row.
- **HTTP:**
  - start, then callback with a stubbed token exchange; the manual row upgraded in place; one row per person;
  - disconnect clears the tokens and calls revoke;
  - the Picker read: `configured: false`, `connected: false`, a live token, a refresh, `needs_reconnect`;
  - attach:
    - authorisation before validation: a caller refused `read` on the task gets 403 even with a bad body;
    - another tenant's task answers 404;
    - a Drive file the token cannot reach answers 404 `drive_file_not_found`;
    - attaching the same file twice answers 409;
    - the written row carries Drive's own name, MIME type and link.
- **Fixtures** come from Google's documented response shapes: the OAuth 2.0 token response, Drive v3 `files.get`. Cite the doc URLs in the client's header.
- **UI vitest:** the connection block's four states; the attach button shown only when connected and configured; the Picker loader wired lazily, tested with a fake `gapi` and `google.picker`; the refusal sentences.
- **Live proof** waits for DW-11 item 6. It means connecting one real account, picking one file, attaching it to a task and opening it from the task.


### 42.8 As built (backend, DW-6i, 2026-10-14)

Google is STUBBED at `fetch` in every test; nothing here has met real Google (DW-11 item 6). The UI of §42.6 is the "As built (UI)" block below.

**Where it is.**
- `core/google-drive/` (new):
  - `surface.ts`: registers the `google_drive` surface (`module: null`, scopes `drive.file` + `openid` + `email`, `ownerKind: "user"`, `authz` = `integration_connection` · `create`, the self-service action `connectionAction("create", me, me)` gives for your own row). It registers when the file is imported, and the controller imports it.
  - `client.ts`: the one Drive client (`files.get`), the only file in the directory that touches the network.
  - `service.ts`: start, callback, disconnect, the live token and refresh, the Picker answer, attach.
  - `google-drive.controller.ts`: the routes and every authorisation (`GoogleDriveController`, and `GoogleDriveOauthCallbackController` for the one tenant-agnostic callback path).
- `core/google-oauth/` (shared, extended compatibly):
  - `token-endpoint-client.ts`: `TokenResponse` gains `idToken`; `exchangeAuthorizationCode`, `refreshAccessToken`, `revokeToken` and `buildAuthorizeUrl` take an optional `client` (a surface's own OAuth client). With none given they read `config.google` exactly as before.
  - `id-token.ts` (new, pure): reads the account from the ID token (see "ID token" below).
  - `hosts.ts`: `GOOGLE_DRIVE_API_HOST` and `isDriveApiUrl` (exact host `www.googleapis.com`, https, `/drive/v3/`, no userinfo, default port).
- `core/file-reference.ts` (new): the reference-attach write extracted from `POST /files` (the scrub of name and link, the 2048 cap, the INSERT, the `attached` activity row). `files.controller` calls it with no options; `files-reference.test.ts` pins its behaviour. Drive's attach calls it with `rejectDuplicateUrl`, which takes an advisory lock so two simultaneous attaches of one file cannot both pass.
- `config.ts`: `config.googleDrive` (`clientId`, `clientSecret`, `redirectUri`, `pickerApiKey`, `pickerAppId`) and `googleDriveConfigured()` (all five, or false). No defaults. `app.module.ts` registers both controllers. No migration: `google_drive` was already an allowed provider, and an `owner_kind = 'user'` row already fits.
- Env: `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_DRIVE_REDIRECT_URI`, `GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_PICKER_APP_ID` are documented in `platform-nest/.env.example` and `infra/compose/.env.example`, and passed through in `infra/compose/docker-compose.vps.yml` beside `GOOGLE_OAUTH_*` (which are passed through there).

**Routes** (no new Cerbos kind; no policy change):

| Method | Path | Answer | Authz |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/:t/integrations/google-drive/oauth/start` | `{ authUrl }` | `integration_connection` · `create`, `ownerId` = the caller |
| GET | `/api/google-drive/oauth/callback?code&state` (or `error`) | `{ status: "connected", accountEmail }` or `{ status: "denied", reason: "drive_consent_denied" }` | the surface's `authz`, against the TENANT IN THE VERIFIED STATE, before the state is spent |
| DELETE | `/api/:t/integrations/google-drive` | `{ disconnected, revokedAtGoogle }` | `integration_connection` · `delete`, own row |
| GET | `/api/:t/integrations/google-drive` | `{ configured, connected, needsReconnect, accountEmail }`: the status alone, read from the row (no token; Google is never called) | `integration_connection` · `read`, own row |
| GET | `/api/:t/integrations/google-drive/picker` | `{ configured, connected, needsReconnect, accountEmail, accessToken, expiresAt, apiKey, appId }`, `Cache-Control: no-store` | `integration_connection` · `read`, own row |
| POST | `/api/:t/integrations/google-drive/attach` | 201, the file row | `file` · `create`, then `task` · `read`, as `POST /files` |

**Errors.** Each puts its token at the START of `message` and repeats it in `reason`: `drive_not_configured` (503), `drive_state_invalid` (400), `drive_exchange_failed` (502), `drive_not_connected` (409), `drive_needs_reconnect` (409), `drive_file_not_found` (404), `drive_unavailable` (502), `drive_already_attached` (409), `target_not_found` (404), `unsupported_target_type` (400), `bad_drive_file_id` (400) and `user_required` (400).

**Docs used** (all read on 2026-10-14; the fetch tool summarises a page, so the quoted lines are its report of each page):
- OAuth 2.0 for web server apps, https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server: the token response is `access_token`, `expires_in`, `refresh_token` ("only present ... if you set the `access_type` parameter to `offline`"), `scope` and `token_type` (always `Bearer`). Revoke is `POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke`, form-encoded, body parameter `token`, success is HTTP 200. `prompt=consent` is what re-issues a refresh token.
- OpenID Connect, https://developers.google.com/identity/openid-connect/openid-connect: the token response also carries `id_token`. `iss` must be `https://accounts.google.com` or `accounts.google.com`, `aud` must be the app's client id, and `exp` must be in the future. `email` is present only when the `email` scope was granted, and `sub` is the stable identifier.
- Drive v3 `files.get`, https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/get: `GET https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{fileId}`. That page does not document `fields`; it is documented at https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/fields-parameter (a comma-separated list).
- The File resource, https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files: `id`, `name`, `mimeType` and `webViewLink` ("Output only. A link for opening the file in a relevant Google editor or viewer in a browser").
- Drive errors, https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/handle-errors: 401 (`authError`), 403 (usage limits and privileges), and 404 `notFound` ("the user doesn't have read access to a file, or the file doesn't exist"). The body is `{ error: { code, message, errors: [{ reason }] } }`.

**Scope classification: `drive.file` is NOT restricted (it is not even sensitive).**
- Source: https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/api-specific-auth, read 2026-10-14. It lists `drive.file` under "Non-sensitive scopes", with `drive.appdata`, `drive.appfolder` and `drive.install`. "Sensitive" holds `drive.apps.readonly`. "Restricted" holds `drive`, `drive.readonly`, `drive.activity`, `drive.activity.readonly`, `drive.meet.readonly`, `drive.metadata`, `drive.metadata.readonly` and `drive.scripts`. The `drive.file` row reads: "Create new Drive files, or modify existing files, that you open with an app".
- Cross-check: https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/scopes (Drive API v3) describes `drive.file` as "See, edit, create, and delete only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app" and `drive` as "See, edit, create, and delete all of your Google Drive files". That page has no sensitivity column, so the classification above rests on the Drive page alone.
- So the build needed no stop. A test (`google-drive.test.ts`) pins that the surface asks for no Drive scope wider than `drive.file`.

**ID token.** The shared client had no ID-token handling, so `id-token.ts` adds it. The callback reads the account's email (and `sub`) from the ID token the token endpoint returned to OUR authenticated POST, and checks `iss` (the two documented spellings), `aud` (our Drive client id), `exp`, and that `sub` and `email` are present. It does NOT verify the JWT signature: Google's own page says a token that came directly from the token endpoint over HTTPS, in a request carrying the client secret, is authentic without it. That is the only way a token reaches the function; it is never taken from a browser. The ID token is read once and dropped (never stored, never returned). Any failure is `drive_exchange_failed` and seals nothing.

**Deviations from §42** (each is deliberate):
1. **The callback answers JSON; it does not redirect.** §42.3 says it redirects "as search's callback does", but search's backend callback does not. Google's redirect is a top-level navigation that cannot carry the `Authorization` header `AuthGuard` needs, so the URL registered as `redirect_uri` is a page the FRONT END owns. That page calls the backend callback as an ordinary authenticated request and then redirects with the coarse flag (`platform-ui/src/app/api/search/google/callback/route.ts` is that page for search). The Drive UI ticket must do the same. The backend answers the coarse outcome (`connected` or `denied`) and never a token.
2. **Consent denied is a 200 `{ status: "denied", reason: "drive_consent_denied" }`**, as search's is, not an error: pressing Cancel is a normal OAuth outcome. The same answer covers a granular-consent token that lacks `drive.file` (the person unticked Drive access): it cannot power the Picker, so nothing is sealed. `drive_state_invalid` and `drive_exchange_failed` are errors (400, 502).
3. **The Picker answer has one extra field, `needsReconnect`** (true when the connection exists but Google refused it), so the UI can show "Reconnect" without a second read. `connected` is false then.
4. **"needs_reconnect" is not a new status.** The vault's status CHECK has no such value, so the row is set to status `error` (the vault's own state for a credential that stopped working) with `meta.driveNeedsReconnect = true`. The tokens are kept (a read path must not shred a credential). A successful reconnect clears the flag.
5. **A failed refresh marks the row only when Google REFUSES it** (the token endpoint answers 4xx, such as `invalid_grant`, or there is no refresh token to use). A token-endpoint outage (network, 5xx) answers `502 drive_unavailable` and does not mark the row, since the grant may be fine.
6. **Attach: a Drive 401 earns one forced refresh and one retry** before `409 drive_needs_reconnect` (the token may have been revoked or rotated since it was stored). A Drive 403 that is a usage limit is `502 drive_unavailable`; any other 403 is `404 drive_file_not_found` (with `drive.file`, a file the person did not pick answers as 404 or 403).
7. **Added error tokens**: `drive_not_connected` (409, no usable connection), `unsupported_target_type`, `bad_drive_file_id` and `target_not_found`. The Drive link is accepted only when it is `https` on a Google host (it is opened in a new tab).
8. **Order of the attach checks:** `file` · `create`; `task` · `read` (with the id when it is usable); then the `targetType` list of one. So a caller who may not read tasks is refused 403 even for an unsupported `targetType`. The task must exist in the tenant (404 `target_not_found`, which is also what another tenant's task answers); only then is `fileId` validated.
9. **Target `task` covers BOTH task tables** (corrected in review, `42c5e37c`).
   - The PM task page (`TaskDetailView`, which loads its task through `getPmTask`) shows a `pm_tasks` row, and attaches files as target `task` with that PM task's id. The legacy base `tasks` rows use the same target.
   - The attach's existence check therefore accepts either table. The first build checked base `tasks` only, which would have refused every real PM task.
   - `POST /files` itself checks no existence, only `task` · `read`.
10. **The attach answer is the file row in the shape `GET /files` lists** (snake_case: `id`, `filename`, `content_type`, `byte_size`, `scrubbed`, `uploader_id`, `created_at`) plus `url`, `target_entity_type` and `target_entity_id`. The `attached` activity row carries `source: "google_drive"` and `driveFileId` beside the usual `fileId` and `filename`; never a token.
11. **`Pragma: no-cache`** is sent beside `Cache-Control: no-store` on the Picker answer.
12. **The Drive call and the token calls use `config.google.timeoutMs`** and the shared `config.google` endpoints. Drive has no endpoint seam of its own: its host is a constant, and `isDriveApiUrl` refuses any other.
13. **A status read with no token** (added in review). The Picker read refreshes the token when it is near expiry, so a page that only needs to know whether to offer Drive would wait on Google's token endpoint on every view.
   - `GET /api/:t/integrations/google-drive` answers `{ configured, connected, needsReconnect, accountEmail }` from the row alone. It never unseals or refreshes a token and never calls Google.
   - The Tools & connections block and the task page's "Attach from Google Drive" gate read it. Only the click that opens the Picker reads the Picker answer.
   - `connected` there means a credential is held and the connection is not flagged. A refresh Google refuses is found on that click, which flags the row, and the next status read says `needsReconnect`.

**For the UI ticket.**
- `GET /api/:t/files` now returns `url` (added in review, `42c5e37c`; NULL for an uploaded file), so an attachment can be opened from the list. `FileMeta.url` carries it in the UI.
- The Picker script and the CSP note of §42.6 are unchanged and wait for the live proof.

**As built (UI, DW-6i, 2026-10-14).** In `platform-ui/src`; none of it has met real Google (DW-11 item 6).
- **The redirect URI the owner registers at Google (`GOOGLE_DRIVE_REDIRECT_URI`) is `<ERP origin>/api/google-drive/callback`**, for example `https://erp.gaiada.com/api/google-drive/callback`. The route is `app/api/google-drive/callback/route.ts`; the path is `DRIVE_CALLBACK_UI_PATH` in `lib/drive.ts`.
  - It reads `code`/`state`/`error` off its own URL, calls the backend `GET /api/google-drive/oauth/callback` as the signed-in person (§42.8 deviation 1), and redirects to the page the flow started from with `driveOAuth=connected|denied|error`. It adds `driveOAuthReason=<token>` only when the backend refused with one of its own known tokens.
  - The return path comes ONLY from a short-lived httpOnly cookie (`HOST_COOKIES.driveOAuthPending`, set by `startDriveConnectAction`, 10 minutes) and is re-validated by `sanitizeReturnTo` where the redirect is issued. No query parameter is ever a redirect target. With no cookie it still completes the connection and lands on `/departments`.
- **Readers and actions.**
  - `lib/drive.ts`: pure; the shapes, route paths, the token-to-sentence map `driveErrorText`, the outcome line, `isDriveUrl`.
  - `lib/drive-data.ts`: `readDriveStatus`, a `ReadResult` of the token-free status route (`GET /api/:t/integrations/google-drive`, deviation 13). It never reads the Picker route.
  - `lib/driveActions.ts`: start, disconnect, `loadPickerCredentialsAction`, attach.
  - `lib/drivePicker.ts`: the Google loader. `lib/drive-pending.ts`: the cookie.
- **Tools & connections** (pilot): `components/departments/DriveConnectionBlock.tsx` replaces the manual Drive row in the pilot with the four states and the outcome line. Classic is unchanged (it keeps the manual row).
- **PM task page:** `components/drive/DrivePicker.tsx` ("Attach from Google Drive") sits inside `components/Attachments.tsx`, shown only when `readDriveStatus` says `configured && connected`.
  - On click it loads `https://apis.google.com/js/api.js` once, opens the Picker (multi-select) with a FRESH token, posts each picked id to the attach route in turn, then `router.refresh()`.
  - A file with a `url` opens it in a new tab (`rel="noopener noreferrer"`), with a Drive mark for `drive.google.com` and `docs.google.com` links.
- **The access token** is read only by `loadPickerCredentialsAction` on the click, held in that closure, and never stored, logged or passed as a page prop. The page's own read (`readDriveStatus`) never sees it.
- **Deviations from §42.6:**
  - (1) The attach button's gate and the connection block read the token-free status route (deviation 13), so a page view never mints a token or waits on Google. The click alone reads the Picker answer, for a fresh token.
  - (2) The OAuth landing adds the optional `driveOAuthReason` beside the coarse flag, whitelisted to the backend's own tokens.
  - (3) A new pending-flow cookie rather than reusing search's, because that one's parser only accepts a search provider.
  - (4) No CSP was changed: the global CSP is `frame-ancestors 'self'` only, so the Picker is not blocked.

**Tests** (the Linux gate; Google stubbed at `fetch`): `core/google-drive/google-drive.http.test.ts` (Postgres and Cerbos), `google-drive.test.ts`, `client.test.ts`, `egress.test.ts`, `core/google-oauth/id-token.test.ts`, the extended `core/google-oauth/egress.test.ts`, and one added case in `core/files-reference.test.ts`. The secret rule is asserted twice: over every response the HTTP suite received (an access token only in a Picker answer, nothing else anywhere) and over every table the run wrote (activities, events, files, state rows, the connection's non-secret columns). The vault columns hold only `enc:v1:` envelopes. The capability inventory (`docs/modules/CAPABILITY-INVENTORY.md`) is unchanged: `inv-drivers.mjs` reports no owner row that differs.

## 43. The head is made aware: condition changes, off-track alerts and the weekly digest (DW-4j, 2026-10-15) — `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/dept-kpi-watch*.ts` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (4j-1: dept-kpi-watch.test.ts, dept-kpi-watch.controller.db.test.ts, seed/automation.test.ts and mcp-hub automation-policy.test.ts on the Linux CI gate; 4j-2: deptKpiAlertFormat.test.ts, deptKpiAlerts.test.ts, deptKpiAlertActions.test.ts, queue.test.ts, queueUrgency.test.ts, demoDeptKpis.test.ts, NeedsMeQueue.test.tsx, NeedsYouBlock.test.tsx and KpiAlerts.test.tsx on the Linux CI gate; 4j-3 backend: dept-kpi-digest.test.ts and dept-kpi-digest.controller.db.test.ts on the Linux CI gate; 4j-3 UI: deptKpiDrivers.test.ts, deptKpiDriverFormat.test.ts, BehindTheMiss.test.tsx, the department page.test.tsx and the extended demoDeptKpis.test.ts on the Linux CI gate)**

**Why.** Plan §5.5, "How the HOD is made aware", items 2 and 3, and the 4j row of §5.6. The §40 engine computes a condition on read and remembers nothing, so nothing can say "it changed". This section adds:
- the memory (the last condition seen);
- the scheduled run that n8n drives (reporting blueprint §10: n8n schedules, the platform exposes an endpoint, and platform-nest gains no timer);
- the Inbox notification;
- the Needs-you item;
- the weekly digest.

It ships in three tickets:
- **4j-1**, backend: §43.1 to §43.6;
- **4j-2**, the UI: §43.7;
- **4j-3**, the digest and the "behind the miss" read: §43.8.

### 43.1 Who is told: the department's heads
- A department's heads are the users who hold `org_unit_lead` scoped to that department's node **exactly**: a `user_roles` row with `scope_type = 'org_unit'` and `scope_id` equal to the node id.
  - The row comes either from the position reconciler (a lead seat's `own_unit` role) or from a direct grant. It is the same authority that Cerbos and `loadLedUnitScope` use.
  - Not told: the leads of enclosing units (the GM reads the company Overview), a `manager` placed in the unit, and a `positions.is_lead` seat that carries no grant.
- One function computes this: `loadUnitLeadUserIds(tenantId, unitNodeId)`. A DB test pins it against the forward direction: every user it returns has the unit in their `loadLedUnitScope`.
- `notify()` already skips a recipient who is no longer an active member of the company. A department with no head is told nothing, and the run lists it in `unitsWithoutHead`.

### 43.2 What is evaluated
- **The period** is the current calendar month to date in `REPORTS_TZ`. That is the default of the KPI page and of the Overview.
- **The engine** is `evaluateUnits` over every `department` node, exactly as `GET /dept-kpis/overview` computes it. So a notification always agrees with what the head sees when they open the page. The GM workspace's unit is evaluated like any other.

### 43.3 The memory: `dept_kpi_conditions`
- **Columns:** `tenant_id, unit_node_id, kpi_key, period_start, condition, reason, value, target, evaluated_at, changed_at, origin_site`.
- **`kpi_key`** is the KPI's key, or `'*'` for the department's own condition. It is never NULL, because NULL defeats the unique key.
- **Unique** on (tenant, unit, kpi_key). There is one row per (unit, KPI), holding the last state seen. It is not a history; the history is recomputed on read, as §41 does.
- **RLS** with the tenant and the `reports` module wall, like `dept_kpi_targets`. `origin_site` has no default.

### 43.4 The change rule
The rule is pure: `classifyChange(previous, next)` returns `tell` or `store`. It applies to each KPI and to the department.
- **No previous row** (the first run, a new KPI, a new department): store, and tell nothing. A deploy never floods the Inbox.
- **Tell** when the new condition is real (`on_track`, `at_risk` or `off_track`) and either:
  - the previous one was a different real condition, in either direction (worse, or back); or
  - the previous one was `unavailable` and the new one is `at_risk` or `off_track`.
- **Store silently** in every other case:
  - no change;
  - anything to `unavailable` (a new month with no data yet, a target withdrawn, a failed reader);
  - `unavailable` to `on_track`.
- **A new month is not a change in itself.** The comparison is condition to condition:
  - if the condition is the same across the month boundary, nothing is told;
  - if the new month starts `unavailable` (no data yet) and then turns at risk or off track, that is told, because it is the month's first real reading.

**One notification per unit per run**, sent only when the unit has something to tell:
- `type: "dept_kpi.condition_changed"`.
- `title`: the department's condition now, e.g. "Web Dev: off track".
- `body`: one line per change told, e.g. "Projects on time: at risk → off track (71% against 85%)", plus the department line when the department changed.
- `href`: `/appraisals/department?unit=<id>`.
- `severity`: `critical` if the department or any KPI told is now off track; `warning` if at risk; `info` when every change told is an improvement.
- No `entityType`, so the Inbox opens no thread panel. No person is named, and the numbers are department-level ones the head already reads on the KPI page (blueprint §11).

**Once, under retries:**
- The run evaluates first (read-only).
- It then decides and writes in one transaction under a per-tenant transaction advisory lock, and notifies after the commit.
- So a retried or doubled run tells each change once. This covers n8n's retries and the bridge's redelivery.
- A crash between the commit and the notification loses that notification rather than doubling it, and it is logged.

### 43.5 Off-track alerts: the Needs-you item
- **Table `dept_kpi_alerts`:** `id, tenant_id, unit_node_id, kpi_key, opened_at, period_start, value, target, acknowledged_by, acknowledged_at, ack_note, resolved_at, resolved_condition, origin_site`.
  - There is one open alert per (unit, KPI), enforced by a partial unique index `WHERE resolved_at IS NULL`.
  - RLS and the module wall are as in §43.3. An alert is never deleted.
- **Opened** by the run when a KPI is `off_track` and has no open alert. An alert is a state, not a change, so the first run opens alerts for KPIs that are already off track; it does not notify.
- **Resolved** by the run when the KPI is no longer `off_track`. Any other condition counts, `unavailable` included, and `resolved_condition` records which.
- **Acknowledged** by a head: `POST /api/:t/dept-kpis/alerts/:id/acknowledge {note?}`, where `note` is up to 1000 characters.
  - It records who and when. The alert leaves Needs you but stays open until the run resolves it.
  - Acknowledging twice → 409 `already_acknowledged`. A resolved alert → 409 `resolved`. An unknown id → 404.
- **Read:** `GET /api/:t/dept-kpis/alerts`.
  - **Without `unitNodeId`:** the open, unacknowledged alerts of the units the caller heads (§43.1's rule, applied to the caller). This is the Needs-you source. A caller who heads no unit gets 200 `{alerts: []}`, and that is true: they have none.
  - **With `unitNodeId`:** the unit read's gate (§40.3a). Every alert of that unit (open, acknowledged, resolved), newest first, up to 100.
  - **A row:** `{id, unit: {id, name}, kpiKey, kpiLabel, kpiUnit, periodStart, openedAt, value, target, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedByName, acknowledgedAt, ackNote, resolvedAt, resolvedCondition}`.
- **Who may acknowledge:** a head of the alert's unit (§43.1) or the company-wide tier. The check order is Cerbos `read` with the unit's ancestry, then that narrowing, else 403. No new Cerbos kind or action (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §38b).

### 43.6 The scheduled run
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/:t/dept-kpis/watch` → 200 `{period: {start, end}, evaluatedUnits, told: [{unitNodeId, recipients, changes}], alertsOpened, alertsResolved, unitsWithoutHead}`.
  - Gate: Cerbos `report_admin` · `recompute`, the action `POST /reports/facts/recompute` uses (company_admin and platform_admin). It sits behind the reports module guard. No new Cerbos kind or action.
  - Two runs in a row: the second tells nothing.
- **Flow:** `automation/workflows/reports-kpi-watch.json`, daily at 06:30, after `reports-nightly-facts` at 02:00.
  - It follows the shape of every reports flow: one tenant through `$env.AGENCY_TENANT_ID`; the service token with OBO `wf:reports-kpi-watch`; retry 3; an error branch to the hub `notify`.
  - It needs a new automation account in `seed/automation.ts` (company_admin, like the other reports accounts) and the hub allowlist entry `["notify"]` in `mcp-hub/src/automation-policy.ts`, with its pinned test.
  - Importing the flow on the server is a server step. A CLI import deactivates the flow, so it must be activated after the import.
- **No mail.** The new types stay out of `MAIL_NOTIFICATION_TYPES`; the plan asks for the Inbox.

### 43.6a As built (4j-1, 2026-10-15)

Files: `dept-kpi-watch.ts` (the pure rules, the run, the recipients and the alert reads and write), `dept-kpi-watch.controller.ts` (the three routes), migration `202610150200_dept_kpi_watch.sql` (both tables), `automation/workflows/reports-kpi-watch.json`, the account in `seed/automation.ts`, the allowlist entry in `mcp-hub/src/automation-policy.ts`. The KPI controller's unit read gate is now an exported function, `authorizeUnitRead` in `dept-kpis.controller.ts` (the class method delegates to it, behaviour unchanged), so the alerts read applies that exact gate and not a copy. No Cerbos, permission-catalog or `MAIL_NOTIFICATION_TYPES` change. Where the text above left a choice open, this is what was built:
- **A current grant** (§43.1) is, in SQL: `roles.name = 'org_unit_lead' AND user_roles.scope_type = 'org_unit' AND user_roles.scope_id = <node id> AND (user_roles.expires_at IS NULL OR user_roles.expires_at > now())`, the exact conjunct `assemblePrincipal` applies, so the recipients are the people Cerbos and `loadLedUnitScope` see as heads. `user_roles` has no tenant column and no revoked flag (a revoke deletes the row). **One addition to the text:** the holder must also be an ACTIVE member of the company (`company_memberships.tenant_id = <tenant> AND deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'active'`, read in a tenant transaction after the global grant read, because `company_memberships` is tenant-RLS'd and reads zero rows under `withGlobal`), because `user_roles` is global and an org node id such as `d-hr` can exist in two companies, so without it a head of company B's `d-hr` would be told company A's numbers. It also makes `unitsWithoutHead` honest (a department whose only head has left is listed). The forward pin is the DB test: every returned head has the unit in `loadLedUnitScope`, and the reverse is shown to be wider on purpose (an enclosing head and a placed manager have the unit in their led scope and are not told).
- **Functions:** `loadUnitLeadUserIds(tenantId, unitNodeId)` (sorted, distinct), `loadLeadUserIdsByUnit(tenantId, unitIds)` (the batch the run uses) and `loadUnitsLedExactly(tenantId, userId)` (the same rule applied to the caller, for the Needs-you read). All three read `user_roles` through `withGlobal`, from one shared SQL conjunct.
- **The period** is `resolveRange("month", <first day of the current month in REPORTS_TZ>)`, so `period.end` is the month's last day, exactly what `GET /dept-kpis/overview?periodKind=month&start=` computes. The service takes an optional `now` (`runDeptKpiWatch(tenantId, now?)`); the route takes none.
- **The lock** is `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('dept_kpi_watch:' || tenant_id))`, the first statement of the module-walled tenant transaction. The memory and the open alerts are read after it is held, so a concurrent run waits and then reads the first run's committed state.
- **The memory** is `dept_kpi_conditions` with `UNIQUE (tenant_id, unit_node_id, kpi_key)`; every run upserts every (unit, KPI) and every unit's `'*'` row in one statement (`evaluated_at` moves each run, `changed_at` only when the condition changes; `period_start` is the run's month start). Rows for a KPI or unit that is no longer evaluated are left in place (a memory, not a history).
- **The change rule** is `classifyChange(previous: KpiCondition | null, next): "tell" | "store"`, table-tested over all 16 pairs and "no previous". The plan (`planWatch`, pure) tells a KPI only when it also had a previous row; the department's own row is judged the same way. A unit with a told change gets ONE notice; its body is the KPI lines in the workspace set's order, then `Department: <from> → <to>` when the department changed. `severity`: `critical` when anything told is now off track, else `warning` when anything told is now at risk (an off track KPI that improved to at risk is still `warning`), else `info`. `href` is `/appraisals/department?unit=<encodeURIComponent(id)>`. The text uses the KPI catalogue's labels and a server port of `deptKpiFormat.ts` (a percent as a whole percent, a duration as `45 d`, `3h 20m` or `45 min`, a count to two decimals); three golden lines are pinned in `dept-kpi-watch.test.ts`. A line has no numbers when the KPI has no value or no target.
- **Sending.** After the commit, per head, `notifyBestEffort(tenantId, null, headIds, "dept_kpi.condition_changed", payload)` (`actorId` null: a scheduler). The payload is exactly `{title, body, href, severity}` (plus the `actorId: null` that `notify` adds). A unit with something to tell and no head is stored and told to nobody.
- **Alerts.** Opened for an off track KPI with no open alert (`ON CONFLICT ... WHERE resolved_at IS NULL DO NOTHING` behind the lock). Resolved when the KPI's condition now is anything but off track; an open alert whose unit stopped being a department, or whose KPI left the unit's workspace set, resolves as `unavailable`, so a stale item never stays in Needs you. `resolved_condition` is the condition then read.
- **The run returns** `{period: {start, end}, evaluatedUnits, told: [{unitNodeId, recipients, changes}], alertsOpened, alertsResolved, unitsWithoutHead}`. `recipients` and `changes` are COUNTS (heads addressed; KPI changes plus one for the department), never user ids. `told` lists only units that had a head to tell. `unitsWithoutHead` is every evaluated department with no head today, sorted by id (not only those that had something to tell), so the list doubles as a roster audit. No per-row activity is written. A run with no org tree evaluates 0 units and returns empty lists.
- **The gate** of the run is `authorize(principal, {kind: "report_admin", tenantId}, "recompute")`, called as `POST /reports/facts/recompute` calls it; the body is ignored.
- **The alerts read.** Without `unitNodeId`: Cerbos `read` on the tenant, then the open, unacknowledged alerts of the units the CALLER heads exactly (`loadUnitsLedExactly`), newest first, no limit. So an enclosing unit's head, a placed manager and the company-wide tiers who head no unit get `200 {alerts: []}`; a caller with no role gets 403 from Cerbos. With `unitNodeId`: `authorizeUnitRead` (§40.3a: Cerbos `read` with the unit's ancestry, then placed or led or company-wide, 403, then 404 `unit_not_found`), every alert of the unit, newest first, at most 100; an empty `unitNodeId=` is 400. A row's `kpiLabel` and `kpiUnit` come from the catalogue for the unit's current workspace; for a KPI the workspace no longer has, `kpiLabel` is the key and `kpiUnit` is `null`; a unit missing from the tree reads as its id. `acknowledgedByName` is the user's display name or `null`.
- **Acknowledge.** Order: Cerbos `read` on the tenant (403), the alert (404 `{error: "alert_not_found", field: "id"}`, a malformed id is the same 404), Cerbos `read` with the alert's unit ancestry plus the narrowing (a head of that unit per `loadUnitLeadUserIds`, or `isCompanyWide`, else 403 `outside your reporting line`), the state (409 `resolved` first, then 409 `already_acknowledged`), the body (400 `field: "note"` when `note` is not a string or has over 1000 characters; the stored note is trimmed and an empty one is stored as none). The write's own `UPDATE ... WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL AND resolved_at IS NULL` decides a race, and a lost race returns the same 409. The 200 body is the alert row of the read. The activity row (`writeActivity`, entity `dept_kpi_alert`, verb `acknowledged`, metadata `{unitNodeId, kpiKey}`) never holds the note.
- **Tables.** Each of `acknowledged_by`/`acknowledged_at` and `resolved_at`/`resolved_condition` is whole or absent (CHECK); `dept_kpi_alerts.kpi_key` can never be the `'*'` sentinel; the unique key of the memory has `kpi_key` NOT NULL. Both tables carry the tenant and `reports` module walls on USING and WITH CHECK, FORCE RLS, `origin_site` with no default; the DB test proves the rows are visible under the module scope, invisible without it, and invisible to another tenant.
- **The flow.** `reports-kpi-watch.json`: cron `30 6 * * *`, one POST with the Bearer service token and OBO `wf:reports-kpi-watch`, `retryOnFail` 3 tries (5 s apart), no hub call on success; the error branch calls the hub `notify` with type `reports_kpi_watch_failed`. The account is `wf:reports-kpi-watch` (company_admin) and the hub allowlist is `["notify"]`. Both are pinned: `seed/automation.test.ts` drives the route as that identity, `automation-policy.test.ts` pins the scope.
- **Tests.** `dept-kpi-watch.test.ts` (pure) and `dept-kpi-watch.controller.db.test.ts` (live). The DB suite drives the run through the service with a pinned `now` (September and October 2026, so it does not depend on the wall clock) and the routes through `app.inject`.
- **Known gap (recorded at landing).** A grant carries a node id and no company. The membership conjunct stops a head of another company's `d-hr` from being told, unless that person is an active member of both companies. Node ids are per company today; putting the company on a grant is an IAM-wide question, not this section's.
- **The flow's id** is `wsrptkpiwatch001`, so a CLI re-import replaces the flow instead of adding a copy.

### 43.7 The UI (4j-2)
- **Needs you** gains the source `GET dept-kpis/alerts` (open, not acknowledged).
  - It is a new queue item type `alert`, labelled "KPI off track", with the approval tier's rank.
  - It is decidable by the head with one action, **Acknowledge**, with an optional note. Its href is the unit's KPI page.
  - A failed read goes to `partialSources` and is never shown as an empty claim.
  - The exhaustive label maps (`NeedsMeQueue.tsx` and the department decisions page) gain the type.
- **The KPI page** shows a KPI's open alert ("Off track since 3 Oct · acknowledged by Ayu") and the unit's alert history.
- **The Inbox** needs no change: it renders title, body, href and severity.

### 43.7a As built (4j-2, 2026-10-15)

Files: `lib/deptKpiAlertFormat.ts` (types, pure formatters, the row guard), `lib/deptKpiAlerts.ts` (the two readers), `lib/deptKpiAlertActions.ts` (the acknowledge server action), `components/deptkpis/KpiAlerts.tsx` and `AcknowledgeAlert.tsx`, the Needs-you rows in `components/dashboard/NeedsMeQueue.tsx`, the source in `lib/queue.ts`, the rank in `lib/queueUrgency.ts`, and the demo routes in `lib/demoDeptKpis.ts`. No backend change. Where the text above left a choice open, this is what was built:
- **Readers** are `getMyKpiAlerts(userId, tenantId)` and `getUnitKpiAlerts(userId, tenantId, unitNodeId)`, with the house `(user, tenant)` argument order. Each returns ok / forbidden / not_found / error and refuses a row of the wrong shape as an error. A typed 404 (`unit_not_found`) is `not_found` in both; a BARE 404 (the `reports` module is dark) is `not_found` for the personal read and an `error` for the unit read, whose page has already read the unit.
- **The queue source** treats `forbidden` and `not_found` as "no alerts for this person in this company", not as a lost source, because naming them would put a permanent "some sources could not be read" note on every company without the module. Any `error` goes to `partialSources` as "KPI alerts". The id is `alert:${companyId}:${alertId}`; `originId` is the alert id; `origin` stays unset (no decide endpoint). Title "Projects on time is off track · Web Dev", `meta` "72% against 90%" (none when the KPI has left the workspace), `href` `/appraisals/department?unit=<encoded id>`, `createdAt` = `openedAt`, `decidable` true. It ranks with the approval tier and reads as a NOW item.
- **Acknowledge** is `acknowledgeKpiAlert(tenantId, alertId, note?)`, taking the company as an argument because Needs you spans companies. It trims the note, sends none when empty, refuses over 1000 characters before the call, and words only the two 409 codes (`already_acknowledged`, `resolved`); every other sentence is the server's, as sent. On success it revalidates `/`, `/departments`, the department and functional Overviews and `/appraisals/department`. The row UI takes it as an optional `acknowledge` prop (Home variants and the Overview block); without it an alert row offers "Open" only. The row leaves the list at once and returns with the server's sentence if refused.
- **Where alerts show.** Needs you on the Home and the Overview, and the GM console's Decisions tab (listed with approvals and gates, link "Acknowledge"). The Home's "Approvals" filter chip and the console rail's "Waiting on me" stay approvals and gates only, and the company Overview's Decisions block is unchanged.
- **The KPI page** reads the unit's alerts in parallel with the KPIs, not bound to the period. A tile with an open alert shows "Off track since 3 Oct" and " · acknowledged by Ayu" once acknowledged. The Alerts card below the tiles lists the history newest first, with the state in words (Open / Open, acknowledged / Resolved), the reading when it opened, who acknowledged it and the note, and how it resolved ("Back on track on 9 Oct", "Improved to at risk on ...", "Resolved (unavailable) on ..."). Days are UTC calendar days. Forbidden shows nothing; error and not found say the alerts could not be loaded; an empty ok read says "No alerts yet". The Acknowledge button sits on the history row of an open, unacknowledged alert only (not duplicated on the tile), and is offered when the page's `propose` or `approve` mirror holds (the head of the unit, or the company-wide tier); the server decides.
- **Demo.** Creatives (`dept-2`) has an open alert on its off-track KPI "Asset requests delivered on time" (72% against 90%, opened 3 Oct). Nobody in the demo heads Creatives, so no demo user's Needs you shows it; `demo-hansel` and `demo-owner` (company-wide) read and may acknowledge it on the Creatives KPI page. Web Dev has history only (it has no off-track KPI): one alert acknowledged by `u-webhead` ("Ketut Arta") with a note and resolved as back on track, and one resolved as `unavailable` that nobody acknowledged. `u-webhead`'s Needs you is honestly empty. No existing demo condition, lead or target changed.

### 43.8 The weekly digest and "behind the miss" (4j-3)
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/:t/dept-kpis/digest {weekStart?}`, with the same gate as the run. The default is the last complete ISO week in `REPORTS_TZ`.
- **One Inbox row per head** of each department, `type: "dept_kpi.weekly_digest"`:
  - `title`: e.g. "Web Dev this week: at risk";
  - `body`: one line per KPI that has a condition, giving the week's value against its target and its condition, plus the change from the week before, with "no data" said as such. The KPIs with no reader are summed up in one line ("4 KPIs not measured yet");
  - `href`: the KPI page with that week as its period.
- **Ledger** `dept_kpi_digests (tenant_id, unit_node_id, week_start, sent_at, recipients)`, unique on (tenant, unit, week_start). A retried run never sends twice.
- **The top contributors to a miss stay on the page, not in the Inbox row.** A notification links and never carries person-grain data (blueprint §11, and the weekly-seal flow's precedent).
  - The KPI page gains "Behind the miss" for each KPI that is at risk or off track, visible to the unit's heads and the company-wide tiers only.
  - Read: `GET /api/:t/dept-kpis/drivers?unitNodeId=&kpiKey=&periodKind&start` → `{kpi, drivers: [{kind: "project" | "person", id, name, value, numerator?, denominator?}]}`, at most 5, worst first.
  - Projects on time lists the projects with missed milestones, because the metric has no person grain. Reopened work, overdue tasks and check-in compliance list people, from the person-grain rows the Team report already shows the head (§37).
  - A unit's staff get 403: they never see a ranking.
- **Schedule:** a second trigger in the same flow, Mondays at 07:00.

### 43.8a As built (4j-3 backend, 2026-10-15)

Files: `dept-kpi-digest.ts` (the week rule, the text and the run), `dept-kpi-drivers.ts` (the drivers read), the two routes in `dept-kpi-watch.controller.ts`, migration `202610150500_dept_kpi_digests.sql` (the ledger), the second trigger in `automation/workflows/reports-kpi-watch.json` and its `automation/README.md` row. The head-only unit read gate is now an exported function, `authorizeUnitHeadRead` in `dept-kpis.controller.ts`, extracted from the department appraisal's `authorizeRead` (the appraisal controller's private method now delegates to it, behaviour unchanged), so the drivers read applies that exact gate and not a copy. No Cerbos, permission-catalog, `MAIL_NOTIFICATION_TYPES`, automation-account or hub-allowlist change. Where the text above left a choice open, this is what was built:

**The digest**
- **The week.** `weekStart` is optional. Absent or `null`, it is `lastCompleteWeekStart(today)`: the Monday on or before today in `REPORTS_TZ`, one week back (a Monday morning gives the week that ended yesterday; a Sunday night still gives the week before, because this week is not over until the day is). Given, it must be a string, a real calendar date written `YYYY-MM-DD`, a Monday, and not later than that default; the current week and any future week are not complete. Every other case (a non-Monday, `2026-02-30`, `""`, a number, an object, a future week) is 400 `field: "weekStart"`. The body is read AFTER the gate, so a non-admin sending a bad body gets 403. The service takes an optional `now` (`runDeptKpiDigest(tenantId, weekStart?, now?)`); the route takes none. `weekEnd` is `weekStart` plus six days, the same as `resolveRange("week", weekStart).end`.
- **The evaluation** is `evaluateUnits` over every `department` node for `resolveRange("week", weekStart)` (the week's value, condition, and the target in force at the week's start: exactly `GET /dept-kpis?periodKind=week&start=`), and, for the departments that have a head, the same for the week before. `evaluatedUnits` counts the departments evaluated for the week, heads or not. The week before is read as the engine reads it, so a week before the tenant's first fact date, or with no milestone due, reads "no data".
- **The claim** runs in ONE module-walled tenant transaction whose first statement is `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('dept_kpi_digest:' || tenant_id))` (the watch's key is `dept_kpi_watch:...`, so the two never block each other). One statement then inserts a ledger row for every department that has a head, `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, unit_node_id, week_start) DO NOTHING RETURNING unit_node_id`; the rows returned are the departments told, the others are `alreadySent`. The commit comes BEFORE the notifications: a crash between the commit and a send loses that notification and never doubles it. A department with no head is never claimed, so a head appointed later still gets that week's digest on the next run. The heads are the §43.1 rule (`loadLeadUserIdsByUnit`), read once before the claim; `recipients` in the ledger is their count then.
- **The notification** is `notifyBestEffort(tenantId, null, headIds, "dept_kpi.weekly_digest", payload)` (`actorId` null: a scheduler), one call per department, each head in its own try/catch. The payload is exactly `{title, body, href, severity}` (plus the `actorId: null` that `notify` adds), no `entityType`.
  - `title`: `<unit name> this week: <on track | at risk | off track | unavailable>`, the department's condition that week. A department with nothing measured still gets its notification ("Web Dev this week: unavailable") with only the summing-up line as its body.
  - `severity`: the watch's `noticeSeverity` applied to the department's condition (`critical` off track, `warning` at risk, else `info`).
  - `href`: `/appraisals/department?unit=<encodeURIComponent(id)>&periodKind=week&start=<weekStart>`.
  - `body`: one line per KPI that has a condition, in the workspace set's order, then at most one summing-up line, joined by a newline.
    - KPI line: `<label>: <value> against <target> · <condition word> (<change>)`, the values formatted by `formatKpiValue` (imported from `dept-kpi-watch.ts`, not copied: a percent as a whole percent, a duration as `45 min` / `3h 20m` / `2.5 d`, a count to two decimals). The separator is U+00B7 (middle dot) with a space either side.
    - `<change>` is `▼ 6 pts from the week before` or `▲ 5 pts from the week before` for a percent: the difference between the two WHOLE percents the head reads (71% against 77% is 6), so the line is arithmetically consistent with its own numbers. For a count or a duration it is the difference in the KPI's own unit, formatted as the value is (`▲ 1.5 from the week before`, `▼ 3h 20m from the week before`). When there is nothing to show at the precision the value is shown at (equal, or equal once rounded: a percent difference of 0 whole points, a count difference under 0.005, a duration difference under half a minute) it reads `no change from the week before`, never a zero with an arrow. When the week before had no value (no reader, no data, or no fact history) it reads `no data the week before`.
    - Summing-up line: the KPIs with condition `unavailable`, counted by reason, only the non-zero ones, in the order `no_reader`, `no_target`, `no_data`, joined by `"; "` in ONE line: `4 KPIs not measured yet; 2 KPIs have no target; 1 KPI has no data`, with the singular forms `1 KPI not measured yet`, `1 KPI has no target`, `1 KPI has no data`. A reason the code does not know (a later engine can add one, such as a failed reader) is counted last, in generic words: `2 KPIs could not be read`; it is never dropped and never an error. (The text said "ONE line, e.g. ... and ..."; the counts are read as parts of one line, not as one line each.)
  - No person is named and no person-level number appears; a DB test scans every digest payload for the seeded people's names, their name parts and their ids.
- **The ledger** `dept_kpi_digests (tenant_id, unit_node_id, week_start date, sent_at timestamptz default now(), recipients int, origin_site)`, `UNIQUE (tenant_id, unit_node_id, week_start)`. `week_start` has a CHECK that it is a Monday (`extract(isodow ...) = 1`) and `recipients` a CHECK that it is above 0, so a stray date can never open a second row for one week and an empty claim is never recorded. Tenant and `reports` module walls on USING and WITH CHECK, FORCE RLS, `origin_site` NOT NULL with no default, and the self-assertion block, as `dept_kpi_conditions`. The DB test proves the rows are visible and written under the module scope, invisible without it and to another tenant, and that each constraint holds.
- **The response** is `{weekStart, weekEnd, evaluatedUnits, sent: [{unitNodeId, recipients}], alreadySent: [unitNodeId], unitsWithoutHead: [unitNodeId]}`. `sent` is in the org tree's order, `alreadySent` and `unitsWithoutHead` are sorted by id. `recipients` is a count, never user ids. `unitsWithoutHead` is every evaluated department with no head today, claimed or not.

**The drivers read**
- **The gate and the order of checks.** `unitNodeId` and `kpiKey` missing or empty: 400 with that `field`, first (there is no unit to authorize yet); then the period (`resolveRange`, 400 `periodKind`/`start`/`end`, the KPI read's order); then `authorizeUnitHeadRead`: Cerbos `dept_kpi_target` · `read` with the unit's ancestry, then the company-wide tiers (`isCompanyWide`) or a caller whose led scope (`loadLedUnitScope`) holds the unit, else 403 `outside your reporting line`, then 404 `unit_not_found`; then the KPI must be one of the unit's workspace set, else 400 `field: "kpiKey"`. There is NO placed-staff branch: a unit's staff get 403, as they do for the appraisal. A DB test pins that, for nine callers, "drivers is 403" is exactly "the appraisal read is 403". Note that a manager PLACED in the unit and the head of an enclosing unit hold the unit in their led scope, so they pass, as they do for the appraisal.
- **The response** is `{kpi: {key, label, unit, direction}, period: {periodKind, start, end}, drivers, reason?}`. `drivers` is an array of at most 5, worst first (ascending for an up-is-good KPI, descending for a down-is-good one; ties by name in locale order, then by id), or `null` with a `reason`: `no_reader` for a `module` KPI (a `module` KPI that carries a `readerId`, once the catalogue has one, answers `no_drivers`: it has a value and no drivers); `no_drivers` for the GM's derived KPI, for `utilization` (company grain) and for any report-fact KPI that is not one of the four below. An empty array is a real answer (nothing missed in the period). `reason` is absent when `drivers` is an array. The department's value is never read or changed by this route.
- **The sources** (`DRIVER_METRICS` in `dept-kpi-drivers.ts`) are the rollup rows of the period, `computeReportRangeRows(tenantId, start, end)`: the very rows `GET /reports/overview?grain=person&unit=` builds a person's `kpis` from, so a driver's number equals the Team report's (and `GET /reports/document?grain=person`'s) for the same period; the DB test compares each driver to the person document. They are live rows, not a sealed period's stored document; like the Team report's overview they do not refresh today's fact slice.
  - `projects-on-time` (`delivery.milestone_hit_rate`, project-grain rows): the projects with `projects.department_id = <unit>` (the join the department's own milestone row is summed over, so the drivers add up to the department's number), `kind: "project"`, `name` the project's name, `numerator` milestones hit and `denominator` milestones due, `value = numerator / denominator`. A project is listed only when it has at least one milestone due in the period AND missed at least one (hit rate below 100%): the contract's "projects with missed milestones" and the ticket's "at least one milestone due" are both met, and a project that hit everything is not "behind the miss". Not narrowed per person: a project has no person grain.
  - `reopened-work-rate` (`flow.reopen_rate`): the unit's roster, person rows with a denominator above 0 and a numerator above 0 (a reopen rate of 0 is not a miss, a 0 denominator is no data). `value` the rate, with `numerator` (reopened) and `denominator` (completed).
  - `overdue-tasks` (`discipline.overdue_open`): the roster, person rows with a count above 0. `value` is the count and there is no numerator or denominator (the metric has none).
  - `check-in-compliance` (`discipline.checkin_compliance`): the roster, person rows with expected days above 0 and fewer check-ins than expected. `value` the compliance, with `numerator` (submitted) and `denominator` (expected days).
- **The roster** is the §37 rule: `loadUnitRoster` over `collectUnitSubtree(structure, unit)` as of TODAY in `REPORTS_TZ` (never the period's end), then, for a unit-scoped caller (`requiresUnitNarrowing`), filtered to the people whose primary unit is in the caller's led scope: the two steps `getUnitRosterOverview` takes. A person with no row for the metric is not listed; a person on the roster with a row but no miss is not listed; a person outside the roster never is. `kind: "person"`, `id` the user id, `name` the user's display name (`users.name`, the Team report's own name; an unresolvable name reads as the id).
- **A period that is still running** reads today's live rows, as the Team report does; nothing here seals or caches.

**The flow.** `reports-kpi-watch.json` (id `wsrptkpiwatch001`, unchanged) gains a second trigger, `Mondays 07:00` (`0 7 * * 1`), into `POST dept-kpis/digest` (the same headers, `jsonBody` `={{ JSON.stringify({}) }}`, `retryOnFail` 3 tries 5 s apart, error output into the existing `Build dead-letter payload` node, so a failed digest dead-letters through the same hub `notify` as a failed watch), and a `Parse digest result (success)` node that only shapes the execution-log summary. The same account `wf:reports-kpi-watch`; the hub allowlist is unchanged. As with the watch, a CLI re-import deactivates the flow, so it must be activated after the import.

**Tests.** `dept-kpi-digest.test.ts` (pure: the week arithmetic including a Monday morning, a Sunday night, a REPORTS_TZ boundary and every 400, the golden lines for a percent up and down, a count, a duration, "no change", "no data the week before" and the summing-up line, the severity, the href, the driver ordering up-good and down-good with ties and the cap, and the row selection per metric) and `dept-kpi-digest.controller.db.test.ts` (live: a digest once per head per department, a second run `alreadySent`, another week a separate row, two concurrent runs once, a department without a head listed and not claimed, the payload equal to `GET /dept-kpis` for both weeks and free of any name, the ledger under both walls and its constraints, `digest` by a non-admin 403 before the body and a bad `weekStart` 400, and the drivers: the gate for nine callers against the appraisal's, 404, 400 on a KPI outside the set, `no_reader`, projects, reopened work, overdue tasks and check-in compliance equal to the Team report's numbers, the cap of five, the zero-miss person not listed). The DB suite drives the digest through the service with a pinned `now` and the routes through `app.inject`, over a fixed week (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-04) and the week before.

### 43.8b As built (4j-3 UI, 2026-10-15)

Files: `platform-ui/src/lib/deptKpiDrivers.ts` (the honest reader, server-only), `lib/deptKpiDriverFormat.ts` (types, shape guard, wording; client-safe), `components/deptkpis/BehindTheMiss.tsx` (the panel), the `dk-miss` / `dk-drivers` / `dk-driver*` classes in `components/deptkpis/deptKpis.css`, `kpiPeriodFromQuery` in `lib/deptKpiFormat.ts`, the page `app/(app)/appraisals/department/page.tsx`, and `GET dept-kpis/drivers` in `lib/demoDeptKpis.ts`. No backend, Cerbos or contract-shape change: the wire is §43.8a as built.

- **The reader** `getKpiDrivers(userId, tenantId, {unitNodeId, kpiKey, periodKind, start, end?})` returns ok / forbidden / not_found / error. 403 is `forbidden`; only the typed 404 (`unit_not_found` / `field: "unitNodeId"`) is `not_found`; a bare 404, a 400 (a KPI outside the unit's set), a 5xx, a network failure and an answer that fails the shape guard are `error`. The guard (`isKpiDrivers`) takes `drivers` as an array of well-formed rows (an empty array is a true answer) or `null` WITH a `reason` string; `null` with no reason, a row of the wrong kind or type, or a missing `kpi` / `period` is an error. Any reason string passes the guard, so a reason a later engine adds is shown as "No breakdown for this KPI".
- **Who asks, and for what.** The page asks only when `canPropose || canApprove` (a head of the unit, by `canInUnit` over the unit's path, or the company-wide approver tier: the mirror the targets screen and the alert acknowledgement already use). A unit's staff never trigger the read and never see the block; the server 403s them anyway (§43.8a: no placed-staff branch). It asks for the KPIs whose condition is `at_risk` or `off_track` only, with the period the KPI read RESOLVED (`view.period`: periodKind, start, end), so the drivers and the tiles are always for the same period. Because the KPI conditions decide what to ask, the drivers cannot be read before the KPI read; they are read in parallel with the targets read (one `Promise.all`), and the unit's alerts read stays in parallel with the KPI read as before.
- **The panel** is ONE card, "Behind the miss", under the tiles and above the alerts, with one section per KPI that missed (its name, its condition in words and in the `dk-badge` tone, then its list). Each list is named "Behind the miss: <KPI label>". Up to five rows (the server's cap, also applied here), in the order the server sent (worst first), a project or a person each. A KPI whose read was refused renders nothing; when every read was refused there is no card. Rows: name (a link), the value, the parts.
  - Wording (`deptKpiDriverFormat.ts`): the value goes through `formatKpiValue` in the KPI's unit; the parts are per KPI key: `projects-on-time` "3 of 5 milestones hit", `reopened-work-rate` "3 of 10 tasks reopened", `check-in-compliance` "18 of 22 check-ins", `overdue-tasks` has no ratio so the count is the parts, "4 overdue" (and the row does not also show a bare "4"), any other KPI with a ratio "N of M".
  - States: rows; ok empty ("No project missed a milestone" for `projects-on-time`, else "No one stands out"); `drivers: null` ("Not measured yet" for `no_reader`, "No breakdown for this KPI" for `no_drivers` and for any other reason); error and `not_found` ("Couldn't load what is behind this", never an empty claim); forbidden (nothing).
  - Links: a project row to `/projects/<id>`; a person row to `/reports/person?periodKind=&start=&end=&scopeRef=<userId>`, the person's report for the period (the route reads the report under the server's own gate; the head of the unit reads it, §37). These are the app's existing routes; none was invented.
- **The digest's link.** The page already took `periodKind` and `start` from the query and passed them to the KPI read, and the period bar shows the resolved period, so the digest's href (`/appraisals/department?unit=<id>&periodKind=week&start=<Monday>`) opened the right week; what changed is that the parsing is now `kpiPeriodFromQuery` (pure, tested): a missing, empty or repeated param falls back (month, today) and `end` is sent only when given, where a repeated param used to reach the server as `a,b`. The page test pins that the digest's query reaches the KPI read as `{unit, periodKind: "week", start}` with no `end`, and that the bar shows that week.
- **The demo** (`DEMO_MODE`): `GET dept-kpis/drivers` has the server's check order (400 parameters, 400 period, 403 before any word on the unit, 404, 400 for a KPI outside the unit's set) and the head-only gate: `demo-hansel` and `demo-owner` (company-wide) and the unit's own head (`u-webhead` for Web Dev, `dept-manager` for SEO); a unit's placed staff (`u-dev`, `seo-staff`), another unit's head and anyone else are 403. The demo never shows what the real server cannot answer, so drivers exist only for the report-fact KPIs that have them. Payloads: Web Dev's at-risk "Projects on time" lists "Client site redesign" (3 of 5) then "Mobile app revamp" (4 of 6), which add up to the department's four misses (21 due, 17 hit), and link to the demo's own projects; Web Dev's on-track "Reopened work rate" has one person (`u-dev`). Every other KPI answers as the server does: Creatives' off-track "Asset requests delivered on time" is a module KPI, so it answers `drivers: null, reason: "no_drivers"` (the panel shows "No breakdown for this KPI"; the real server says `no_reader` until DW-6's reader seam lands, then `no_drivers`), a KPI with no reading at all answers `no_reader` (Web Dev's "Client site uptime"), and one with a reader and no breakdown `no_drivers` (utilization, the derived KPI, SEO's reports). No demo condition, value, lead or target was changed.

**Tests.** `deptKpiDrivers.test.ts` (the four outcomes, the path and query, the shape guard), `deptKpiDriverFormat.test.ts` (golden strings, links, the guard, the period parse), `components/deptkpis/BehindTheMiss.test.tsx` (every state), `app/(app)/appraisals/department/page.test.tsx` (the page asks only for missed KPIs, only for a head or the approver, for the resolved period, in parallel with the targets; staff never; the digest's query), and the added `GET dept-kpis/drivers` cases in `demoDeptKpis.test.ts` (the gate across the demo's roles, the order of checks, the payloads).

### 43.9 Not in DW-4j
- Iterating tenants. The reports flows are single-tenant today; a tenant list for n8n is a reports-wide ticket.
- "Trending to miss" (§40.3: it needs a projection rule).
- Mail.
- Telling the GM. The company Overview's departments block is the GM's view.

**Proof (live Postgres + Cerbos on the CI gate):**
- `classifyChange`: every pair of the four conditions, plus "no previous";
- a first run stores and tells nothing, and opens alerts for KPIs already off track;
- an approved target that puts a KPI off track: one notification to the head and one alert; the same run again tells nothing;
- the KPI back within tolerance: "back" is told and the alert is resolved;
- a new month with no data is silent;
- two concurrent runs tell once;
- the recipients are exact-node `org_unit_lead` holders only (not an enclosing head, not a placed manager), and a unit with no head is reported;
- no notification payload carries a person's name;
- the alerts read: a head gets their own units only;
- acknowledging: a head 200, another unit's head 403, twice 409, a resolved alert 409;
- `watch` by a non-admin is 403.

## 45. Attachments on requests, campaign parts, campaigns and the staff client page (DW-8h, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/core/files.controller.ts`; UI `platform-ui/src/components/Attachments.tsx` — **STATUS: BACKEND AND UI BUILT, PROTOTYPED (HTTP suite `files-targets.test.ts` written for the Linux CI gate; UI tested in vitest and built in demo mode, not yet driven live)**

**Why.** Plan §8.1 (row 8h) and §14.2. Today only the task and project pages show files. A request between departments, a campaign, a department's part of a campaign and a client cannot carry a brief, a spec or a delivered file, so that work leaves the ERP.

The `files` table and `files.controller.ts` already store attachments for any kind in an allowlist (`TARGET_KINDS`), and the UI already has a download route (`GET /api/files/:fileId`, the files row of the endpoint table above). This section adds two kinds, a real upload from the UI, an honest list read and the panel on four pages. There is no migration and no Cerbos policy change.

### 45.1 Two new target kinds, with their own write rule
- `TARGET_KINDS` gains `work_request` (DW-5c, §32) and `agency_campaign_part` (DW-5a, §31). `client` and `agency_campaign` are already in it.
- **Reading follows the target's read; writing follows the target's own write.** Reads of both new kinds are open to every member of the company (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §35, §36). If "may read" also meant "may attach", anyone could add files to any request or part. So for the two new kinds:
  - **list** and **download:** `file` · `read`, then the target's read, in the shape its own read route sends: `{kind: "work_request", tenantId, id}`, and for a part `partResource(tenantId, {id})`.
  - **attach** and **delete:** `file` · `create` (or `delete`), then the target's WRITE check, with attributes read from the database, never from the body:
    - `work_request`: allowed when `deliver` (the receiving side) OR `cancel` (the asker) is allowed on `factsResource(tenantId, facts)` (`requestedBy`, `assigneeIds`, `unitAncestors`). This covers the asker, the assignees, the receiving department's head, and managers.
    - `agency_campaign_part`: `update` on `partResource(tenantId, {id, ownerId, unitAncestors})`. This covers the part's owner, the department's head and managers. Without those attributes, the owner and head rules fail closed.
  - DW-6k already resolves exactly these targets and their write check (`core/figma/figma.controller.ts`: `readResourceOf`, `readTarget`, `requireTarget`, `authorizeWrite`; §36.5). 8h moves them, unchanged, into a shared `core/work-targets.ts` that both controllers import. There is one copy of the rule, and DW-6k's Cerbos matrix keeps covering it.
- **The existing kinds are unchanged** (`file` · action, then the target's `read`). Changing their write rule is out of scope here; it is recorded as a gap.
- **The target must exist** (the two new kinds). `requireTarget` reads the row under the tenant. A request or part that is absent, soft-deleted or another tenant's, or an id that cannot be one, answers 404 `{error: "target_not_found"}` after the `file` check. Because a caller outside the tenant is refused first, the 404 is never an existence oracle.
- **A closed target takes no new files.** Attaching to a `cancelled` or `declined` request, or a `cancelled` part, answers 409 `{error: "target_closed"}`. A `delivered` request still takes files ("deliver more"). Listing, downloading and deleting stay open on a closed target.
- **PV rules stay** for every kind (PV5-06, PV5-07): a file with a `role` (an issued invoice PDF, a sealed or certified copy, a receipt, a certificate) is never deleted or replaced (409), and `files.sha256` is written on every upload that holds bytes.
- **Staff only.** Neither new kind, nor `client`, is ever a portal parent:
  - the portal download route (`portal/files/:fileId`) keeps its parent list;
  - `core/client-documents.ts` (the portal and staff Documents list) and the `documents.list` agent tool list legal and money documents by role and parent only.

  A guard test pins that a `client`, `work_request` or `agency_campaign_part` file is absent from the portal Documents list and refused by the portal download route.

### 45.2 Upload from the UI
- The platform already takes `{content}` as base64 up to 25 MB, scrubs text types and stores the bytes. The UI gains a real upload: the panel's file input sends the file through a server action, which base64-encodes it and posts `{targetType, targetId, filename, contentType, content}`.
- **The route needs its body limit.** `POST /api/:tenantId/files` is not in `core/upload-body-limits.ts`'s table, so Fastify's 1 MiB default refuses (413) any upload over about 750 KB, although the handler allows 25 MB. 8h adds the entry `{method: "POST", url: "/api/:tenantId/files", capBytes: MAX_BYTES, label: "staff file upload"}`, which exports `MAX_BYTES`. `assertAllMatched()` then fails the boot if the route is ever renamed.
- The action refuses a file over 25 MB before sending, with a sentence. The Server Action and proxy body caps (520 MB, `next.config.ts`) are not the limit; the platform's 25 MB is.
- When the answer says `scrubbed: true`, the panel says that personal data was removed from the stored copy.
- Linking stays: name plus an optional URL, stored as a reference row with no bytes. Once DW-6i lands, list rows carry `url`, and a reference row opens it. A row with bytes downloads through `GET /api/files/:fileId`.
- The attach and remove actions take the page path to revalidate from the caller. Today they derive `/${entityType}s/${id}`, which is wrong for these kinds.

### 45.3 An honest list read
`listFiles` folds every failure into `[]` (`skipUnavailable`), so a refusal reads as "no files". The panel uses a new reader `readFiles(userId, tenantId, entityType, entityId)` that returns a `ReadResult`:
- 403 → "You can't see this item's files.";
- 404 `target_not_found` → "This item no longer exists.";
- unreachable → "Files can't be read right now.", never an empty list.

The existing callers of `listFiles` (the task and project pages) are not changed by this ticket.

### 45.4 Where the panel appears
- **A request** (`/requests/[id]`): the request's files (`work_request`, the request id). Everyone who can read the request sees them; the asker, the assignees, the receiving head and managers add them (§45.1). The add controls follow the page's existing write hints. Where there are none, the panel offers adding and words a 403 as "Only the people on this request can add files."
- **A campaign** (`/agency/[campaignId]`): the campaign's own files (`agency_campaign`). Each department part on that page shows a quiet file count, which opens that part's files (`agency_campaign_part`) in place. There is no panel per part by default, so the page stays clean (plan §13 trap 5).
- **The staff client page**, on its Internal "notes and files" tab (`/clients/[clientId]/notes`, PV's call under PV-D4; the Details tab first agreed is only a redirect to People since CC-D8): a Files card for the client (`client`). **Staff only** (§45.1); the panel says "Only staff see these files."
- The panel shows each file's name, size, who added it and when (pinned locale and time zone), and Download or Open. Remove is offered when `canEdit` is true.

### 45.5 Demo mode and tests
- **DEMO_MODE:** `demoFixtures` answers list, attach and remove for the new targets, with a labelled placeholder file.
- **Platform**, on the Linux CI gate (an HTTP suite against real Postgres and Cerbos):
  - **A request:** the asker, an assignee and the receiving head may attach and delete. A plain member of a third department may list but not attach (403).
  - **A part:** the owner and the department head may attach. A member of another department may not (403).
  - another tenant's caller is refused 403 on list and attach;
  - a missing or soft-deleted target answers 404 `target_not_found`;
  - a cancelled or declined request, or a cancelled part, answers 409 `target_closed` on attach, while a delivered request takes files;
  - an unsupported kind still answers 400;
  - an upload over 25 MB answers 400, and one of about 5 MB is stored (the body limit applies; extend `upload-body-limits.http.test.ts`);
  - a file with a `role` still answers 409 on delete;
  - the staff-only guard: a `client`, `work_request` or `agency_campaign_part` file is absent from the portal Documents list and refused by the portal download route.
- DW-6k's Figma suite stays green after the move to `core/work-targets.ts`.
- **UI:** the panel's sentences for refused, missing, closed and unreachable; the size refusal before sending; the scrubbed notice; the revalidated path; the staff-only line on the client page; DW-6i's Drive button kept beside the upload.

### 45.6 As built (backend)
Built exactly as §45.1 to §45.5 specify, with these points the text left open:
- **Shared module.** `platform-nest/src/core/work-targets.ts` holds `WorkTargetKind` (`pm_task | work_request | campaign_part`, the strings Figma's `TargetKind` uses), `CERBOS_KIND`, `readResourceOf`, `Target`, `readTarget`, `authorizeWrite`, and `findTarget` (the uuid-shape test plus `readTarget` under `withTenants`). `figma.controller.ts` imports them; its behaviour and its tokens (`target_not_found` as a `FigmaRuleError`) are unchanged. The not-found outcome is neutral: `findTarget` returns `null`, and each controller throws its own refusal (Figma: `svc.targetNotFound()`; files: `NotFoundException("target_not_found")`).
- **`closed`.** `Target.closed` is true for a `work_request` whose `status` is `cancelled` or `declined`, and for an `agency_campaign_parts` row whose `status` is `cancelled`. `delivered` requests, every other part status and PM tasks are never closed. The request status is one extra read in `readTarget`; `loadAuthFacts` is untouched. Figma ignores the flag.
- **Order in the new-kind handlers.** `file` check, then the target KIND's read (no id), then the target read from the database (404), then the target's write check (403), then `closed` (409), then body validation. A caller who may not write a closed target gets 403, not 409. The missing-field and unsupported-kind 400s still come first, as they name the kind. Reads (list, metadata, content) authorise the target's read with the id, then (list only) require the target.
- **Ids.** For the new kinds a uuid is trimmed and lowercased before it is read or stored; a non-uuid answers 404 `target_not_found` (list, attach, upload) after the tenant-level gates.
- **Delete on a target that is gone.** Because the write check needs the target's attributes, deleting a file whose request or part is soft-deleted answers 404 `target_not_found` and leaves the row. Metadata and download of such a file are not gated on the target's existence (read check only), as for the old kinds.
- **Roles.** The `files_role_target` CHECK allows a `role` only on `invoice` and `contract` targets, so a role file can never sit on a request or part; the 409-on-delete test uses an `invoice_pdf` row, and the suite also pins that the database refuses a role on the new kinds.
- **Body limit.** `MAX_BYTES` is exported from `files.controller.ts`; `upload-body-limits.ts` lists `POST /api/:tenantId/files` ("staff file upload"), so the table has six entries and `assertAllMatched()` covers the route. `upload-body-limits.test.ts` pins the entry and the controller's decorator path; `upload-body-limits.http.test.ts` adds the ~5 MB (201), just-over-25 MB (400 `file too large`, not 413) and 26 MB (413: past the derived limit, the ceiling) cases. (CI corrected the first draft, which expected 400 for 26 MB.)
- **Old kinds.** Unchanged: `file` then the target's `read` with `{kind, id, tenantId}`, also for attach and delete. This read-for-write is the recorded gap (§45.1), noted in a comment in the controller.
- **Tests.** `files-targets.test.ts` (23 cases) covers §45.5 including the staff-only guard (a control invoice PDF is listed and downloads, a `client`, `work_request` and `agency_campaign_part` file is not and 404s on `GET portal/files/:fileId`). It and `upload-body-limits.http.test.ts` run on the Linux gate only. The capability inventory (`docs/modules/CAPABILITY-INVENTORY.md`) was regenerated because the new HTTP suite changes its driver counts. No Figma test was touched.

### 45.7 As built (UI)
- **Reader and upload.** `readFiles` (`lib/entities.ts`) returns a `ReadResult`; a 404 is `unavailable` with the reason `target_not_found`. `listFiles` and its callers are unchanged. `uploadFileAction(entityType, entityId, revalidate, formData)` (`lib/collabActions.ts`) takes the `file`, refuses over 25 MB before sending ("Files can be at most 25 MB."; the component checks the same limit first), base64-encodes it, posts `{targetType, targetId, filename, contentType, content}` and revalidates the given path. `attachFileAction` and `deleteFileAction` take an optional trailing `revalidate`; without it they keep the old `/${entityType}s/${id}` guess (the task page). The sentences live in `lib/fileUpload.ts`.
- **Panel.** `components/FilesPanel.tsx` wraps `Attachments`: it words a refused, missing or unreachable read as itself and never draws an empty list for them. `Attachments` gained an optional `upload` prop (file input and "Upload"); the link attach and DW-6i's Drive button are unchanged. A file without a `url` links to `/api/files/:id` with its size and date. The list read does not carry the uploader's name (only `uploader_id`), so "who added it" is not shown.
- **Pages.** `/requests/[id]`: Files card, one read. `/agency/[campaignId]`: a Files card for the campaign, and a quiet "Files (n)" button on each part that opens that part's files in place. The page makes 1 + N reads (the campaign's, and one per part; a campaign holds one part per department). `/clients/[clientId]/notes`: Files card with "Only staff see these files.", between Notes and History.
- **Placement.** `/clients/[clientId]/details` is only a redirect to `contacts` since CC-D8, so PV placed the card on the Internal Notes tab ("notes and files"): staff-only material lives there (PV-D4), and a staff-only card on People could be mistaken for something the portal's People list shows.
- **Demo mode.** `demoFixtures` seeds a labelled placeholder file on each of the four kinds (`wr-demo-1`, `cmp-demo-1`, `part-demo-1`, `cl-1`) and its POST takes the new body and answers `{id, scrubbed, byteSize}`. The demo has no request or campaign pages to show them on.

## 46. Knowledge search for staff (DW-8i, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/modules/knowledge/search.controller.ts` (new), `modules/knowledge/search-filter.ts` (new); UI `/knowledge` — **STATUS: BACKEND AND UI BUILT, PROTOTYPED (backend unit suite `search-filter.test.ts` run locally; the HTTP suite `search.controller.test.ts` is written for the Linux CI gate against real Postgres + Cerbos and has NOT been run yet; UI: vitest, `tsc` and the demo-mode `next build` gate run locally, not yet driven in a browser or against a live platform)**

**Why.** Plan §8.1 (row 8i) and §14.2 ("Find a company document"). The knowledge store (WS8, `ai-agents/src/knowledge/`) indexes ERP records every 6 hours, but staff cannot search it. `/knowledge` lists sources only, and `/search` is a client-side substring match over a few lists.

**The rule that shapes this section.** The internal tier's chunks are written with an empty `acl`, which means "every member of the company" (`modules/knowledge/README.md`, "Known limits"). The ERP's own reads are narrower: a person's report, a meeting transcript and a file each have their own read rule. A search that returned chunks on the tier's rule alone would show a member records they cannot open in the ERP. That would widen visibility, which D-UX-2 forbids. So **every hit is re-checked against the caller's read right on its source record before it is returned, and a family with no such check is never returned.**

### 46.1 The route
