- **Request:** `GET /api/:tenantId/knowledge/search?q=&limit=`, behind `AuthGuard` and `ModuleEnabledGuard("knowledge")`. The gate is Cerbos `activity` · `read` on the tenant, the gate `GET :tenantId/knowledge/sources` already uses. There is no new Cerbos kind or action.
- **Validation:** `q` is 2 to 200 characters after trimming, else 400 `{error: "query_invalid"}`. `limit` is 1 to 20 (default 10).
- **The store call:** the platform calls the knowledge service's `POST /search` the way `modules/search/knowledge-client.ts` does (`selfLinkUpsert`, then `x-obo-provider: platform` and `x-obo-external-id: <userId>`, with the service token). It asks for `topK = min(limit × 4, 80)`, leaving room for the filter.
  - A new caller in that file returns a result or throws. The existing helper, which folds every failure into `[]`, is left as it is for its own callers.
- **Tier and tenant:** only `audience: "internal"` hits whose `tenantId` equals `:tenantId` are kept. A public-tier hit (the website corpus) is not a company record and is dropped here.
- **Service down:** an unset knowledge URL, a timeout or a non-2xx answer gives 503 `{error: "knowledge_unavailable"}`, never an empty list.

### 46.2 The filter: one read check per hit
`sourceRef` names the record (`erp:<family>:<id…>`, `modules/knowledge/ingest/erp-source.ts`).

**Searchable (v1)**, each with the read check its own ERP read route makes, using the same resource shape and attributes:

| Family | Record | Read check (verify each against its route) | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | client | the client read of `/clients/:id` | `/clients/:id` |
| `project` | project | the project read | `/projects/:id` |
| `task` | base task | the task read | `/tasks/:id` |
| `pmtask` | PM task | the `pm_task` read | the PM task's own page (the href `GET /api/tasks/mine` builds) |
| `deliverable` | deliverable | the deliverable read | `/deliverables/:id` |
| `meeting` | meeting recording | the recording read of `meetings.controller.ts` | `/meetings/:id` |
| `pmdoc` | PM doc | the PM doc read | the doc's page |
| `file` | file | `file` · `read`, then its parent's read (as `GET :tenantId/files/:fileId` does) | the parent's page; the file downloads through `GET /api/files/:fileId` |

**Withheld (v1):** `report`, `person`, `org` and `orgunits`, and any family not in the table above (fail closed).
- Their read rules depend on who the person is: a report is read by self, head or HR; the people directory has its own gate.
- Each can join the table later, with its own check and its own test.

**How it is checked:**
- Every check runs **after** the record is confirmed to exist under the tenant (`withTenants`). A deleted record's stale chunk is dropped, so search never surfaces a record the ERP no longer shows.
- The checks are batched through Cerbos at most 50 per request (the batch limit).
- **A refused hit is dropped silently.** No count of withheld hits is returned, because a count would confirm that hidden records match the query.

### 46.3 The answer
```
200 { query, results: [{ sourceRef, family, title, snippet, href, score }], indexedAt }
```
- **One result per record.** Several chunks of one record collapse to the best-scoring one. Results are in score order, at most `limit`.
- **`title`:** the record's current name, read from the ERP row during the existence check, never from the chunk.
- **`snippet`:** up to 300 characters of the chunk, with whitespace collapsed.
- **`indexedAt`:** the last successful sweep's finish time (`GET :tenantId/knowledge/ingest/status`), or `null`.
- **Not stored:** the query text is never written to activity or audit logs. It can carry personal data, and it is not an action on a record.

### 46.4 UI
- `/knowledge` gains a search field at the top, kept in the URL (`?q=`), with results under it: title as a link, a family label, and the snippet. The source list stays below for the people who use it.
- **Honest states:**
  - 503 → "Search isn't available right now.";
  - no results → "Nothing you can open matches." plus "Results include only records you can open.";
  - always the line "Indexed every 6 hours (last: …). PDF and Word files are found by name, not by their contents."
- ⌘K gains a "Search company knowledge for '…'" item that opens `/knowledge?q=…`.
- **DEMO_MODE:** a fixture answers with a few labelled results.

### 46.5 Tests
- **Unit:** the family parser and the allowlist (an unknown family is dropped); collapsing to one result per record; the topK arithmetic.
- **HTTP suite** on the Linux CI gate, against real Postgres and Cerbos, with the knowledge service stubbed:
  - a member's hits on a record they can read are returned;
  - hits on a record they cannot read are dropped;
  - another tenant's and public-tier hits are dropped;
  - a deleted record is dropped;
  - a `report` or `person` hit is dropped for every caller, including `company_admin`;
  - the service down gives 503;
  - `q` too short gives 400;
  - the query text appears in no activity row.

### 46.6 A finding outside this ticket
The hub's `knowledge.search` tool and the assistant's retrieval (`config.knowledgeTopK`, ASST-18) apply only the tier's rule today. So the AI Assistant can quote internal chunks, such as a person's report or a meeting transcript, to any member of the company. §46.2's filter is written as a shared function (`search-filter.ts`) so those paths can adopt it. Whether and when they do is the owner's decision (see the DW-8 board), not part of DW-8i.

### 46.7 As built (backend, DW-8i)

**Files.** `modules/knowledge/search.controller.ts` (the route), `modules/knowledge/search-filter.ts` (ref parser, collapse, topK, snippet, the per-family table, the filter), `modules/search/knowledge-client.ts` (`searchKnowledgeStrict`, which returns the store's hits whole or throws `KnowledgeUnavailableError`; the old fail-soft helper is untouched), `rbac/cerbos.ts` (`checkMany`: one action on many resources, at most 50 a request, fail closed), `core/files.controller.ts` (`TARGET_KINDS` and `targetReadResource` are now exported, no behaviour change). Registered in `app.module.ts` next to `IntelligenceController`. No migration, no Cerbos policy, no new permission.

**The read resource per family** (each copied from the record's own read route; `search-filter.ts` `FAMILY_SPECS` carries the same comment):

| Family | Existence and title (tenant, not deleted) | Cerbos `read` resource | Copied from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | `clients.name` | `{kind: "client", id, tenantId}` | `getClient` in `clients.controller.ts`; the route sits behind `ModuleEnabledGuard("clients")`, so the hit is dropped when that module is off |
| `project` | `projects.name` | `{kind: "project", tenantId, id}` | `projectDetail` in `core.controller.ts` |
| `task` | `tasks.title` (joined to `projects`) | `{kind: "task", tenantId, id}` | `taskDetail` in `core.controller.ts` |
| `pmtask` | `pm_tasks.title` (joined to `projects`, as `TASK_SELECT` does) | `{kind: "pm_task", tenantId, id}` | `getTask` in `pm.controller.ts`; behind `ModuleEnabledGuard("pm")` |
| `deliverable` | `deliverables.name` | `{kind: "deliverable", id, tenantId}` | `getDeliverable` in `client-work.controller.ts` |
| `meeting` | `meeting_recordings.title`, else "Meeting <date>" | `{kind: "meeting_recording", tenantId}` (the route sends no id) | `get` in `meetings.controller.ts` |
| `pmdoc` | `pm_docs.title` | `{kind: "pm_project", tenantId, id: <the doc's project>}` | `getDoc` in `pm.controller.ts`; behind `ModuleEnabledGuard("pm")` |
| `file` | `files.filename` | BOTH `{kind: "file", id, tenantId}` and the parent's read from `targetReadResource` | `metadata` in `files.controller.ts` |

**Deviations, with reasons.**
- **Module guards.** The `clients` and `pm` routes are behind their module guard, so a hit on one of them is dropped when the module is off for the company (§46.2 did not say this; the route would 404).
- **File parents.** A file is returned only when its parent kind is one the upload route can attach to (`TARGET_KINDS`). Files attached to other kinds (reports, assistant messages, and so on) are withheld, not guessed at. The ERP's own file route would ask Cerbos about those; fail closed here costs findability, never visibility.
- **Hrefs.** A deliverable has no page of its own in the UI (only the list), so it opens on its project (`/projects/:projectId`, or `/deliverables` when it has none). A PM doc opens on its project's Docs tab (`/projects/:projectId?view=docs`). A PM task opens at `/tasks/:id`, as `GET /api/tasks/mine` builds it. A file opens on its parent's page for a client, project, task or campaign, else it downloads (`/api/files/:fileId`).
- **`indexedAt`** is the finish time of the last sweep of this company's internal tier in this process when that sweep had no errors, else `null` (the sweep result is held in memory, so it is `null` after a restart until the next sweep).
- **`limit`** outside 1 to 20 is clamped and a non-number falls back to 10 (§46.1 gives only the range).
- **Acting for someone.** When the principal acts for a human (`actFor`), every read must also be allowed for that human, as `authorize()` does. This only narrows.

**Who the filter actually narrows.** Every v1 family except `file` is readable by every `company_admin`, `manager`, `member` and `viewer` of the company (and by the matching `core.*.read` permission arm), so for those the filter matters for outsiders, for principals without the role, for the module switch, and for deleted rows. The genuinely narrower case is a `file` whose parent has a narrower read, such as a contract (`contract` read is `company_admin` and `manager`; the member and viewer bundles hold no `core.contract.read`). The HTTP suite drives that case.

### 46.8 As built (UI, DW-8i)

- **Reader.** `searchKnowledge(userId, tenantId, q, limit?)` in `platform-ui/src/lib/admin.ts` returns a `ReadResult`: 200 is `ok`, 403 `forbidden`, 503 or an unreachable platform `unavailable`. A 400 is `unavailable` with reason `query_invalid`, which the page words as "Type at least 2 characters." A failure is never folded into "no results".
- **Page.** `/knowledge` has a GET form (`?q=`) at the top. The page checks the 2-character floor before calling. States and wording are exactly §46.4's, plus "You can't search company knowledge." for 403. Family labels: Client, Project, Task (also for `pmtask`), Deliverable, Meeting, Document (`pmdoc`), File. The line "Indexed every 6 hours" shows always, with "(last: ...)" in the pinned display zone when `indexedAt` is set. The source list and quarantine card are unchanged.
- **Palette.** With 2 or more typed characters the palette adds a "Knowledge" group holding "Search company knowledge for '<text>'", opening `/knowledge?q=<encoded text>`. It is reachable by arrows and click but is never the default highlight, so Enter with nothing else matching still goes to `/search` (DW-2c).
- **DEMO_MODE.** `demoFixtures.ts` answers the route with three labelled sample results for any query of 2 or more characters, an empty list for a query containing "nothing", and 400 `query_invalid` otherwise.

## 47. Calendar events and meeting scheduling (DW-8g, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/core/calendar-events.{controller,service}.ts` (new), migrations `202610151100_calendar_events.sql` and `202610151110_iam_calendar_event_permissions.sql`; UI `/calendar` — **STATUS: BACKEND AND UI BUILT, PROTOTYPED (UI: `/calendar`, `/calendar/new`, `/calendar/events/[id]` and its `/edit`, the Overview Today block and the DEMO_MODE store, tested with vitest and `next build`, not yet driven against a live backend; the backend rules `calendar-events.service.test.ts`, the scheduler pin `meeting-schedule.test.ts` and the Cerbos static pin run anywhere; the HTTP suite `calendar-events.test.ts`, the migration suite `calendar-events-migration.db.test.ts` and the live Cerbos matrix `src/rbac/cerbos-calendar-event.test.ts` are written for the Linux CI gate and have not run yet); busy times (§47.4) NOT built, waiting for an owner ruling, so the UI draws none)**

**Why.** Plan §8.1 (row 8g) and §14.2 ("Meetings: schedule a meeting, see events, not only tasks").
- The calendar shows tasks only.
- The one way to put a meeting in the future is `POST /:t/meetings/recordings/schedule`. It creates a recording row in state `scheduled`, with no attendees, no end time and no invitation.

This section adds events with attendees. A meeting is an event that can carry that scheduled recording. The Cerbos kind is PERMISSION-CONTRACT §39.

**Out of scope (v1):**
- recurrence;
- client contacts as attendees;
- email invitations (system mail stays approvals and risk only; personal Gmail is DW-8j);
- Google Calendar sync (waits for DW-11's OAuth client);
- agent writes (the `calendar_event` DENY for automation and bot principals follows the `work_request` precedent; agents get it under the separate AI plan).

### 47.1 Data

**`calendar_events`:**

| Column | Type and rule |
|---|---|
| `id`, `tenant_id` | |
| `title` | 1 to 200 characters |
| `description` | at most 5,000 characters, scrubbed like other free text |
| `starts_at`, `ends_at` | `timestamptz`, for a timed event |
| `starts_on`, `ends_on` | `date`, for an all-day event (inclusive) |
| `location` | at most 300 characters |
| `video_url` | `https:` only, at most 2,048 characters |
| `organizer_id` | `users` |
| `visibility` | `attendees` (default) or `company` |
| `status` | `confirmed` or `cancelled` |
| `cancelled_at` | |
| `client_id`, `project_id` | nullable FKs in the same tenant |
| `meeting_recording_id` | nullable, unique, FK `meeting_recordings` |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | |
| `origin_site` | no default |

**CHECKs:**
- exactly one of the two time shapes is set;
- `ends_at > starts_at`, and at most 14 days apart;
- `ends_on >= starts_on`;
- `cancelled_at` is set exactly when `status = 'cancelled'`. Use `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`, because a CHECK passes on NULL.

**`calendar_event_attendees`:**
- `(event_id, user_id)` is the primary key. Columns: `tenant_id`, `response` (`needs_action`, `accepted`, `declined` or `tentative`) and `responded_at`.
- The organizer is always an attendee, with the answer `accepted`.

**RLS, indexes and time zone:**
- FORCE RLS on both tables, with the standard tenant predicate.
- Indexes: `(tenant_id, starts_at)`, `(tenant_id, starts_on)`, and `(user_id)` on the attendees.
- Times are stored in UTC. The UI shows them in the display zone (`NEXT_PUBLIC_DISPLAY_TZ`).

### 47.2 Who sees and does what (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §39)

**Who may read an event:**
- the organizer;
- every attendee;
- every member, viewer and manager of the company, when `visibility = 'company'`;
- `company_admin`.

Nobody else reads it. A manager reads only as the organizer, an attendee or through a company-visible event (added at review, 2026-10-14).

**What a read never reveals:**
- Calendar reads never leak the title of an event the caller cannot read.
- Busy times (§47.4) carry no title at all.

**A linked recording keeps its own rule.** Meeting recordings are readable by every member today (`resource_meeting_recording.yaml`). An event's privacy does not narrow its recording, and the form says so when "Record this meeting" is ticked.

**Who may change an event:**
- `create`: `company_admin`, `manager` and `member`. A viewer cannot.
- `update` and `cancel`: the organizer and `company_admin`.
- `respond`: an attendee, for themselves only.

### 47.3 Endpoints

**`GET /api/calendar/events/mine?from=&to=&scope=`**

The caller's events (organizer or attendee) across their companies, in the `tasks/mine` envelope (`{items, companies}`). A failing company leg is `included: false`, never a 500.
- **Parameters:** the window `[from, to)` is required and at most 92 days, else 400. `scope` is `all` or a company id.
- **A row:** `{id, tenantId, company, title, startsAt, endsAt, allDay, startsOn, endsOn, location, videoUrl, status, myResponse, organizer: {id, name}, attendeeCount, recording: {id, status} | null, client: {id, name} | null, project: {id, name} | null, href: "/calendar/events/<id>?company=<tenantId>"}`.
- **Included states:** cancelled events are included, so the calendar can strike them through. An event the caller declined is included with `myResponse: "declined"`.

**`GET /api/:t/calendar/events/:id`**

The detail, with `attendees: [{userId, name, response}]` and `canEdit` / `canRespond` (from Cerbos). An event the caller cannot read answers 404, not 403, so an id is never an existence oracle.

**`POST /api/:t/calendar/events`**
- **Body:** `{title, startsAt, endsAt}` or `{allDay: true, startsOn, endsOn}`, plus `location?, videoUrl?, description?, attendeeIds: string[], visibility?, clientId?, projectId?, record?: boolean}`.
- **Attendees:** at most 50, each an active member of the company, else 422 `{error: "attendee_not_member", userId}`. The organizer is added if absent.
- **`record: true`:** also authorizes `meeting_recording` · `create`. It creates the `scheduled` recording row through the same code path as `POST …/recordings/schedule`, in the same transaction, linked by `meeting_recording_id`. The recording's `scheduledAt` is `startsAt`, so this is for timed events only: an all-day event with `record` is 400.
- **Answer:** 201 with the detail.
- **Invitations:** every attendee except the organizer gets an Inbox notification (`type "calendar.invited"`, the title, the time in words, an `href` to the event).

**`PATCH /api/:t/calendar/events/:id`**

The organizer edits any field above, except `record`.
- **Attendees:** added people are invited, and removed people are told it is off for them.
- **A time change:** tells everyone and resets the answers to `needs_action`.
- **A linked recording** that is still `scheduled` has its `scheduled_at` moved with the start.
- **A cancelled event** answers 409 `event_cancelled`.

**`POST /api/:t/calendar/events/:id/cancel`**

Sets `cancelled` and tells every attendee.
- **Idempotent:** a second call answers 200 with the same state.
- **A linked recording** is left as it is; Meetings shows that the event was cancelled.

**`POST /api/:t/calendar/events/:id/respond`**

Body `{response: "accepted" | "declined" | "tentative"}`. Attendees only, for themselves. On a cancelled event it answers 409.

**Activity rows** (`writeActivity`) are written for create, update, cancel and respond. They carry ids, never the description.

### 47.4 Busy times, for scheduling

**`GET /api/:t/calendar/busy?userIds=a,b&from=&to=`**

- **Answer:** `{busy: [{userId, intervals: [{startsAt, endsAt}]}]}`. The intervals come from confirmed timed events the person attends with an answer other than `declined`. All-day events are left out.
- **What it never carries:** a title, a location or an organizer. A person is not told who looked.
- **Limits:** at most 20 users and a window of at most 14 days. Each user must be an active member of the company, else 422.
- **Gate:** `calendar_event` · `create` on the tenant, the same people who can schedule.
- **To confirm with the owner when 8g starts.** Busy times show only when someone is busy, never what they are doing. This is the scheduling aid every calendar offers, but it is new people data, so it is asked, not assumed (compare DW-D19).

### 47.5 UI

**`/calendar`:**
- Events join the Day, Week and Month grids next to tasks, from the cross-company read.
- Cancelled events are struck through; declined ones are dimmed.
- "Schedule a meeting" opens `/calendar/new`.

**`/calendar/new`:**
- title;
- date and time in the display zone, or all day;
- attendees (picked from `GET /api/:t/members`);
- location or video link;
- an optional client and project;
- "Record this meeting", shown where the Meetings row is (`agencyRow: meetings`);
- visibility: "Only the people invited" or "Everyone in the company".

The chosen attendees' busy times for that day show as plain blocks.

**`/calendar/events/[id]`:**
- the detail and the answer buttons;
- edit and cancel, for the organizer.

It sits in the personal area, Calendar row.

**The Overview's Today block** (`components/overview/widgets/TodayBlock.tsx`) lists today's events, and its note "No calendar events exist yet (DW-8g)" goes.

**DEMO_MODE:** a stateful demo store for events, as `demoMeetings` does for recordings.

### 47.6 Tests

**Migration:**
- the CHECKs: each time shape, the 14-day span, cancelled, and both shapes refused;
- RLS returns zero rows with the GUC unset.

**HTTP suite** on the Linux CI gate (real Postgres and Cerbos):
- create: timed, all-day, and with `record` (both rows written);
- attendee validation: 422;
- read: 200 for the organizer, an attendee and a member of a company-visible event; 404 for an uninvited member and for a manager;
- update: 200 for the organizer, 403 for an attendee;
- a time change resets the answers and moves a scheduled recording;
- cancel is idempotent;
- respond: 200 for an attendee, 403/404 for a non-attendee, 409 on a cancelled event;
- busy times carry no title, and 21 users or a 15-day window is refused;
- `mine` returns only the caller's events, and its envelope reports a failing leg;
- an automation principal is refused `create`.

**Cerbos matrix:** `src/rbac/cerbos-calendar-event.test.ts`.

**UI:**
- the grid merge: tasks and events, and the time zone at the day's edges;
- the form's validation sentences;
- the busy blocks;
- the Today block.

### 47.7 As built (backend, DW-8g, 2026-10-14)

Built as §47.1 to §47.3 and §47.6 specify, except busy times: **§47.4 (`GET /:t/calendar/busy`) is not built.** It waits for the owner's ruling on showing when people are busy; no route, no test, nothing in the policy for it beyond the `create` gate it would reuse. Everything below is a point the text left open or a deviation, with its reason.

- **Migrations.** `202610151100_calendar_events.sql` (both tables, FORCE RLS, the CHECKs, the indexes) and `202610151110_iam_calendar_event_permissions.sql` (the permissions seed, 23 role rows, with the DO-block self-assertion). Beyond §47.1: composite FKs `(meeting_recording_id, tenant_id)` and `(project_id, tenant_id)` so a link cannot cross companies (`client_id` is a plain FK: `clients` has no `(id, tenant_id)` unique, so the service checks the client against the tenant); `UNIQUE (id, tenant_id)` for the attendee FK; an index on `(tenant_id, organizer_id)`; `created_at` on attendees. `description` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`. The cancelled rule is `(status = 'cancelled') IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (cancelled_at IS NOT NULL)`.
- **The 422 body.** `{error: "attendee_not_member", reason: "attendee_not_member", detail: {userId}}`. The error filter forwards only `field`, `reason` and `detail`, so the person is in `detail.userId`, not at the top level.
- **Who counts as an attendee.** A live, `active` membership of the company AND `users.kind = 'employee'` (the `GET /:t/members` list): a bot, an automation account or a client login is refused with the same 422, because they can never answer. On PATCH only the people being ADDED are checked, so someone who has since left does not block an edit that keeps them.
- **Other refusals.** All 400 unless noted, each with a `reason`: `attendees_too_many` (more than 50), `attendees_invalid`, `time_invalid` (an instant needs a UTC offset: a bare local time is refused), `date_invalid`, `time_shape_invalid` (both shapes, half of one, dates without `allDay: true`), `time_range_invalid`, `time_span_too_long`, `title_invalid`, `description_invalid`, `location_invalid`, `video_url_invalid`, `visibility_invalid`, `id_invalid`, `link_invalid` (a client or project that is not a live record of this company), `record_invalid`, `record_needs_timed_event`, `record_not_editable` (PATCH), `nothing_to_change` (PATCH), `response_invalid`, `body_invalid`, and for `mine` `window_required`, `window_invalid`, `window_too_large`, `scope_invalid`. 409: `event_cancelled`, `recording_needs_timed_event` (a PATCH that would make an event with a recording all-day).
- **Answers.** POST create is 201 and PATCH, cancel and respond are 200, all with the detail. The detail adds `tenantId`, `myResponse`, `canCancel`, `cancelledAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`; an attendee name is `""` for a person who no longer resolves. `canEdit`, `canCancel` and `canRespond` are Cerbos's answer for this event and this caller, and are all false on a cancelled event.
- **Order.** Every handler reads the event (organizer, attendees, visibility), asks Cerbos whether the caller may READ it (a refusal is 404, the same body an unknown id gets), then authorizes the action (403), then validates the body (400), then runs one transaction under the row lock. A caller who cannot read an event never learns it exists; a caller who can read it and may not act on it gets 403.
- **Time change.** A time change is a whole time spec (both ends). The same instants written in another offset are not a change. On a change every attendee goes back to `needs_action`, the organizer stays `accepted`, and a linked recording that is still `scheduled` has its `scheduled_at` moved (with a `meeting.recording.updated` event); a recording that has started or finished is left alone. Changing the title, place or description alone moves nothing and tells nobody.
- **Notifications** (through `notify()`, never the actor): `calendar.invited` (on create, and for people added by a PATCH; title "You are invited: <title>", body the time in words), `calendar.removed`, `calendar.changed` (to everyone who stays, on a time change) and `calendar.cancelled`. The time in words is in `DISPLAY_TZ`, else `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISPLAY_TZ`, else `Asia/Singapore`. Answering notifies nobody. Activity rows (`created`, `updated`, `cancelled`, `responded`) carry ids, counts and field NAMES, never the description or the title.
- **Events** emitted in the same transaction: `calendar.event.created`, `.updated`, `.cancelled`, `.responded` (entity `calendar_event`).
- **`record: true`.** The scheduled recording is written by `scheduleRecordingInTx` in `platform-nest/src/core/meeting-schedule.ts`, the same function `POST /:t/meetings/recordings/schedule` now calls (its INSERT, its `meeting.recording.scheduled` event and its activity moved there unchanged). The recording takes the event's title, client and project, kind `audio`, and `scheduledAt` = the event's start; the event row and the recording commit or roll back together. `meetings.test.ts` still covers the route; `meeting-schedule.test.ts` pins the SQL, the parameters and the event.
- **`GET /calendar/events/mine`.** Legs run in parallel, one `withTenants([t])` per company. Each leg first asks Cerbos whether the caller may read an event they are invited to there (that is what every row is); a refusal is `no_access` (a login with no calendar read, such as a module tier alone), any other failure is `error`, never a 500. `from` and `to` take a date alone (that day's UTC midnight) or an instant with an offset; an all-day event is in the window when its days meet the window's UTC days. At most 500 rows per company. `scope` is `all` or a company id (anything else is 400).
- **Manager added to the self rules at review (2026-10-14).** A manager-only login could create an event but not then read its own; `manager` now holds the organizer, attendee and company-visibility read rules, the organizer update and cancel rules and the attendee respond rule (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §39). The DENY for non-attendees on `respond` still holds for every role.
- **Tests.** `calendar-events.service.test.ts` (33 pure cases), `meeting-schedule.test.ts` (6), `src/rbac/cerbos-calendar-event.test.ts` (10 static, 38 live with `CERBOS_URL`), `src/db/calendar-events-migration.db.test.ts` (23, DATABASE_URL_TEST) and `calendar-events.test.ts` (55, the HTTP suite, DATABASE_URL_TEST plus Cerbos).

### 47.8 As built (UI, DW-8g, 2026-10-14)

`platform-ui/src/lib/calendarEvents.ts` (types and pure rules), `calendarEvents-data.ts` (readers), `calendarEventsActions.ts` (writes), `zoneTime.ts` (zone-aware day maths), `demoCalendarEvents.ts` (DEMO_MODE store). Built as §47.5 says, except busy times: **the chosen attendees' busy blocks are not drawn**, because `GET /:t/calendar/busy` (§47.4) is not built (owner ruling pending). `calendar/page.tsx` carries a comment where they would go.

- **Time zone.** Every day boundary is the display zone's (`NEXT_PUBLIC_DISPLAY_TZ`, default `Asia/Singapore`), computed with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and no date library: an instant maps to its day and time in the zone, and a wall time in the zone maps back to a UTC instant (a time skipped by a clock change moves forward, one that happens twice takes the first). The read window is `[start of the grid's first day, start of the day after its last)` in that zone, sent as UTC instants; a month grid is 42 days at most, inside the 92-day cap. A timed event occupies the days from its start to its last instant (one ending exactly at midnight does not spill over); an all-day event its plain dates. `/calendar` "today" is now the display zone's, not UTC's.
- **`/calendar`.** Events join Day, Week and Month; the Timeline stays tasks only. Cancelled events are struck through, declined ones dimmed, both also said in words. The KPI tiles still count tasks only. An unreadable events read keeps the task grid and says so in one line ("couldn't be read"), never "no events"; an excluded company leg gets its own line.
- **`/calendar/new`.** The active company only. People come from `GET /:t/members` (the organizer is always invited and not listed). "Record this meeting" shows only where the `agencyRow: meetings` gate allows, with "Recordings are visible to everyone in the company.", and is disabled for an all-day event. Dates and times are typed in the display zone and sent as UTC instants. On success it goes to the event page.
- **`/calendar/events/[id]`** reads the company from `?company=` (checked against the caller's companies, else the active one). Which buttons show is only `canEdit` / `canCancel` / `canRespond` from the detail (none on a cancelled event). Cancel asks first. Edit is `/calendar/events/[id]/edit`, the schedule form with the event's values and no "Record" choice. A 404 reads "This event doesn't exist or isn't visible to you."
- **Refusals in words.** 400 by `reason`, 403 (worded per create, change or answer), 404, 409 (`event_cancelled`, `recording_needs_timed_event`), and 422 `attendee_not_member`, which names the person: the id is in `detail.userId` (see §47.7) and the name comes from the members list the page already holds.
- **Overview Today block.** Lists today's events for the Overview's company (time, title, link; cancelled and declined ones stay, marked). An unreadable read says "Events are unavailable". The note "No calendar events exist yet (DW-8g)" is gone.
- **Areas.** `/calendar/new` and `/calendar/events` (subtree) are personal, like `/calendar`.

## 48. Email from the ERP through your own Gmail: read, reply, send, "Email this client" (DW-8j, DW-D24, 2026-10-14) — `platform-nest/src/core/gmail/` (new), `src/integrations/gmail/` (the MAIL-16D seam, extended); UI `/me/mail` — **STATUS: PLANNED**

**Why.**
- Plan §8.1 (row 8j) and §14.2 ("Send an email from the ERP").
- Ruling DW-D24 (owner, 2026-10-14): each employee reads, replies and sends through their OWN Gmail inside the ERP, including "Email this client". It is built now against a simulated Gmail and goes live when the Google OAuth client exists (DW-11).
- This extends the mail design's read-only Gmail scope (§8C, A14), whose constraints still hold:
  - an Internal-type OAuth app;
  - a per-person link;
  - no domain-wide delegation;
  - render on demand, store nothing.
- System mail is unchanged: approvals and risk only. Gmail is never a notification channel.

**What already exists (reused, not rebuilt):**
- **The `GmailClient` seam** (`src/integrations/gmail/`, MAIL-16D): `listThreads`, `getThread`, `getMessage`, `listLabels`, a fixture implementation and a provider-agnostic contract suite.
- **The shared Google OAuth state machine** (`src/core/google-oauth/`): the surface registry, signed single-use state and the token endpoint.
- **DW-6i's Google Drive connection** (`src/core/google-drive/`, §42), the template for every connection route below. Tokens are sealed in `integration_connections` (`owner_kind='user'`, the person).

### 48.1 Two modes, one switch
`GMAIL_MODE` is `simulated` (the default) or `live`.

**Simulated** is the dev and review stage:
- "Connect" links a simulated mailbox with no Google round trip. The fixture threads come from MAIL-16D's fixtures, so the mailbox has content.
- Sent messages land in that mailbox's Sent, held in process memory only: they are lost on restart, nothing is written to the database, and nothing leaves the box.
- Every page and every answer carries `mode: "simulated"`. The UI labels the mailbox "Simulated mailbox: nothing is really sent".

**Live** uses the real Gmail API with the person's own token:
- Scopes are `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly` and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`.
- Live mode refuses to start unless the Google client env is set. It must pass MAIL-16D's contract suite unmodified for reads, and §48.6's send contract.
- Live is the staging step of DW-11. It is not run in this ticket.

### 48.2 The connection (copy §42's shape, provider `google_gmail`)
- **Provider.** `google_gmail` joins `GOOGLE_PROVIDERS` and the `integration_connections` provider CHECK, through a migration that re-declares the whole CHECK from main's current list (a DROP+ADD re-declares everything).
- **Surface.** It is registered like Drive: `ownerKind: "user"`, `module: null`, `authz: {kind: "personal_mailbox", action: "connect"}`.
- **Routes:**
  - `GET /api/:t/integrations/gmail`: the token-free status `{configured, connected, needsReconnect, accountEmail, mode}`. It never calls Google.
  - `GET /api/:t/integrations/gmail/oauth/start` → `{authUrl}`. Simulated mode answers `{linked: true}` and creates the simulated link at once.
  - `GET /api/gmail/oauth/callback`: tenant-agnostic. The tenant and the person come only from the verified state.
  - `DELETE /api/:t/integrations/gmail`: revoke at Google (best effort), then clear the sealed tokens.
- **Failures.** A refused refresh marks "needs reconnect" and keeps the tokens. An outage is 502 `gmail_unavailable` and marks nothing.

### 48.3 Reading your own mail (render on demand, cache nothing)
**Routes.** The owner is always the caller, never a parameter:
- `GET /api/:t/mail/me/threads?label=INBOX|SENT&pageToken=` → `{mode, threads: [{id, snippet, subject, from, lastMessageDate, unread}], nextPageToken}`.
- `GET /api/:t/mail/me/threads/:threadId` → the thread, with every message decoded through `getMessage`: headers, the text part, the sanitized HTML part, and attachment metadata only.

**Rules:**
- **Nothing is stored.** No message content is written to the database, a log or the activity feed. The thread list is not cached between requests.
- **HTML.** HTML bodies are sanitized with the mail module's `sanitize.ts`, and the UI shows them in a `sandbox=""` iframe, as `/admin/mail` previews do.
- **Not connected** → 409 `gmail_not_connected`; the UI offers Connect.
- **Gate.** `personal_mailbox` · `read` on `{ownerId: caller}` (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §40).

### 48.4 Sending, replying and "Email this client"
**The request:** `POST /api/:t/mail/me/send` with:
- `to: string[]`, `cc?: string[]` (at most 20 addresses in all, each a valid address);
- `subject` (1 to 300 characters);
- `body` (plain text, 1 to 50,000 characters);
- `inReplyTo?: {threadId, messageId}`, which keeps the thread and sets `In-Reply-To` and `References`;
- `context?: {kind: "client", id}`.

**The answer:** 202 `{mode, messageId, threadId}`.

**Gates:**
- `personal_mailbox` · `send` on `{ownerId: caller}`.
- With a `context`: the client's read too (the same shape `/clients/:id` sends). A caller who cannot read the client cannot send "about" it.

**What v1 leaves out:**
- attachments (a later ticket may attach ERP files by id);
- HTML compose;
- scheduled send.

**What is recorded:**
- One activity row, `emailed` on the client when there is a `context`, else on nobody. It records who sent, when, how many recipients and `mode`, but never the subject, the body or the addresses (DW-D24: nothing stored).
- No notification.

**Rate limit:** 30 sends per person per hour (429 `gmail_send_rate_limited`, with `retryAfterSeconds`). It is a guard against a runaway client or script, not a quota.

**Errors:** 409 `gmail_not_connected`, 502 `gmail_unavailable`, 400 `gmail_send_invalid` (with `field`), and 403.

**"Email this client"** (staff client page):
- The button opens compose prefilled with the client's primary contact address or addresses and `context: {kind: "client", id}`.
- When the client has no contact address, the button says "This client has no contact email" and is disabled.

### 48.5 UI
**The registry.** You › Inbox becomes a two-tab row (`YOU_ROWS`): Notifications (`/me/inbox`, as today) and Mail (`/me/mail`). The bell still opens Notifications.

**`/me/mail`:**
- With no connection: one sentence and the Connect button, plus the simulated label in simulated mode.
- Connected: the thread list (Inbox and Sent), then the thread, then Reply. Compose is at `/me/mail/new?to=&client=`.
- Honest states:
  - not connected;
  - needs reconnect;
  - unavailable ("Gmail can't be reached right now."), never an empty mailbox;
  - rate limited (with the wait).

**The staff client page:** "Email this client" sits on the client overview's contact area. PV-3 owns that page and reviews the placement before it lands.

**DEMO_MODE:** answers in simulated mode with fixture threads.

### 48.6 Tests
- **The seam:** `sendMessage` joins the `GmailClient` interface with its own contract cases:
  - the threading headers on a reply;
  - recipients validated;
  - a revoked token gives `GmailRevokedError`;
  - a 429 gives `GmailRateLimitedError`.
- **The fixture/simulated client** passes MAIL-16D's existing suite unmodified, plus the send cases.
- **HTTP suite** on the Linux CI gate:
  - connect, status and disconnect in simulated mode;
  - reading another person's mailbox is impossible: there is no parameter for it, and a forged connection row of another owner is never read;
  - send without a connection gives 409;
  - send with a client context the caller cannot read gives 403;
  - the activity row carries no subject, body or address;
  - the 31st send in an hour gives 429;
  - an automation or bot principal is refused `send`;
  - the provider CHECK accepts `google_gmail` and still refuses an unknown provider.
- **Cerbos matrix:** `src/rbac/cerbos-personal-mailbox.test.ts`.
- **UI:** the mailbox states, compose validation, the reply prefill, the "Email this client" prefill and its no-address state, and the simulated label.

## 53. The client grain in reports (PV7-01, 2026-10-15) — `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/` — **STATUS: BUILT, PROTOTYPED (backend: the DB and HTTP suite report-client-grain.db.test.ts and the Cerbos matrix reports-cerbos.test.ts are written for the Linux CI gate; no page yet, PV7-05)**

**Why.**
- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-15-pv7-performance-views-tickets.md`, PV7-01 and findings 1 to 3. The Reports pages and the client Health board (PV7-05) need one document per client, summed across that client's projects.
- It is a **staff-only** document (lead's call L1, PV7-Q1). It carries task- and time-derived numbers, so it is never shown to a client. What a client sees is built from records the client can already see (PV7-02, PV7-04, PV7-07), never from this document.
- It is **sealed with each month like every other grain** (L2), so a project moved to another client does not rewrite history.

### 53.1 The grain
- `client` joins `person | project | department | company` wherever the grain is named: the document, overview, metrics and export routes, the sealed store, the MCP enums and the UI type mirror.
- **`scopeRef`** is the client id. A value that is not a uuid is 400 `scopeRef` (never a 500 at the uuid cast).
- **The `header`** is the usual one: `grain: "client"`, `scopeRef` the client id, `scopeName` the client's name (the id when the client no longer exists).
- **KPI set:** the project grain's metrics, in the same order. `evidence.source_diversity` has no project grain, so it is not offered here either.

### 53.2 What is in a client's numbers
A client's figures are the sum of its projects' figures. The sources are the same rows the project grain reads, regrouped through `projects.client_id`:
- **Fact-backed metrics:** `report_work_facts` joined to `projects` (same tenant) and `clients`.
- **Milestones, flow and overdue:** regrouped through a project to client map, the way flow already maps a project to its department.

**Excluded, both shapes of "internal":**
- a project with `is_internal` (internal work);
- a project whose client is the sentinel internal client (`clients.is_internal`);
- a soft-deleted project or client.

These are the same two shapes the department KPI readers exclude (`dept-kpi-readers/scope.ts`).

### 53.3 The arithmetic (what the tests pin)
- **Additive metrics:** the sum of the projects' values.
- **Ratios:** sum of numerators over sum of denominators across the client's projects. **Never a mean of the projects' ratios.**
- **`flow.wip_open_avg`:** the numerator is the sum of open counts and the **denominator stays the range's day count**. Summing per-project day counts would multiply the days.
- **`discipline.overdue_open`:** a count at the range end. It keeps `pointInTime` and is summed across projects, never across days.

### 53.4 Moved projects
`projects.client_id` can change.
- **A live range** (any open period, a custom range, today) uses the project's **current** client.
- **A sealed period** serves the stored document, so it keeps the attribution of the day it was sealed. Amending and re-sealing re-attributes at that moment, as for every grain.

### 53.5 Routes
All of these are existing routes; only the accepted `grain` value is new.
- `GET /api/:t/reports/document?grain=client&scopeRef=<clientId>&periodKind&start&end[&revision]` returns the usual `ReportDocument`. A sealed calendar period serves the stored client document at the latest revision, else it falls back to a live build.
- `GET /api/:t/reports/overview?grain=client&periodKind&start&end` returns `{periodKind, start, end, scopes: [{scopeRef, scopeName, kpis}]}`: one headline row per client that has any rollup row in the range (the same three headline KPIs as the project overview, no deltas), for the board. A client with no work in the range is not listed.
- `POST /api/:t/reports/export {grain: "client", scopeRef, periodKind, start, end, format}` exports through the same fetch and the same check as the read, so an export never widens access.
- `GET /api/:t/reports/metrics?grain=client` returns the raw rows whose dimensions are `{clientId}`.
- `servedTenant` stays valid for `department` only (400 otherwise). `unit` stays valid for `person` only.

### 53.6 Narrative
A client document's narrative is the **deterministic** one, in a live read and in a sealed one. The seal makes no AI call per client (one call per client would add about 71 calls to every monthly seal). `narrative.source` is `"deterministic"`, and so is `report_documents.narrative_source`.

### 53.7 Access
- **Cerbos:** `report_document` · `read_client` (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §45). The routes above call it for every `grain=client` read, listing and export.
- **Who:** the derived roles that hold `read_project`, without the served-provider arm. A served company's staff read their own department's slice only.
- **Nobody gains reach:** anyone who can read every project document could already compute the sum.

### 53.8 MCP
`reports.getDocument` and `reports.getMetrics` accept `grain: "client"`. Their text says the client document is staff-only.

### 53.9 Migration
`202610151700_reports_client_grain.sql`:
- widens the `report_documents.grain` CHECK to the five grains (found by its column set, never by text);
- seeds the `reports.document.read_client` permission and its role grants (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §45).

### 53.10 Not here
- Any page (PV7-05 builds Reports > Client and the Health board on this).
- Client health states (PV7-02, §54).
- Anything a client can see (PV7-04, PV7-07).

**As built (2026-10-15).**
- **`flow.avg_progress`** is the one project metric with no department or company rollup. It is emitted at client grain too, as Sum(progress x open) / Sum(open) over the client's projects (the 16th metric).
- **The Projects table** (`client_projects`: project, throughput, tasks completed, with a total row) lists which of the client's eligible projects carried the work. It is built from the same facts and the same eligible set as the KPIs.
- **The print route** (`/print/reports/:jobToken`, the PDF export) renders a client document with the project grain's charts until PV7-05 builds the real page.
- **Demo mode** serves two demo clients (`c-acme`, `c-sunrise`) from `lib/demoReports.ts`.
- **The IAM artifacts** a new action on an existing kind needs are in the same change: the catalog key, the `team_project_reports` group, the regenerated bundles and the seed in the migration (PERMISSION-CONTRACT §45).

**Proof.**
- `platform-nest/src/modules/reports/report-client-grain.db.test.ts` (DB and HTTP, on the CI gate): the golden table (two clients, six projects of four kinds), Sum/Sum ratios that differ from the mean of ratios, `wip_open_avg` on the day count, overdue summed point-in-time, internal work absent in all four shapes, the document, overview, metrics and export routes, the access check, and the moved project (sealed keeps the old client, live shows the new one, no AI call for a client document).
- Pure: `metrics.test.ts`, `document-builder.test.ts`, `report-seal.test.ts` (run anywhere).
- UI demo: `platform-ui/src/lib/demoReports.test.ts`.
